stories.title: 25,000 UP instructors to receive 9 years' pending arrears:Supreme Court dismisses state government's review plea
stories.summary: Around 25,000 instructors in Uttar Pradesh have received major relief from the Supreme Court. The court has ordered that instructors be paid a monthly honorarium of ₹17,000 along with arrears pending since 2017. On Thursday, the court upheld its February 4, 2026 judgment and dismissed the Uttar Pradesh government's review petition. Following the Supreme Court's order, the state government will now have to proceed with the payment of the revised honorarium and pending arrears. A bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Prasanna B. Varale said there was no apparent legal error in the February 4, 2026 judgment that warranted a review. Demand for hearing in open court also rejected The Supreme Court also rejected the state government's application seeking an open court hearing of the matter. With this, all pending applications related to the case were also disposed of. Instructors will receive arrears from 2017 In its February 4, 2026 judgment, the Supreme Court had directed the state government to pay instructors a monthly honorarium of ₹17,000. It also ordered that arrears pending since 2017 be paid within the stipulated time frame. Around 25,000 instructors are currently working under Uttar Pradesh's Basic Education Department. Counsel for the instructors, Durga Tiwari, said that following the Supreme Court's latest order, the government must now begin the process of paying arrears in line with the original judgment.

stories.summary: BJP MLA Brijbhushan Rajput, who held Minister Swatantra hostage, was seen in a new avatar on Thursday. He inaugurated a direct roadways bus service from Charkhari in Mahoba to Ayodhya Dham. Then he himself drove the bus for about 800 meters. During this, Charkhari MLA Brijbhushan Rajput stuck his hand out of the bus window and called out for passengers by shouting "Ayodhya... Ayodhya...". He said - Look, is there any passenger for Ayodhya? At this, the passengers sitting in the bus welcomed the MLA by clapping. A video of this entire incident has also surfaced. Before this, a 12-year-old student showed the green flag to the bus. Now the complete matter in detail The distance from Charkhari town to Ayodhya Dham is 372 kilometers. It takes approximately 7.5 hours to reach Ayodhya from here by car or bus. Since the construction of the Ram Temple, a large number of people from here go to Ayodhya for darshan. That's why Charkhari MLA Brijbhushan Rajput had been demanding the start of a direct bus service to Ayodhya for quite some time. His demand was fulfilled on Thursday. Brijbhushan Rajput says I can drive a bus, handcart, everything In the video, while driving the bus, the MLA is saying- I am not just any ordinary MLA, I can drive a bus, handcart, everything. To this, a passenger present in the bus said that you are driving the bus very well. ARM was also present in the bus. The MLA told him- Get its horns fixed properly. There should be no deficiency in any vehicle running on the road. The MLA said- The safety and facilities of the bus in which people from our area will travel must be better; that is most important. I drove a bus for the first time in my life, but I felt it necessary to check the arrangements myself for the safety of passengers. Says direct facility to Ramlala is a gift for the area While addressing the program held at the bus inauguration, MLA Brijbhushan Rajput said, “Ayodhya is the centre of faith for crores of people. It is a great achievement for devotees of Charkhari to get direct facility to reach Ramlala's court. Calling passengers for the bus going to Lord Ram's abode was a fortunate moment of my life.” The MLA expressed gratitude to UP's Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh for this bus service. He said, “This is not just a transport service, but an initiative to fulfil the religious sentiments and needs of the area residents that are several years old. This bus service will increase the number of devotees going to Ayodhya. The Bundelkhand region will also get a new identity from religious tourism.” Says we love Ram Lalla from our hearts MLA Brajbhushan Rajput said, “Lord Ram is the centre of faith for all of us. We have a lot of devotion towards the Lord. We love Lord Ram very much from our hearts. In such a situation, calling passengers for the bus going to Lord Ram's abode becomes a fortunate matter in itself. If we can be of any service to God, we consider ourselves very fortunate.” Who is Brijbhushan Rajput? BJP MLA from Charkhari (Mahoba) Brijbhushan Rajput was born on 28 May 1982 in Orai (Jalaun). His father Ganga Charan Rajput has been a Lok Sabha MP 3 times (1989, 1996, 1998) and a Rajya Sabha MP (2009). Brijbhushan Rajput married Kanak Lodhi on May 9, 2005. He has two sons. Brijbhushan Rajput inherited political confrontation. His father Ganga Charan Rajput was known for controversies and defections in UP politics. Ganga Charan Rajput has been in Janata Dal, BJP, Congress and BSP. He led several movements on electricity-water and OBC issues in Bundelkhand. On May 18, 2004, after UPA's victory, when there was talk of Sonia Gandhi becoming Prime Minister and she declined the post, a high-voltage drama took place outside the Congress office in Delhi. Ganga Charan Rajput climbed on the roof of a car, brandished a pistol and threatened while pointing it at his own temple that if Sonia Gandhi did not become PM, he would shoot himself.

stories.title: UP reel-making groom’s ‘three brides’ wedding sparks legal trouble:One bride found minor; 'All 4 of us will end our lives'
stories.summary: Three reel-making sisters who married a cameraman in Amroha are in the headlines. Hindu organisations are opposing this marriage. The police have also become active. On Thursday morning at 10 am, all four were called to the police station. Three hours later at 1 pm, the three brides arrived at the police station with their husband, where everyone appeared quite happy. The three brides told the police, “We did not marry under any pressure. All three of us are adults. We used to think that if we marry, we would marry into the same house, but we couldn't find such a house where there would be three boys of our age. That's why we married one boy. We will die but will not separate.” On the question of registering the marriage, they said, “Some marriages don't work even after registration. We are happy as we are, if someone asks us for proof then we will see.” The three sisters had married their cameraman on July 17 at Chamunda Mata Temple. The wedding video surfaced on Wednesday. 'Dainik Bhaskar' spoke with the three brides. Read the report… Havan-worship in temple, took seven rounds Alka (20 years), Devika (19 years) and Santosh (18 years) are sisters living in Dhauria village in Hasanpur Kotwali area. All three create video content on Instagram and Facebook. Alka and Santosh are real sisters, while Devika is their maternal aunt's daughter. Devika has been raised with Alka and Santosh since childhood. Vikas alias Vikku, a resident of Shyampuri village, is the cameraman for all three sisters. He had been working for the three girls for the past 6 months. He also played the role of husband in reels. All three sisters say that they always wanted to live together, but the family members were not agreeable. On July 17, all three married Vikas in a temple. Family members did not attend the wedding At the temple, the cameraman filled the vermilion in the parting of all three brides one by one, and the brides touched their husband's feet to seek his blessings. However, no one from either family attended the wedding. This wedding came to light when the video surfaced on Wednesday evening at 5 PM. The three sisters have defended themselves by releasing a video. They said, “In ancient times, there was King Dashrath who had three queens. So what wrong have we done?” Now read the conversation Dainik Bhaskar first spoke with the eldest sister Alka- Question: Are all three of you real sisters? Alka: Yes, one is a cousin sister, but we have grown up together since childhood, so we consider her as our own. Question: How did all three of you meet Vikas? Alka: We used to make videos on YouTube, so we needed characters. That's how we met him. Question: Is this marriage fake, done to increase followers? Alka: No, we have gotten married. All three of us don't want to live separately. Question: Have you registered the marriage? Alka: Some marriages don't work even after registration. We are married, we are happy. Otherwise, if someone asks us for proof of this thing, we will give it. Question: Can all three live with one husband? Have you made any plan? Alka: Our plan was already made beforehand. We had been thinking from before that if we get married, we would either do it in one house, but we didn't find such a house. That's why we did it with one boy. We will die, but we won't separate; we have been saying this from before. Everything happened with our consent and all four of us are very happy. Devika said- People talk, we cannot stop them The second sister Devika said - We three sisters are together. We are feeling very good. After marriage, there has been no problem between the four of us. Some people are opposing, many people are also supporting. Many people are speaking well, but some people are speaking badly. It's people's job to speak. We cannot stop them. Santosh said - We three were saved from death The third sister Santosh says that if we had separated, we might have died. We survived death and are together, and now we will always remain together. The family members wanted to get us married separately. We had told Vikas about this. He agreed to marry all three of us. Got married against parents' wishes All three sisters said - We got married against our parents' wishes, but now they have also agreed. Some Hindu organizations are raising questions. So how is our marriage against Sanatan? King Dashrath was also a Hindu. He also had three marriages. How can we be wrong? If we are criminals, then he was also wrong. Vikas has been living at his in-laws' place since the wedding It should be noted that Alka is a B.Tech second year student, while Devika and Santosh have passed 12th grade. Father Ramesh is a farmer. Vikas passed 12th grade this year. He now wants to pursue LLB. He is the youngest among three brothers. After the wedding, these four people are living at a relative's house. See 2 pictures after the wedding Household expenses will be managed through social media income After the wedding, on the question of expenses, all three brides said - We earn income from social media. We will work even harder in the future. There is also some land in our husband's name, which will cover the expenses. Police said - Action will be taken after checking documents Hasanpur police station in-charge Rajesh Tiwari said that three young women have married one young man. All three young women and the young man have been called to the police station. They are being interrogated. After examining the statements and age-related documents, further action will be taken in the matter.

stories.title: Varanasi woman dies by suicide after mother stops mobile use:Police bring down body from noose; forensic team arrives
stories.summary: In Varanasi, when her mother forbade her from using her mobile phone, the daughter locked herself in her room. Family members kept knocking on the door from outside, but the young woman did not open it. On Thursday at 12 noon, angry with her mother, the young woman hanged herself. Family members informed the police, after which the door was broken down. Inside, the young woman's body was found hanging from a hook. She was then taken down from the noose. The police called the forensic team. They took possession of the body, completed the inquest, and sent it for post-mortem. Now read the full story Hanuman Chaurasia lives with his family on rent in a house in Lallapura, under the Sigra police station area. His wife, son, and daughter Pooja Chaurasia (19) also live with them. One son and daughter are already married and live separately with their families. The whole family was troubled by the habit of using the phone Hanuman Chaurasia was busy preparing for his daughter Pooja's wedding, but the whole family was troubled by Pooja's habit of using her phone. In recent days, there were several arguments at home over talking on the phone all night, but Pooja was not ready to listen. Kept using the phone all night On Wednesday night, Pooja took her phone and went out of the room and kept using the phone all night. When her mother reprimanded her, she got angry, saying she was watching reels on social media. After this, when her mother expressed displeasure in the morning, an argument broke out between them. After this, Pooja went inside the house and locked herself in the room. Then, she placed a cylinder on the cot, made a noose with a dupatta in the fan hook, and hanged herself. Her mother kept screaming and shouting from the window, but Pooja did not listen at all. Police broke down the door and removed the body In a hurry, neighbours were called to try and break down the door, but the latch did not break. After this, Sigra police were called, and the door was broken. After this, ACP Chetganj Shubham Singh also reached the spot and gathered information. Family members said that the deceased Pooja was forbidden by her mother Savitri Chaurasia, from using her mobile phone late at night. She was one of two brothers and two sisters; one brother and one sister were already married. She was the third child and had studied up to class 5, after which she left school.

stories.title: Executive engineer slapped in Gorakhpur:Black helmet-clad attackers storm office and assault him
stories.summary: A case of assault and life-threatening attack on an Executive Engineer has come to light in the flood division office of Gorakhpur. The commotion continued in the office for about 20 minutes. The entire incident has been captured on the CCTV camera installed there. In it, the Executive Engineer is seen being slapped by a youth wearing a black helmet along with other people. The incident occurred on Thursday afternoon around 1 PM. Cantt police, who arrived upon receiving information, are investigating the matter. The Executive Engineer has accused a clerk from his own office of the assault. Executive Engineer Vipin Singh had gone to inspect the Flood Division office located in Padleganj, in the Cantt police station area, along with Chief Engineer Vikas Singh. It is alleged that during this time, the accused clerk came with his companions and started abusing. Upon protesting, the Executive Engineer was attacked. During this, there was an atmosphere of chaos in the office. Employees working in the office came screaming to intervene. Right in front of them, a youth wearing a black helmet slapped the Executive Engineer several times. After the incident, the accused left, threatening to kill him. The Executive Engineer alleges that the clerk is suspended in a case. Police from Cantt police station reached the spot and started an investigation. The accused who attacked are also being identified from the office's CCTV cameras, who had come with the clerk.

stories.title: 1.86 lakh UP teachers must take TET:Centre rejects state's demand; Jayant Chaudhary says no relaxation possible
stories.summary: Around 1.86 lakh teachers in Uttar Pradesh have received a major setback from the central government. Union Minister of State for Education Jayant Chaudhary has refused to grant exemption from the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET). In response to a question asked in the Lok Sabha, he said, “The matter of passing TET is linked to a Supreme Court order, therefore no relaxation is possible at present. Old teachers will also not get any kind of relief.” The decision was announced after Congress MP from Karnataka E. Tukaram had asked a question on whether an amendment to Section 23 of the Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009 is being considered to provide relief to teachers appointed before TET was implemented. The Union Minister said, “The government is not bringing any such proposal at present, nor is any interim relief being considered.” Meanwhile, the UP government is going to conduct a special TET for teachers of the Basic Education Department soon. The government has asked the Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission, Prayagraj, to immediately provide a detailed action plan for the examination. Special Secretary Awadhesh Kumar Tiwari issued a letter in this regard on 21 July. The Selection Commission has been asked to soon provide the complete action plan for conducting special TET for both categories. Central minister says teacher recruitment is a matter of the state government Union Minister Jayant Chaudhary said, “Recruitment and service conditions of teachers are state subjects; therefore, data of such teachers is with state governments. The Supreme Court, in its judgment dated September 1, 2025, clarified that TET is the minimum qualification prescribed under Section 23 of the RTE Act 2009. TET is mandatory to become a teacher in schools covered under RTE.” While hearing review petitions filed thereafter, the Supreme Court on May 29, 2026 gave relief by extending the final date for passing TET from August 31, 2027 to August 31, 2028. This means teachers have got an additional one year. States ordered to conduct TET twice a year The Supreme Court also stated in its order that state governments and concerned authorities should attempt to conduct TET at least twice every year. There should be a gap of approximately 6 months between both examinations. This will provide teachers with adequate opportunity to fulfil the qualification. This means that now there is increased pressure on all states, including UP to conduct TET regularly. In UP, the TET examination was held in July. In this regard, the TET examination should now be conducted again in January 2027. 1.86 lakh teachers in UP fall under this order According to the UP Basic Education Department, there are approximately 1.86 lakh teachers who have not yet passed TET. A large number of these are teachers who were appointed before the TET system was implemented. This includes assistant teachers, teachers adjusted from Shiksha Mitras, teachers with old training, and teachers working in remote areas for a long time. These teachers argue that the RTE Act was passed in 2009 and implemented in UP in 2011. In such a case, how can this be applied to the recruitment of teachers who were already working before this. Why was there hope for relief? Teacher organisations had demanded that the RTE Act be amended to provide exemption to old teachers. Their argument was that experience should be considered as eligibility. They were talking about providing relief at least to teachers who had reached close to retirement. However, the central government has made it clear in Parliament, citing the Supreme Court's order, that it is not ready for any kind of amendments to the RTE. What Next? The UP government will have to conduct regular TET examinations as per the Supreme Court's directives. Teachers will have to be allowed to apply. Arrangements will have to be made to complete the qualification by August 31, 2028. Failing to do so, the services of such people will be considered terminated after the stipulated time period. Those who do not pass TET will also not get the benefit of promotion.

stories.title: Fake international call centre busted in Lucknow:Four, including uncle-nephew duo, arrested for targeting US citizens
stories.summary: Police in Lucknow's Vibhuti Khand area busted a fake call centre which targeted American citizens by posing as Apple customer support officials. Police have arrested four operators of the call centre. The role of 35 calling agents found at the scene is being investigated. During the operation, a large number of laptops, mobiles and other electronic devices were seized. DCP East Dr Diksha Sharma held a press conference on Thursday and informed that on the night of 22 July, Vibhuti Khand police station in-charge Upendra Singh was conducting vehicle checking in front of Jalwa Bar. During this time, an informer provided information about a fake call centre operating in flat number 420A on the fourth floor of Cyber Height building. After this, a raid was conducted at around 2.55 AM along with the crime team and the call centre was busted. Mastermind was running gang with relatives Police arrested Suraj Tripathi, a resident of Pratapgarh, his relatives Vivek Pandey and Rahul Tripathi, and Mumbai resident technical expert Akash Arun Datta alias Ricky from the spot. Investigation revealed that Suraj is the mastermind of the entire gang, while Akash operated the fake website and VOIP system. This is how they used to defraud people in America Investigation revealed that the gang promoted a fake Apple customer support website through s on Google. When calls came from America to the number given on the website, the calls reached the call centre located in Lucknow through voice over internet protocol (VOIP). Here, agents would identify themselves as customer support officers. After this, the call closers would extort money in the form of gift cards, gold, or cash by intimidating or luring victims by posing as officials from government departments like the FTC or the US Supreme Court. Money reached through hawala According to the police, gang members present in America would collect the extorted money. After this, the money was sent to Lucknow through hawala. Employees were also paid in cash, so that there would be no digital record of the transactions. During the raid, 35 workstations were found running in the call centre. Thirty-five calling agents were working here. Among them, the highest number of 10 agents were from Uttarakhand, 9 from Maharashtra, 3 each from Gujarat and Nagaland, two each from Assam and Manipur. Apart from this, agents from West Bengal, Telangana, Tripura, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Nepal were also working. Police are interrogating all of them and investigating their roles. Investigation of Calling Agents' Roles 35 calling agents were also found at the location. The police are interrogating them. The police are trying to find out from the arrested agents whether they were aware of the fraud or were employed and made to work as employees. Information including their bank accounts is being collected. Maternal uncle and nephew were running the fraud call centre Among the arrested accused, three are relatives. Rahul Tripathi is Suraj Tripathi's maternal uncle, while Vivek Pandey is the son of main accused Suraj Tripathi's paternal aunt. Suraj is a graduate, while Vivek Pandey has done a diploma. Rahul Tripathi has passed 12th grade and the fourth accused, Akash Arun Datta looked after field operations. All the fraudsters were committing fraud worth $4.000-$5,000 daily.

stories.title: Environment in UP resembles that of Ravan raj, says Avimukteshwaranand:Sends legal notice to Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Trust
stories.summary: Shankaracharya of Jyotirmath, Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati, on Thursday said there is Ravan Raj in Uttar Pradesh. Speaking in Lucknow, he said that during the 81-day Gavishti (Gau Raksha Dharmayuddha) yatra, he and his supporters were harassed at several places. The proposed Gau Garjan Akshauhini Sankalp programme in Lucknow has now been decided to be organised through a digital medium (virtual) due to administrative circumstances. The Shankaracharya claimed that at many places during the yatra, he was not given permission for night rest. “We had to spend the night on the road,” he said. 'Workers are being placed under house arrest' He alleged that many workers coming to the 24 July event have been stopped at their homes. Some people are being threatened with bulldozers being run on their houses and electricity is being cut off in many places. “What is the reason for this, when we have received permission for the event,” Shankaracharya said, adding that the situation visible in Uttar Pradesh suggests that Ravan Raj has arrived here. 'Now Gau Sankalp will be digital from 12 to 2 pm' He said that initially a public event of Gau Garjan Akshauhini Sankalp was to be held at 12 noon on 24 July at Kanshi Ram Smriti Upvan located in Ashiana, but now it will be organised through a digital medium instead of physical presence. Between 12 noon and 2 pm, a pledge for the protection of Gau Mata and an announcement of future strategy will be made. The journey started from Gorakhpur Avimukteshwaranand said that the journey, which started from Gorakhpur on May 3, passed through all 403 assembly constituencies of Uttar Pradesh. The purpose of the journey was to create public awareness for the protection of Gau Mata. During the journey, he engaged with people in all 403 assembly constituencies of the state. During the journey, he received support from people across the state.

stories.title: Italian national thrashed in Varanasi:After days of creating a ruckus, police admit him to mental hospital; embassy informed
stories.summary: When a video of a foreign national being severely beaten with a stick went viral on social media in Varanasi, the police went into action mode. The police took the foreign national into custody on Wednesday afternoon and admitted him to the District Mental Hospital after a medical examination at Kabirchaura. Doctors there have indicated the possibility of fractures in his hands and feet. Currently, his X-ray will be done after his appearance in court. The foreign national has been identified as Fabio from Italy. Before this, on 16 July, Fabio was admitted to Kabirchaura Hospital after entering people's houses in Saptasagar Mandi, Varanasi. Doctors there had stated that he was intoxicated. On that day, ACP Kotwali Vijay Pratap Singh had stated that Fabio would be handed over to the concerned agencies. But on Tuesday, Fabio suddenly appeared in the Harhua area, where people mistook him for a child thief and chased him. Someone informed the police, and the police took him into custody. The same night, in the Mukimganj area, people severely beat Fabio with sticks. The video of which went viral, and he has now been admitted to a mental hospital. See three pictures Dr Arvind Singh of the Mental Hospital said, “The foreign national is currently being treated in the emergency family ward. The police have not yet been able to present him before the CJM. Therefore, he has currently been admitted to the emergency ward. After being presented before the CJM, we will first admit him to Deen Dayal District Hospital because a fracture is suspected. So, an X-ray will be done there first, and if there's an injury, it will be treated.” The doctor said that Fabio has a psychiatric problem. “An injection was given last night. He has been fine since then. Further treatment will begin after his court appearance,” the doctor said. Embassy Informed ACP Kotwali Vijay Pratap Singh said, “A foreign national has been causing trouble in various police station areas of Banaras for several days. Several videos of disputes with people have also surfaced. In such a situation, the said foreign national has been taken into custody and admitted to the mental hospital. Additionally, the embassy has been contacted to send him back to his country.” The matter in detail In Varanasi, on Thursday, July 16, at 10 AM, a foreign youth created a ruckus in the Saptasagar medicine market area. He ran into a house and started bothering the people present there. Despite much persuasion, he did not calm down. During this, the foreigner bit a young man's hand with his teeth. The foreign youth also misbehaved with the police who arrived after being informed about the commotion. He started shouting 'Go Away' at the policemen. After this, the residents of the neighbourhood collectively beat up the youth. The police caught the foreign youth and admitted him to Kabirchaura Divisional Hospital. Here, his hands had to be tied. Harhua Police showed negligence On Tuesday, Fabio, a resident of Italy, was seen in the Harhua area. In Harhua, people surrounded him, mistaking him for a child kidnapper. Later, the police, who arrived on information, took him to the outpost. Local people allege that he was sent to another location again without any concrete action being taken. In fact, on Tuesday afternoon, the foreign tourist reached Harhua in the Baragaon police station area. During this, he picked up food and drink items from some shops and stalls. When asked not to, he got into an argument with the shopkeepers. Upon reaching near Harhua pond, people suspected him of being a child kidnapper, after which a crowd gathered at the spot. Meanwhile, some people present there immediately informed the police. Subsequently, the foreigner was taken to Harhua police outpost. At the outpost, he told the police that his belongings had been stolen and because of this, he was unable to return to his country. But a few hours later, the police sent him off alone in an auto towards the city.

stories.title: CM inaugurates Gorakhpur's first six-lane flyover:Supporters raise 'Jai Shri Ram' slogans; development projects worth ₹995 crore also announced
stories.summary: Vehicle operations have commenced on Gorakhpur's first six-lane flyover. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath inaugurated it, at 11 AM on Thursday. After the inauguration, the CM walked some distance on the flyover. After this, he posed for a picture standing near the foundation stone. The 2.6 km long six-lane flyover built on the TPNagar-Padleganj route is considered a major achievement for Gorakhpur in terms of inter-district connectivity. A total of ₹429.49 crore have been spent on both sides of the flyover. This will provide significant convenience to vehicles travelling to and from Lucknow, Varanasi, Prayagraj, Azamgarh, Kushinagar, Deoria, Maharajganj, Bihar, and Nepal. Along with the inauguration of the flyover, the Chief Minister also inaugurated and laid the foundation stone for development projects worth ₹995 crore. See 3 pictures

stories.title: Shri Ram Katha begins at Gorakhnath Mandir today:CM Yogi to attend opening day; live streaming on YouTube, Facebook and X
stories.summary: On the occasion of Guru Purnima week in Gorakhpur, a grand Shri Ramkatha is being organised at Gorakhnath Temple from Thursday. Kathakar Acharya Shantanu Maharaj from Prayagraj will narrate the Katha. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will also participate in the Katha inauguration programme. The Shri Ramkatha, which will be held daily from 3 pm to 6 pm, will be live telecast on all social media platforms of Gorakhnath Temple -- YouTube, Facebook and X. The Katha will conclude on 29 July on the auspicious occasion of Guru Purnima. Yogi Kamalnath, the chief priest of Shri Gorakhnath Temple, gave details on Guru Purnima week, on Wednesday night. Saints from Prayagraj will narrate the Katha He said that in the Sanatan tradition, the Guru-disciple relationship is beyond definition in unique words. On behalf of Shri Gorakshapith, the carrier of the Guru-disciple tradition, this year too, on the occasion of Guru Purnima, a grand Shri Ramkatha is being organised from Thursday, July 23, at the Mahant Digvijaynath Memorial Building of Shri Gorakhnath Temple. Acharya Shri Shantanu Ji Maharaj, who has come from Prayagraj, will narrate the Katha. A procession will be taken out before the Katha Yogi Kamalnath said that before the auspicious beginning of Shri Ramkatha on Thursday, saints, chief patron, other patrons, and 151 Veda-reciting students will take out a procession with conch sounds and band music. This procession will proceed at 2:45 PM in the afternoon from the sanctum sanctorum of Shri Gorakhnath Temple to the Katha pavilion located in Mahant Digvijaynath Memorial Building. After that, the grand Shri Ramkatha will commence. Yogi Kamalnath invited all devotees to listen to the Katha. He informed that the conclusion and Purnahuti of Shri Ramkatha in the presence of CM Yogi will be held on July 29 from 9 AM to 11:30 AM. On Guru Purnima day, there will be a traditional programme of special worship, blessings, bhajans and community feast at the temple. stories.title: NEET aspirant gangraped in Chitrakoot:Boyfriend held hostage on hill by 3 men posing as forest officials
stories.summary: In Chitrakoot, UP, three youths gang-raped a NEET student who had come for sightseeing. According to the police, the girl was sitting on a hill with her boyfriend when three men arrived. They posed as forest officials and started threatening the couple. Then they began beating up the male victim. It is alleged that one of the accused tied the boyfriend's hands and feet with a towel. The other two dragged the female student into the bushes by threatening her. They raped her one by one. Then all three fled from the spot. The boyfriend somehow untied his hands and feet and reached the girl. After coming down from the hill, he called the police. Police registered a case based on the student's statement. CCTVs are being examined in the area. Based on suspicion, police have taken one suspect into custody. He is being interrogated. The incident occurred in the forest of Devangana Valley in Bahilpurwa Police Station area, 12 km away from the district headquarters. Police said, “A 20-year-old female student from Satna, Madhya Pradesh, is preparing for NEET while staying in Kota, Rajasthan. She had come home on leave a few days ago. Her boyfriend (17), a resident of Chitrakoot, is studying in 12th grade. They became friends on social media two years ago. Then an affair started.” Minor boyfriend narrated his ordeal The boyfriend said, “Girlfriend came to meet me on Wednesday. At 1 PM, both of us reached Devangana valley on a bike. We were sitting on a hill in the valley, talking. We were making reels. At 3 PM, three boys on a bike arrived. Claiming to be forest department employees, they started interrogating. They started touching my girlfriend inappropriately. When I protested, they started threatening us.” “They started blackmailing and demanding money. When I refused, they started beating me with a belt. One held me, and the other two started threatening my girlfriend. They said if we made noise, they would throw both of us down the hill. Then they forcibly took her into the bushes and raped her. After a while, the accused who was holding me hostage also went into the bushes. Even he raped my girlfriend,” the boyfriend said. He said that his girlfriend was screaming. She was begging for mercy. “I was lying on the ground listening to her screams. I was struggling to free myself. Somehow I freed my hands. I ran and reached the girlfriend. By then, the accused had fled. I called Dial-112 from my mobile. The call didn't connect due to no network,” he said. “When I went down the hill a bit, I got network on my mobile. I called again and summoned the police. The police arrived at 4:45 PM. They started searching for the accused. Both of us were admitted to the hospital,” he said. Medical examination of both will be conducted Station In-charge Vivek Singh said, "After receiving information about the rape in Devangana Ghati, the PRV team immediately reached the spot. The boyfriend has been discharged after primary treatment. The girl student's medical examination is being conducted. SP Arun Kumar Singh said: The student has mentioned gangrape in her statement to the police. The boyfriend is a minor. Therefore, his medical examination will also be conducted. An FIR has been registered based on the complaint and investigation is underway. CCTV footage from around the location and help from passersby is being taken to search for the accused. Two teams have been formed. SP MLA gave warning of gherao SP's Sadar MLA Anil Pradhan has launched a sharp attack on the state government and police-administration. In a statement issued on social media, he said, “The place where this incident occurred is just 500 meters from the proposed Devangana airport boundary, and the Collectorate and SP office are only 3 km away. Despite this, such an incident happening in broad daylight raises serious questions about law and order. If the accused are not arrested soon, the SP office will be gheraoed along with SP workers.”

stories.title: ₹72-crore fake drug case raises questions:Lab clears 27 of 28 samples, probe links stretch from Lucknow to Agra
stories.summary: Serious questions have emerged over Uttar Pradesh’s high-profile counterfeit drug case after laboratory tests cleared 27 of the 28 medicine samples seized during a joint operation by the Special Task Force (STF) and the Drug Department in August 2025. At the time, authorities had claimed to have unearthed counterfeit medicines worth ₹72 crore from Agra’s Fawwara wholesale medicine market. However, the Central Drugs Laboratory later found only one sample to be substandard, while the remaining 27 met prescribed quality standards. The findings have triggered debate over the investigation, especially as another major drug seizure in June 2026 awaits laboratory analysis. Fresh 2026 seizure still awaiting test reports In June 2026, the STF and Drug Department carried out another large-scale crackdown, seizing medicines worth ₹3.80 crore. Around 90 samples have been sent for laboratory testing, but the reports are still awaited. Following the 2025 laboratory findings, traders and industry representatives are closely watching the outcome of the latest investigation. Drug companies had declared medicines fake during raids On August 22, 2025, the Drug Department and STF raided He Maa Medico, Bansal Medical Agency, their associated firms, and Golden Transport Company in Agra’s Fawwara medicine market. Representatives of several pharmaceutical companies were called to the site during the operation. After examining packaging, fonts, holograms, batch numbers, and QR codes, they reportedly identified multiple medicines as counterfeit. Investigators claimed that many of the medicines had been shown as procured from firms in Puducherry, including Aman Pharma, Meenakshi Pharma, and Param House. Large quantities of medicines, including the anti-allergy drug Allegra, were seized. Authorities also alleged that some pharmaceutical companies had never supplied the medicines to the firms from which they were recovered. Raids were also conducted at Lucknow’s Aminabad medicine market. How the alleged counterfeit network operated According to the STF’s investigation, the alleged racket purchased a genuine medicine pack from the market and then used its batch number and QR code to manufacture between 100 and 1,000 counterfeit packs. Company representatives reportedly found that multiple medicine boxes carried the same QR code, whereas genuine pharmaceutical manufacturers issue a unique QR code for every pack. Based on these findings, investigators claimed to have exposed a large counterfeit medicine network operating through fake billing practices. Authorities alleged that medicines were procured from Puducherry using addresses in Lucknow and distributed from Agra to other states. Only one pneumonia drug failed laboratory tests The 28 samples collected during the August 2025 raids were sent to the Central Drugs Laboratory for analysis. The laboratory report, received in November, found 27 samples compliant with quality standards, while only one pneumonia medicine was classified as substandard. The findings sparked controversy, with traders questioning how medicines declared counterfeit by company representatives during the raids could later pass laboratory quality tests. Experts say laboratory and counterfeit tests serve different purposes Experts note that laboratory testing primarily evaluates the chemical composition and quality of medicines. Determining whether a medicine is counterfeit, however, also involves examining packaging, trademarks, batch numbers, QR codes, and supply chain records. As a result, a medicine may meet chemical quality standards while still being considered counterfeit if its branding or origin has been falsified. Nine cases registered, more than 40 accused Following the 2025 operation, the STF and Drug Department registered nine criminal cases and named more than 40 people as accused. Several individuals were arrested and sent to jail before securing bail. The laboratory findings have since led to renewed questions among medicine traders about the transparency of the investigation and the basis on which the initial counterfeit claims were made. Focus now on 2026 investigation Between June 22 and 24, 2026, authorities again conducted extensive raids across 38 medical firms and warehouses, seizing medicines worth ₹3.80 crore. The consignment included government-supplied medicines, physician samples, expired medicines, and other suspicious stock. A total of 90 samples have been sent for laboratory examination. Industry stakeholders say the forthcoming laboratory report could become crucial. If most of the medicines are again found to meet quality standards, fresh questions may arise over the investigation process, enforcement methods, and the criteria used to classify medicines as counterfeit.

stories.title: Yogi orders strict action against land mafia during Janata Darshan:CM hears around 200 grievances in Gorakhpur, meets children and gifts chocolates
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday directed officials to take strict action against land mafias involved in illegal encroachment while interacting with citizens during a Janata Darshan in Gorakhpur. On the second day of his three-day visit to the city, the Chief Minister heard the grievances of around 200 people at the Gorakhnath Temple premises. He assured citizens that every genuine complaint would be addressed and instructed officials to ensure prompt resolution of public issues. Strict warning against illegal land encroachment Addressing complaints related to land disputes, the Chief Minister said that anyone found illegally occupying another person's land will face stringent action. Officials, including the ADG Zone, Commissioner, DIG, District Magistrate, Senior Superintendent of Police, and the Chief Minister's OSD, were present during the public hearing. Citizens arrived early to present their grievances People began arriving at the Gorakhnath Temple early in the morning. After security checks, they were seated outside the Mahant Digvijaynath Memorial Hall. At around 7:30 a.m., Yogi Adityanath personally met each complainant, collected their applications, asked about their place of residence, and assured them that the concerned officials would take appropriate action. Medical assistance and family disputes raised Several women sought financial assistance for the treatment of their family members. The Chief Minister instructed officials to prepare cost estimates and ensure that eligible beneficiaries receive financial support. A young woman requested help in securing a hospital bed for her relative at SGPGI, Lucknow. In another case, a woman alleged that her in-laws were preventing her from living in her matrimonial home. The Chief Minister directed officials to counsel the family and, if necessary, ensure that the woman is allowed to occupy her lawful residence. Another woman claimed that two children from her family had been falsely implicated and sent to jail. Yogi Adityanath said that if they were innocent, justice would be ensured, and ordered an inquiry into the matter. CM interacts with children During the public interaction, the Chief Minister also greeted children accompanying their families, affectionately interacted with them, and distributed chocolates. Feeds cows at Gorakhnath Temple Gaushala Before the Janata Darshan, Yogi Adityanath visited the Gaushala at the Gorakhnath Temple, where he fed jaggery and rotis to the cows and spent time petting them. The cows appeared eager as they gathered around the Chief Minister while he fed them, a scene that drew attention during his morning visit.

stories.title: ‘Husband's death should look natural’, says snakebite murder accused:Wife searched venomous snakes on Google
stories.summary: In the first part of this story, we explained how Damini, accused of orchestrating her husband Atul's death through a snakebite in Meerut, became involved in an extramarital relationship. The second and final part details how her married boyfriend Tushar allegedly helped her execute the plan with the assistance of snake charmers, in an attempt to make the killing appear to be a natural death. 'It should look like a natural death' According to the police investigation, Damini allegedly told Tushar one day- Kill Atul in such a way that it doesn't look like murder, but a natural death. You remember the Ravita-Amardeep case from April 2025. It happened in our neighbouring village, where Ravita and her lover left a snake on her husband's bed. Why don't we do the same? Tushar allegedly agreed with the idea and said he knew two snake charmers, Sonu and Uday, from Khadar Basti. He reportedly approached them, saying- Someone has to be killed through a snakebite, but it should not appear to be murder. It should look like a normal death. When the snake charmers asked who the target was, Tushar allegedly replied that it was the husband of a female friend who wanted to get rid of him because he was causing her distress. Police claim a deal was struck for ₹5 lakh, with an advance payment of ₹15,000. The snake charmers allegedly instructed Tushar that Atul would first need to be heavily intoxicated or rendered unconscious before they released the snake. They also said the snake would have to be kept hungry to increase the likelihood of it biting. The alleged plan was scheduled for the night of 17 July. Google search for the most venomous snake After finalising the arrangement, Tushar allegedly informed Damini that the plan would involve a venomous snake, ensuring that the post-mortem would indicate death by snakebite and arouse no suspicion. He allegedly warned her not to repeat the mistake made in the 2025 Ravita case, where investigators concluded the husband had actually been strangled before a non-venomous snake was placed on the bed. According to the investigation, Damini said she had already searched Google to learn- Tushar allegedly told her there was no need to search further and showed her a photograph on his mobile phone of the snake that would allegedly be used. Police claim it was a black krait, one of India's most venomous snakes, which had deliberately been kept hungry. Sleeping pills mixed into milk According to the police, on the night of 16 July, Damini and Atul had dinner together before Atul went to bed. Damini allegedly went into the kitchen, mixed sleeping tablets into a glass of milk and gave it to Atul before lying down beside him. At around 2 am, she allegedly got out of bed, picked up her seven-year-old son, Manik, and left the bedroom. She then lay down with him on a cot outside the room and allegedly called Tushar, telling him- Come now. Atul is asleep. Snake released inside the bedroom Police allege that Tushar then arrived at the house with snake charmers Sonu and Uday, carrying a box containing a live black krait. Damini allegedly led them into the bedroom. According to investigators, the snake charmers advised that the snake should be released directly onto the bed to prevent it escaping. Damini allegedly handed them a bedsheet. The four allegedly covered Atul with the sheet before Sonu and Uday lifted one side and released the hungry krait onto the bed. Police claim the snake bit Atul's feet two or three times. The three men allegedly waited for around 20 minutes, checked whether Atul had died and then left the house. Before leaving, Tushar allegedly instructed Damini to begin crying and raising the alarm the following morning before going back to sleep. Damini then allegedly slept beside her son. Morning drama to make the death look natural At around 6 am on 17 July, Damini allegedly entered the bedroom carrying tea for Atul. According to the police, she pretended to wake him before screaming for help when he did not respond. Neighbours gathered after hearing her cries. She allegedly told them Atul had been bitten by a snake and pointed to the snakebite marks on his foot, saying there was still a snake inside the room. Initially, neighbours believed Atul had died from a snakebite. However, members of Atul's family became suspicious. His elder brother informed the police. When officers arrived, they found Damini sitting beside her husband's body, crying. How police uncovered the alleged conspiracy During questioning, police asked Damini how Atul had died. She allegedly said she had left the bedroom during the night because it was too hot and had slept outside with her son. Investigators said they found her explanation suspicious. Police then examined her call records and allegedly discovered that she had spoken several times during the night to Tushar Payla. After Tushar was detained, investigators claim he disclosed the entire alleged conspiracy involving Damini and the two snake charmers.

stories.title: How to check if petrol contains only 20% ethanol:File a complaint if you suspect irregularities; can also be used for cooking, govt to provide subsidy
stories.summary: When filling petrol in a bike or car, many motorists wonder how much ethanol is blended with the fuel. Is it 20%, or more? While it cannot be identified by sight or smell, there is a simple test that can help estimate the ethanol content. Meanwhile, the Central Government is also preparing a major policy to promote ethanol as a domestic cooking fuel. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas is working on a new policy under which ethanol will be promoted as an alternative to LPG for household cooking. How to check whether petrol contains E20 Ethanol ? Petrol and ethanol mix completely, making it impossible to distinguish them visually or by smell. However, you can carry out a simple water test in about two minutes. Since ethanol dissolves in water, the petrol separates out. The water-ethanol mixture settles at the bottom. According to the government and public-sector oil companies, claims that petrol contains more than 20% ethanol are false. They state that only E20-grade petrol is currently being supplied. How to check whether your vehicle is E20-Compatible ? You can verify whether your vehicle supports E20 fuel by- Most vehicles manufactured after April 2023 carry an E20 Compatible sticker. For vehicles manufactured before 2023, prolonged use of E20 fuel is claimed to potentially affect rubber hoses, gaskets and fuel injectors over time. Owners of older vehicles are advised to- Where to report suspected fuel adulteration If your water test indicates ethanol or water content above 20%, or if an E20 information board is not displayed at a petrol station, complaints can be lodged through the following channels- Government plans to introduce Ethanol for household cooking Ethanol is a highly flammable liquid and will not be stored in existing LPG cylinders. Instead, the proposed system will use specially designed ethanol-compatible cooking stoves and fuel containers, which are expected to meet safety standards. The government's objective is to expand the use of biofuel (ethanol) beyond transport and into household kitchens. Subsidy planned for Ethanol stoves and fuel The proposed policy includes financial support to encourage adoption. 'Ethanol ATMs' planned at fuel stations Under the proposed scheme, 'Ethanol ATMs' will be installed at petrol pumps and retail outlets. Consumers will be able to fill special ethanol canisters, take them home and use the fuel in ethanol-compatible cooking stoves. When will Ethanol cooking become available? The ethanol cooking initiative is still in the planning stage. The government's new policy is expected to be announced by September 2026, after which the required infrastructure will be developed. The system is therefore expected to become available to the public towards the end of 2026 or later. The government has clarified that ethanol is intended as an alternative to LPG, not a replacement. Consumers will be free to choose either LPG or ethanol, depending on their preference and convenience. It has also stated that reports claiming LPG cylinders will be discontinued from 1 October 2026 are false. Aim is to reduce LPG imports India imports a significant share of its LPG requirements. According to the government's estimates, if 7 billion litres of ethanol are used annually for domestic cooking, the country could save billions of rupees in foreign exchange by reducing LPG imports.

stories.title: Premanand Maharaj's new ashram draws attention after Virat-Anushka visit:Built on nearly 9 bigha land in Mathura, also equipped with dialysis unit
stories.summary: Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma arrived at Saint Premanand Maharaj's new ashram Yamuna Vihar Kunj in Vrindavan on July 22 (Wednesday). Both stayed in the ashram for about 1 hour. When they came out, Virat had a sandalwood tilak on his forehead and prasad in his hand. This is the same ashram about which devotees have been wanting to know for the past two months. Saint Premanand Maharaj has left his old Keli Kunj ashram and is performing bhajan-sadhana here. He gives darshan to devotees here. Why did Maharaj leave Keli Kunj ashram and make a new abode on the banks of Yamuna? What is the way to reach here? To know the answers to these questions, Dainik Bhaskar's team reached the ashram. They gathered information by talking to people and observing the routes leading to the ashram and the arrangements there. Read the full report Premanand Maharaj Shifted from Keli Kunj to the Banks of Yamuna Saint Premanand Maharaj has been spending very little time in his old Keli Kunj ashram for the past 2 months. He has also postponed his foot pilgrimage since May 18. Poor health has been cited as the reason behind this. A few days ago, a video of Saint Premanand giving discourse to his disciples on the banks of Yamuna also surfaced. In this video, he asked everyone to chant the name of Radha and not to follow him. Meanwhile, news has emerged that Premanand Maharaj has shifted to his new ashram, Yamuna Vihar Kunj Ashram. He is also giving darshan to devotees from here. New ashram is 15 kilometers away from Keli Kunj Ashram Premanand Maharaj's trust, Shri Hit Radha Keli Kunj, has built a new ashram named Yamuna Vihar Kunj. It is built on the banks of the Yamuna near Jahangirpur village in Mant tehsil. It is about one kilometer away from the Lakshmiji temple located in Belvan. It is about 15 kilometers by road from Kali Kunj Ashram. To see the ashram, our team crossed the Yamuna by steamer from Keshighat. After that, we reached Belvan Temple through muddy and uneven roads. ‘Only administration and ashram people are allowed inside’ Near the Lakshmi Temple in Belvan, an unpaved road leads to the ashram. Gravel was being laid on this road. Meanwhile, volunteers were present, setting up camps nearby. We were moving towards the ashram when the volunteers stopped us with folded hands. They said, no one is allowed to enter the ashram without permission. Only those people are allowed to go further who have received permission from the chief volunteer. After the volunteers stopped us, we stood there. Just then, vehicles of the SDM of Mant, CO, and other officers arrived there. The volunteers did not stop these vehicles. These vehicles moved forward without any hindrance. When I asked the volunteers, they said that vehicles of the administration and the ashram are allowed to go inside. After this, we talked to the local people about the ashram. People, without appearing on camera, said that here volunteers allow people to come and go based on instructions received from the ashram. However, farmers of the village can use this path to go to and from their fields. There are two ways to reach the ashram First route- This route goes from Keli Kunj Ashram via Varah Ghat to the Khadar region beyond Saubhari Van. From here, cross the Yamuna by boat or steamer and walk about 2 kilometers to reach the ashram. Second Route- This is a road route. In this, you will reach Mathura Road from Keli Kunj Ashram. From here, one reaches Belvan Temple via Yamuna Expressway Link Road and then through Jahangirpur village. From here, the ashram is about one kilometer inside. It takes 30 to 45 minutes to reach by this route. Yamuna Vihar Kunj built on nearly 9 bighas of land In this conversation, we came to know that the land on which the ashram is being built belonged to Mangal Singh, a resident of Jahangirpur village. After that, we searched and reached Mangal Singh's house. Here we met Mangal's son, Moolchand. Moolchand says - About 5 acres (about 8.75 bigha) of land has been taken from our family for the ashram. Out of this, 2 bigha of land was taken 3 months ago. The remaining land was taken a month ago. Out of this, about one bigha of land has permanent construction. The rest has huts and trees planted. The ashram has been built very beautifully. 2 Halls, Dialysis unit and flood protection system Moolchand said - The ashram has 2 large halls, where Maharaj ji performs satsang and serves Radharani. A dialysis machine has been installed in a container here. Doctors perform Premanand Maharaj's dialysis from time to time. To prevent floodwaters from reaching the ashram, a platform about 7-8 feet high has been built along the Yamuna riverbank. After this, high boundaries have been constructed. When we tried to find out from Moolchand how much land was given for the ashram, he did not disclose anything. Later, we found out that the rate for the land where the ashram is built is approximately 55 lakh rupees per hectare. New abode chosen for peace and solitude Local residents said that Saint Premanand Maharaj chose Yamuna Vihar Kunj because the calm and natural environment along the Yamuna river is conducive to solitary devotion and meditation. Compared to Kali Kunj Ashram, there is less crowd here. This allows him time for spiritual practice and contemplation. This is why he is staying here these days, engaged in devotion and meditation. Not everyone is allowed to go to Yamuna Bihar Kunj Ashram. Servants are stationed at various points along the way, who stop people one kilometer before the ashram. Saint Premanand Maharaj will give darshan in both ashrams on Guru Purnima Saint Premanand Maharaj will celebrate the Guru Purnima festival in both his ashrams. Preparations are underway in both Keli Kunj and Yamuna Vihar Kunj ashrams. From July 23 to 28, Saint Premanand Maharaj will give darshan to devotees in Yamuna Vihar Kunj. After this, on July 29, he will meet devotees at Kelly Kunj Ashram. Kelly Kunj Ashram has been specially decorated for Guru Purnima. From the main gate to the ashram premises, placards with religious messages have been put up. Charan Pujan (worship of feet) will be performed every day during the Guru Purnima festival at Kelly Kunj Ashram.

stories.title: Three reel-enthusiast sisters marry their cameraman:Take seven vows at Amroha temple; Hindu groups call it violation of tradition
stories.summary: Three sisters in Amroha who make reels have claimed to marry their own cameraman. All three are between 18 and 20 years old. They worshipped at the Chamunda Mata Temple and took seven vows around the fire, considering it a witness. The cameraman applied vermilion to their foreheads and the brides touched their husband's feet to seek blessings. However, no one from either family attended the wedding. This marriage came to light when the video surfaced on Wednesday at 5 PM. Leaders of Hindu organizations say that marrying in such a way at a religious place is a violation of Sanatan Dharma. Decorum has been broken. Seeing the opposition, the three sisters released a video defending themselves. They said, "In ancient times, there was King Dasharatha, who had three queens. Was that an insult then?" The three girls got married on July 17. 3 pictures of the wedding- Know the full story Saroj (20 years old), Savitri (19 years old), and Santosh (18 years old), residents of Dhauria village, are real sisters. All three are social media influencers. They create video content on Instagram-Facebook. They have IDs on Facebook and Instagram, on which only 27 videos are currently uploaded. All three have a good fan following on social media. They have over 4.69 lakh followers on Instagram and more than 84 thousand on Facebook. Vikas alias Vikku, a resident of Shyampuri village, is the cameraman for the three sisters. He had been working for the three sisters for the past 6 months. He also played the role of husband in stories related to the village. Elder bride is pursuing B.Tech, groom is intermediate pass Saroj is a second-year B.Tech student, while Savitri and Santosh have passed 12th grade. Their father Ramesh is a farmer. Vikku passed 12th grade this year. He now wants to pursue LLB. He is the youngest of three brothers. After marriage, Vikku is living at his in-laws' house. Saroj, Savitri, and Santosh stated- They have been together since childhood and did not want to be separated in the future either. When their family members tried to arrange their marriages in different places, they decided to marry the same cameraman together, rather than being separated. According to Vikas, he was aware of their feelings and situation. Therefore, he married all three with the intention of keeping them together. Dr. Shivcharan Das, manager of Chamunda Mata Temple, said , At the time the marriage was being discussed, beautification work was going on in the temple. No priest was present there. Trader leader opposed the marriage Local people and Hindu organizations, including trader leader Mukesh Gupta, have strongly objected to this marriage. They say that such an act at a religious place is a violation of Sanatan Dharma and social norms. They have appealed to society to take strict action against such people. 'We are happy with the marriage' In response to people's protest, the three sisters released a video. They said - We have not done anything wrong. It's all about love. All three of us can be happy together. There is nothing wrong with it. When we are happy and we have gotten married, what's the problem with that? All three of us are adults. Hasanpur Kotwali in-charge Rajesh Kumar Tiwari said that the sisters who got married stated that they got married at Chamunda Temple of their own free will.

stories.summary: Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma visited Saint Premanand Maharaj's new Yamuna Vihar Kunj Ashram in Vrindavan on Wednesday. The couple walked to the ashram barefoot, wearing face masks. As they left the ashram, Virat was seen with a sandalwood tilak on his forehead and prasad in his hand. stories.title: UP's oldest Samajwadi Party MLA Alambadi Azmi dies:Took his last breath at 90; won Assembly elections from Azamgarh five times
stories.summary: The Samajwadi Party's oldest MLA, Alambadi Azmi, has died at the age of 90 after a prolonged illness. He breathed his last late on Wednesday night at his residence in Azamgarh. A five-time MLA from the Nizamabad Assembly constituency, Azmi will be laid to rest at 4 pm on Thursday. On 13 April, he was admitted to Medanta Hospital in Lucknow after his health deteriorated. He continued to receive treatment there through May, June and July before being discharged a few days ago. Used a keypad mobile phone Born on 16 March 1936 in Azamgarh, Alambadi Azmi represented the Nizamabad Assembly constituency continuously from 1996 to 2007. Despite his long political career, he was known for his simple lifestyle. He continued to use a keypad mobile phone and wore clothes made from fabric costing ₹30 per metre, produced at the Tanda textile mill in Ambedkar Nagar. Azmi completed his Intermediate education at Islamia College, Gorakhpur, in 1953. He later earned a degree in Mechanical Engineering from Gorakhpur in 1956. Counted among Mulayam Singh Yadav's closest associates Known for his Gandhian values, Alambadi Azmi was regarded as one of Mulayam Singh Yadav's closest political associates and had a reputation as an exceptionally honest public representative. One incident often cited to illustrate his integrity dates back to the 1996 Assembly elections, when Mulayam Singh Yadav reportedly gave him ₹5 lakh to contest the election. Azmi returned the money to Mulayam Singh in Lucknow, saying he did not need it to fight the election. This gesture became one of the defining examples of his personal honesty and frugal lifestyle.

stories.title: Ghaghra river swells in UP, 28 flood posts on alert:Two killed by lightning in Sonbhadra; rain warning for 75 districts
stories.summary: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for 69 districts of Uttar Pradesh, with heavy rainfall expected in 18 districts on Thursday. According to the IMD, the weather is likely to remain mainly clear in Bahraich, Shravasti, Balrampur, Siddharthnagar, Maharajganj and Kushinagar. In Lucknow, the sky has remained cloudy since Thursday morning. On Wednesday, several parts of the state recorded significant rainfall. Mau received the highest rainfall at 72 mm, followed by 70 mm in Lalitpur, 58 mm in Sonbhadra, and 41.5 mm in Prayagraj. Meanwhile, continuous rainfall over the past 10 days has caused rivers to swell across the state. In Lakhimpur Kheri, the Sharda River is flowing above the danger mark, with floodwater entering riverside villages. Crocodiles have also been spotted on roads and in agricultural fields. In Sonbhadra, rising water levels in the Ghaghra River washed away the road leading to the district jail. In Varanasi, nearly 50 small and large temples between Assi Ghat and Namo Ghat have been submerged. Monsoon activity to remain weak until 25 July Regional Meteorological Centre scientist Atul Kumar Singh said the low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal has weakened, while the monsoon trough has shifted south of its normal position. As a result, monsoon activity is expected to remain weak across Uttar Pradesh between 23 July and 25 July. The IMD has forecast light to moderate rainfall at isolated places during this period but has not issued any heavy rain warning for the state. See 2 pictures from Wednesday- Why has the monsoon weakened? According to meteorologists, the decline in rainfall is primarily due to- These changes have shifted the focus of monsoon activity towards west-central India, reducing the likelihood of widespread rainfall across Uttar Pradesh. Weather likely to change again from 26 July The IMD expects the monsoon to become active again from 26-27 July. Following this, good rainfall is likely in many parts of Uttar Pradesh. If fresh weather systems develop, rainfall activity could intensify during the last week of July. IMD issues advisory for farmers and residents The Meteorological Department has advised farmers that heavy rainfall is unlikely over the next few days, and agricultural activities should be planned accordingly. Residents in areas where thunderstorms and lightning are expected have been urged to- Avoid standing in open areas. Stay away from trees during lightning. Keep clear of electricity poles and power lines. Why could UP receive less rain this monsoon? Dr M. Mohapatra, Director General of the India Meteorological Department, said La Niña-like conditions in the Pacific Ocean are coming to an end, with weather patterns showing signs of shifting towards El Niño, which is generally associated with below-normal rainfall. He said this indicates that the 2026 southwest monsoon could be weaker than normal. In addition, reduced snow cover across the Northern Hemisphere between January and March this year may also affect the strength of the monsoon.

stories.title: Ram Mandir Trust to train priests from across India:No fee to be charged; trust to bear lodging and food expenses
stories.summary: A permanent school will be built in the Ram Mandir complex in Ayodhya for the training of priests. Priests will be trained according to Vedic and Ramanandi traditions for temples across the country. How will these priests be selected for training? How will applications be taken? This format is being prepared. The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust decided in a meeting that this training will be completely free. The Trust will fully arrange for the accommodation and food of the 'Batuk' (young students/trainees). The Trust believes that when priests trained in Ayodhya serve in temples across the country and abroad, the religious tradition and worship methods here will gain a new identity. Devotees' trust will also rise. First 30 priests were trained, now a permanent school will be built Swami Govind Dev Giri, the treasurer of the Trust, says, ‘A one-year priest training program was conducted during the construction of the Ram Mandir. In this, about 30 priests were trained in worship methods, Vedic mantras, rituals, and religious procedures. Later, this program was stopped. Now the Trust has decided to make it permanent. It has not yet been decided in which part of the temple this school will be prepared. Work in this direction will be started soon with the consent of the Trust members’. What will be taught in the school? Here, not only chanting of mantras, but also the entire system related to temple management will be trained. After completing the training, priests will be able to serve in temples across the country. These will be the responsibilities of the committee The Trust has also formed a 9-member religious committee for the temple's religious arrangements. Among these, 5 members will be from Ayodhya's saint community and 4 from the Trust. Know the big decisions of the trust Official spokesperson to be appointed for the first time To provide accurate and regular information to people through the media, the Trust has decided to appoint an official spokesperson for the first time. Now, all official information and clarifications from the Trust will be issued through a single medium.

stories.title: SP set to finalise candidates for 46 UP Assembly seats:Purvanchal gets biggest share; 27 close-loss faces set for repeat
stories.summary: The Samajwadi Party (SP) has almost finalised candidates for 46 Assembly constituencies ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The list includes 19 seats in Purvanchal, 13 in western Uttar Pradesh, and 14 in central Uttar Pradesh. According to party sources, the official list is expected to be released in September. SP is also likely to field the same candidates in 27 constituencies where the party lost by a margin of less than 5,000 votes in the 2022 Assembly elections. The party believes these seats can be won in 2027. However, finalising candidates remains a major challenge. While SP continues to follow its PDA (Pichda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak – Backward, Dalit and Minority) strategy, it is preparing to reduce the number of Muslim and Yadav candidates and give greater representation to leaders from other backward communities and Dalits. Party sources say Akhilesh Yadav is not relying solely on caste equations. He is also closely evaluating the booth-level performance and organisational work of every ticket aspirant. Dalit candidates likely on more than 20 general seats For the 2027 Assembly elections, SP is continuing with its PDA formula, while also ensuring that loyal upper-caste leaders within the party are not sidelined. According to party sources, the number of Muslim and Yadav candidates is expected to be reduced. In addition to the 84 Scheduled Caste (SC)-reserved constituencies, the party is planning to field Dalit candidates on 20–25 general seats. Akhilesh meets aspirants; recommendations won't count The party is seeking feedback from district units while finalising candidates. Akhilesh Yadav is personally holding meetings with district office-bearers and ticket aspirants. At the same time, he has made it clear that all party workers must accept the final decision on ticket distribution and that rebellion over nominations will not be tolerated. Akhilesh is also assessing what each aspirant has done to strengthen the party's vote base at the booth level. Their level of activity during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is also being evaluated. The SP chief wants candidates who can effectively manage booth-level challenges. Candidate selection is therefore being based on survey reports, local caste equations, public image and booth-level organisational work. Akhilesh has already made it clear that tickets will not be awarded based on recommendations. Only those who meet the party's selection criteria will be nominated. Candidate list to be released after Congress seat-sharing talks SP has consistently maintained that it intends to contest the Assembly elections in alliance with the Congress. However, the two parties are yet to reach an agreement on seat sharing. Uttar Pradesh Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam has sought 200 seats for the party, while SP is reportedly unwilling to offer more than 60 seats. Akhilesh Yadav has said that Congress must first explain its winning prospects on the constituencies it is seeking before any decision is taken. Once a seat-sharing agreement is reached, SP is expected to release its first list of Assembly candidates in September.

stories.title: Speedboat collision at Gorakhpur's Ramgarh Tal kills youth:Three injured; group had come from Kushinagar for an outing
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur's Ramgarh Tal boating area, around 9:30 PM on Sunday night, two boats collided. One young man aboard died, while three others were injured. The deceased has been identified as Lakhmuddin (21), a resident of Pipra village in Hata, Kushinagar district. Qayamuddin Ansari (25), who is seriously injured, is a resident of Aziz Nagar in Kaptanganj, Kushinagar district. Both friends had come from Kushinagar for sightseeing. The incident occurred during speed boating. People started drowning as the boat overturned According to the police, eight people were on the boat. The boat was moving from the platform towards the lake. Just then, another boat was returning to the platform with passengers. Meanwhile, the two boats collided head-on, causing the outgoing boat to lose control and overturn. As soon as the boat overturned, the people on board started screaming. Many people fell into the water and began to drown. Security personnel present at the scene and the in-charge of the boating outpost immediately started the rescue operation. All people were safely pulled out of the water. Seriously injured Lakhmuddin and Qayamuddin Ansari and a child were immediately rushed to the district hospital. Qayamuddin's condition remains serious During treatment, doctors declared Lakhmuddin dead. Qayamuddin and the child are still undergoing treatment. Among them, Qayamuddin's condition is said to be serious. Upon receiving information about the accident, the Vice Chairman of Gorakhpur Development Authority along with other administrative officers reached the district hospital. Officials inquired about the condition of the injured and instructed doctors to provide better treatment. Police officers also inspected the accident site. An investigation into the accident has been launched. In the preliminary investigation, the collision of both boats is being considered an accident. Police are also investigating whether there was any negligence in safety standards during boat operation. After the accident, questions have also started to arise regarding the safety arrangements and operation of Ramgarh Lake boating.

stories.title: Teacher thrashed with slipper nine times in 19 seconds:Student alleges molestation; accused spits on palm, licks it before apologising
stories.summary: In Kushinagar, a student hit a teacher nine times with a slipper in 19 seconds for molesting her. The student's family also severely beat the teacher. They made him spit on his palm and lick it. After this, the teacher apologised to the student and her family with folded hands. The video of the beating surfaced on Saturday evening. The incident took place in the Seorahi area, where an IIT-NEET coaching centre had opened just a month ago. The student used to go to this coaching centre to study. The student told her family that the teacher used to make obscene gestures towards her. After this, her family reached the coaching centre and severely beat the teacher. 3 pictures of the teacher's beating Now read what is visible in the video The accused teacher is sitting on a chair. The student's family members have surrounded him from all sides. They are beating him with slippers and kicks and punches. Meanwhile, the teacher is seen hiding his face. The family members remove his hand from his face. After this, they start slapping him hard on his cheeks. The accused teacher spits on his palms. Then he licks it. The student's family members tell her to beat him until her anger subsides. The student then hits the teacher with nine slippers in 19 seconds. Accused teacher and student's family absconding Currently, the accused teacher and the student who beat him, along with her family, are absconding. No complaint has been received from either side at the police station. When the police reached the spot after the video surfaced, the coaching centre was found closed. Sevarahi Station House Officer Manoj Verma said Upon receiving information, the police went to the spot, but the coaching centre was found closed. Action will be taken upon receiving a complaint.
