stories.title: Anil Rajbhar attacks Opposition:Says it seeks to vent frustration through riots and exploit disasters
stories.summary: State Minister Anil Rajbhar slammed the opposition on Sunday, saying their desperation to gain power is so immense that they want to vent their frustration through riots. Rajbhar was speaking at Gorakhpur's Circuit House. Speaking about the support received by the students' movement from the Opposition, Rajbhar said that it has two aspects. “Firstly, the students' movement, respecting their sentiments, had its demands met. Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned, and with that, the matter is closed. But those who are looking for opportunities in disaster, who are unable to defeat BJP and Prime Minister Narendra Modi in elections, those who cannot digest India's development, such people want to incite riots everywhere. This is their mentality,” he said. “They did not like the end of the movement, so they will try to do this again by changing their disguise. They are talking about a movement in Uttar Pradesh, let them do the movement. They have nothing to do with the development of the country or the state,” he said, adding that from 2012 to 2017 so many papers were leaked during the SP government but the Opposition had conveniently forgotten those. “Even the chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission had to be removed by order of the Supreme Court. Education had been made a joke. Every child in Uttar Pradesh knows this. Today, those very people are talking about education. The people of the country know everything very well,” Rajbhar said. The Cabinet Minister said that the agitation has taken place. “When Parliament convenes on Monday, the true face of the opposition will be seen. They had gone to Jantar Mantar to support students for educational reforms. They want to weaken the country. Tomorrow, the bill is coming to the House. Let's see if the opposition participates in the discussion or runs away from the field. Tomorrow, everything will become clear. The opposition will be completely exposed,” he said.

stories.title: Bareilly student assaulted on way to Jantar Mantar:Hindutva goon says, 'They were Hindus going to CJP protest; we treated the cockroaches'
stories.summary: A BSc student from Bareilly and his friend were beaten up by a Hindutva leader and his associates in Delhi. Both were going to Jantar Mantar on the morning of July 25 to participate in a CJP demonstration. The video of this incident surfaced on Sunday. The student said that on 25 July, around 5 am, he was going from Bangla Sahib Gurudwara in Delhi to Jantar Mantar with his friend. “Then Hindutva leader Satyam Pandit and his associates stopped us. First, they asked our names and religion,” he said. “After this, they started abusing us. He grabbed my friend's throat and started slapping him. He said that being a Hindu, you support CJP. Then he made us apologise in front of the camera,” he said. He also posted this video on Facebook. In the caption, he wrote - Treated the cockroach. After returning from Delhi, the student narrated the entire incident to the media on Sunday. See 2 pictures... Now read the complete matter... Stopped on the way, asked name and religion, then beaten Bareilly's Faridpur Mahadev Mohalla resident BSc student Ayush Ranjan had gone to Delhi on July 23 with his friend Rahul to participate in a CJP (CJP) demonstration. Ayush said, ''I was staying with my friend at Bangla Sahib Gurudwara in Delhi. As soon as I stepped out around 4 to 5 am on the morning of July 25, after reaching about 200 meters ahead, a young man came with his companions in a vehicle. He blocked our way. The young man asked if we were going to the CJP demonstration. As soon as we both said yes, he got furious. He started slapping my friend Rahul and began abusing him. There was a cameraman with him, and 4 or 5 people were sitting in the car. A young man sitting in the car kept making a video of the entire incident. The accused young man started asking Rahul to apologize on camera. I ran and asked nearby people for help. Then that young man took the vehicle and left from there.'' Video of the incident posted on social media The youth who beat and abused the students is Satyam Pandit, the National President of Rashtriya Veer Hindu Sena. He posted this video on his Facebook account on July 25 at 4:08 PM. Along with the video, he wrote - Went to Jantar Mantar and treated some cockroaches; we do what we say. Read the conversation between student and Hindutva leader in the video In the video, a Hindutva leader asks the students, "Are you supporting CJP?" Both respond with "yes." He then asks for their names, to which the first student says his name is Ayush. He then asks Ayush about his religion. When Ayush says "Hindu," he says, "Then why are you supporting this party? Anti-national slogans are being raised here, don't you feel ashamed?" To this, Ayush responds, "No." After this, the leader asks the second student present with them for his name and place of residence. Both say they are from Bareilly and are staying at Bangla Sahib Gurudwara. The second student says his name is Rahul. Finally, he asks both of them what they do. The students say they are BSc students. After this, in the video, the leader abuses them and asks the reason for participating in the protest. To this, Rahul says they have no connection with any organization. He had come to visit his sister, and both had just come to see Jantar Mantar. After this, the BJP leader threatens the students and asks them to apologize on video. Both students apologize. Despite this, the BJP leader grabs a student named Rahul and starts beating him. During this, he slaps him several times. Satyam Pandit has been in controversies before as well Ghaziabad resident Satyam Pandit has been involved in controversies over several cases before. He describes himself as the president of 'Hindu Veer Sena' on his Facebook profile. In August 2024, he was arrested on charges of allegedly giving inflammatory speeches regarding the Bangladeshi and Rohingya communities. After this, in February 2026, Ghaziabad Police also took action against him on charges of assaulting meat sellers during the closure of meat shops on Tuesday.

stories.title: BSF jawan hacks wife to death:Sits outside room after attack; claims he caught her with three different men
stories.summary: A BSF jawan who had come home on leave in Mainpuri killed his wife with a spade on suspicion of an affair. After committing the murder, the husband sat outside the room. This was revealed when his 9-year-old son came to wake his mother in the morning. He saw his mother lying on the cot drenched in blood. Police, who arrived on information, arrested the accused jawan from the spot itself. The wife's maternal family has filed a report against the husband. The incident is from the Karhal police station area at 8 AM on Sunday. Read the full case Neetu (32), living in Nagla Devjit village, was married to Sanjesh Yadav in 2011. The couple has a son named Nikhil. Sanjesh is posted in Jammu-Kashmir with the G-Company of the 53rd Battalion of BSF. He had come home on leave about 10 days ago. On Sunday morning, when Neetu did not come out of her room for a long time, her son Nikhil went to wake up his mother. He found his mother in a dead state. The son then informed the neighbors about this. When the neighbors reached the house, Neetu was lying on the cot drenched in blood. She had deep wounds on her head. A blood-stained spade was lying nearby. The body was covered with a sheet. As soon as the information about the woman's murder was received, Karhal police station police reached the spot. The body was sent for post-mortem. Neetu's father Balram Yadav said, ''I got information about the incident around 9 am. My grandson informed the neighbors after seeing his mother dead. After that, the neighbors called and told me that Neetu had been killed. Neetu had serious injuries on her eyebrows. My daughter was being continuously tortured since the marriage. Son-in-law Sanjesh had relationships with other women. Apart from this, there used to be frequent fights between husband and wife due to the son-in-law's alcohol addiction. He said that Sanjesh did not even give money to my daughter for expenses. Due to this reason, Neetu had filed a maintenance case against him in court, which is currently pending. He alleged that not only is Sanjesh involved in the incident, but his younger sister Rekha was also involved. Both together murdered Neetu.'' Son said - Father and aunt together killed mother Son Nikhil told the police - Aunt Rekha was also at home on Saturday evening. My father and aunt together killed my mother. Meanwhile, accused Sanjesh Yadav also confessed to committing the murder. Sanjesh said that he suspected his wife of having a relationship with another person. He had caught his wife with three different people. Police are investigating these claims of Sanjesh. Both sides made allegations of illicit relationships In this case, both parties have accused each other of illicit relationships. The maternal family alleges that Sanjesh had relationships with other women. This is why he used to torture Neetu. On the other hand, the accused husband, Sanjesh, claims that his wife had relationships with other people. Meanwhile, village head Ashok Kumar stated that BSF jawan Sanjesh had murdered his wife on Saturday night itself. After the incident, he went to a nearby room and slept. The incident came to light on Sunday around 8 AM when their son Nikhil went to the room to wake up his mother. Sanjesh was addicted to drinking alcohol. SP Abhishek Tiwari stated- Police reached the spot after receiving information about the murder of a woman in Devjit village. Investigation revealed that the husband killed her with a spade in a domestic dispute. The accused husband has been arrested from the spot. The body has been sent for post-mortem. Further action is being taken.

stories.title: 7-year-old boy attacks father with axe:Says, 'I chopped him into pieces' after being stopped from going to Jammu with aunt
stories.summary: A 7-year-old child attacked his sleeping disabled father with an axe in Gonda. He struck 10 consecutive blows, leaving his father seriously injured. Family members have admitted him to the hospital, where his condition remains critical. The child said, ''Papa, was not letting me go to Jammu. That's why I cut him into pieces.'' Actually, on Sunday around 10 AM, the child told his father that he wanted to go to Jammu with his aunt. The father refused and said that if he talked about going again, he would cut him with an axe. Saying this, the father went to sleep outside the house. Around 1 PM, the child saw an opportunity and picked up the axe kept in the house. After this, he attacked his father's head and face. The incident is from Dehat Kotwali. Read the entire incident in sequence... Bishan Lal lives with his family in Bhatta village of Basia Chaingram. He has 2 sons at home - Arvind (12) and Devraj (7). Bishan Lal is physically disabled in his leg. 7 years ago, after the birth of his younger son Devraj, Bishan Lal's wife left him and went away. The elder son lives with his uncle Shyam Manohar and aunt Shrimati in Jammu. Devraj lives at home with his father. Father refused to send him to Jammu These days, the child's aunt was visiting his house. His elder brother Arvind had also come along. Uncle, aunt, and elder brother were going to Jammu today. Devraj was also insisting on going with them. Aunt said that you ask your father. We will take you along only when he says so. Around 10 am, Devraj reached his father, Bishan Lal. He asked, ‘Papa, I will also go to Jammu with uncle’. At this, his father refused. When Devraj persisted stubbornly, the father said angrily, Listen to me. If you talk about going again, I will cut you with a sickle. Attacked father with axe in anger After this, Devraj went inside the house in anger. Bishan Lal went outside the house and slept on a cot under a tree. Around 1 PM, Devraj came out from inside the house with an axe. He attacked his father Bishan Lal's face and head repeatedly with the axe 10 times. Bishan Lal was covered in blood. He started writhing in pain on the cot itself. Hearing Bishan Lal's screams, other people came out from inside the house. Hearing the screams and cries, people from the neighborhood also gathered. The family members immediately took Bishan Lal to the hospital. The police have taken the boy into custody. He told the police- They were not letting me go to Jammu. First I asked my uncle if I could go to Jammu with you, then my aunt said that your father will be angry. Then I came and asked my father, aunt is saying that your father won't let you go. So he said that if you go, I will cut you with a sickle. After that I went inside the house, brought a sickle and cut him into pieces.

stories.title: Yogi announces cashless treatment of ₹5 lakh for teachers:₹3 crore accidental insurance cover to benefit 10 lakh people
stories.summary: In UP, degree college teachers will now receive cashless treatment up to ₹5 lakh. CM Yogi launched the 'Mukhyamantri Shikshak Cashless Yojana' (Chief Minister Teacher Cashless Scheme) in Agra on Sunday. This will provide free treatment facilities to approximately 10 lakh people, including around 1.28 lakh teachers from universities, government-aided, and private colleges in the state, along with their families. During this, Yogi also announced an accidental insurance cover scheme ranging from ₹1.5 crore to ₹3 crore. He said, "The government has signed an MoU with Punjab National Bank (PNB). This will provide teachers with accidental insurance of 1.50 crore, air accident insurance up to 3 crore, hospital expenses up to ₹60,000 (i.e., cash benefit), and term life insurance (Jeevan Bima) up to ₹12 lakh." Yogi appealed to teachers to teach students how to use social media correctly. He said- Social media is today's necessity. One cannot stay away from it, but it should be used for the benefit of society and the nation. Teachers should encourage students to be cautious of fake accounts and misleading information. Teach them to distinguish between right and wrong. It should be noted that 18 days ago, Yogi had launched a cashless treatment scheme from Varanasi for 1.2 million teachers, Shiksha Mitras, instructors, and cooks of primary and secondary schools. Know 2 big benefits of the new scheme- 5 points from Yogi's speech- 1. The teacher's place is highest in India's tradition Yogi said, “The teacher's place has been supreme in India's tradition. When a large part of the world was in the darkness of ignorance, India had already built universities like Taxila and Nalanda. Taxila, which is in Pakistan today, was part of undivided India. It was named after Taksha, the son of Lord Rama's brother Bharat.” 2. A true guru not only gives knowledge to the disciple, but also the right perspective Yogi narrated the story of the famous physician Jivaka. He said, “After completing his education, Jivaka sought permission from his teacher to return home. Taking a final test, the teacher asked him to bring a plant from the forest that had no medicinal properties. Jivaka searched in the forest for several days, but he could not find any such plant. Returning, he told the teacher, 'Nasti mulam anausadham' meaning there is no plant that does not have medicinal properties. Upon this, the teacher declared him successful in the test. The CM said that this incident shows that a true guru not only gives knowledge to his disciple but also the right vision." 3. Every student has potential; they need a teacher who can recognise it Yogi said, “What a student needs to learn will only be decided when the teacher guides them correctly. They should continuously talk to them. Listen to their words. Keep showing them the right path. Keep telling them right and wrong. Only then will there be a change in the student. Better results will be achieved.” 4. Study and academic environment in educational institutions are not like before He said, “There is no person who does not have the ability. The need is only for a teacher who can recognise and hone that ability. It must be ensured that no student falls prey to distraction. The study and academic environment in educational institutions are no longer what they used to be.” 5. Need to teach the correct use of social media Yogi said, “Today, there are many mediums to gain information in society. One section reads newspapers, another watches TV news, and a large number of youth get information from YouTube and other digital platforms on smartphones. In such a situation, students often consider what people who upload more content or gather more views as the truth. Whereas not every piece of information needs to be correct.” "People can also spread misinformation by creating fake accounts on social media. They can create confusion and tension in society. Lack of knowledge of correct facts makes the entire system a victim of disorder and anarchy, which affects both the present and the future," he said.

stories.title: Rewa BJP leader attacked in Prayagraj:Car windows smashed, party flag torn off; complaint filed against Congress and SP
stories.summary: Former Rewa BJP Kisan Morcha district president Prashant Pathak was attacked in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. Pathak says that supporters of the Jantar-Mantar movement surrounded him after seeing a BJP flag on his car. Shouting 'He's from BJP, beat him', those people pounced on Pathak's car. They broke the car's windows and removed and threw away the party flag. According to Pathak, the mob tried to break the car door and pull him out. After struggling for about an hour, the driver was able to get the car away from the spot. The incident took place at Subhash Chowraha in Prayagraj on Saturday. A video of this has also surfaced. Prashant Pathak, a resident of Chaakghat in Rewa, has filed a complaint about the case at Civil Lines police station in Prayagraj. He has held Congress and Samajwadi Party responsible for the attack. Local police have started an investigation. See two pictures of the attack... BJP leader said- I have returned after touching death Pathak said, ''I had gone to Prayagraj for treatment. While returning, some youths protesting at Subhash Chowk stopped our vehicle. They surrounded the vehicle and started vandalizing it. They were intent on assaulting us. The attack was carried out at the behest of Congress and Samajwadi Party leaders. I have returned after touching death.'' Congress leader said - BJP itself is reason for attack Congress has denied Pathak's allegations. Rewa District Congress president Bijendra Gupta said, "If someone has committed wrongdoing, why would anyone garland them? Neither the Congress nor the Samajwadi Party carried out the attack. This is the anger of frustrated and disappointed students, for which the BJP itself is responsible."

stories.title: 'He ruined everything':Yogi targets Akhilesh in SP stronghold; says 'they have a problem with saffron'; praises Mulayam
stories.summary: Speaking in Mainpuri, an SP stronghold, on Sunday, CM Yogi said, "The Samajwadi Party earlier used to say it would not allow the Kanwar Yatra, claiming that if Shiva devotees took out the procession, riots would break out. They wouldn't allow conch shells to be blown or temple bells to ring. The Samajwadi Party appears to have an inherent hostility towards saffron attire." CM Yogi further said- Earlier there used to be an atmosphere of restrictions and tension during religious events. But now all festivals like Kanwar Yatra, Ram Navami, Janmashtami, Durga Puja, Diwali and Holi are celebrated in a peaceful atmosphere. Now there is no curfew, no riots... everything is fine in UP. Yogi said, ''After the BJP government came, only two places remain for criminals in the state - jail or hell. There is no third place for them. The work of crushing the mafia into dust will continue. If any criminal becomes a threat to the safety of daughters and businessmen, he too will be crushed into dust.'' Yogi reached Etawah after Mainpuri. Here too, he attacked the SP chief, but praised former Chief Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav. He said, ''He worked staying connected to the ground, but later dynasticism and the Saifai Syndicate destroyed everything.'' Earlier, Yogi laid the foundation stone and inaugurated 111 development projects worth ₹682 crore in Mainpuri and ₹604 crore in Etawah. He also planted saplings and visited an exhibition. 6 major points from Yogi's address 1. 'Earlier, people wouldn't even give a room after hearing the name Mainpuri' CM Yogi said that once Mainpuri's identity had become associated with crime and lawlessness. Youth from here would not get rooms in hotels in other cities. They were refused accommodation in dharamshalas and faced difficulties in renting houses. But now, under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the efforts of the BJP government, Mainpuri has created a new identity along with its mythological, cultural and historical heritage. Now, when a young person introduces himself as being from Mainpuri, he receives respect. 2. 'Previous governments made the state BIMARU' Yogi, targeting the Samajwadi Party, said that previous governments had made Uttar Pradesh a BIMARU state. In jobs, merit was not considered, but rather face and money were looked at. Poor and honest youth did not get opportunities. Today, in the BJP government, youth are getting jobs through a transparent recruitment process without any recommendation or bribery. More than 9 lakh youth have been given government jobs in the state so far. 3. 'Poor, farmers, women and youth are Govt's priority' The Chief Minister said that the government is running schemes keeping the poor, farmers, women and youth at the center. Under the 'Chief Minister Bal Seva Yojana', orphan children are being provided financial assistance, laptops and education facilities. For farmers, schemes like crop loan waiver, 'Prime Minister Kisan Samman Nidhi', 'Chief Minister Krishak Durghatna Bima Yojana' and relief in electricity bills for private tubewells are being run. The benefits of these schemes are being delivered to every eligible person without any discrimination based on caste or religion. 4. 'Artisans got global platform' Yogi said that through the 'One District-One Product' (ODOP) scheme, artisans of the state have received a new identity. The products of Mainpuri have also been given recognition in national and international markets. The government's objective is to provide work to every hand and dignity to every family. 5. 'Developed Mainpuri necessary for developed UP' CM Yogi said that UP is rapidly moving forward towards joining the country's leading economies. In such a situation, developed Mainpuri is also necessary for developed UP. He assured that the government will work on a priority basis on all proposals related to the development of Mainpuri and Karhal. There will be no shortage of funds for roads, stadiums, museums, irrigation, electricity and other basic facilities. 6. Yogi said- Mulayam did politics by staying connected to the ground Chief Minister Yogi mentioned late SP leader Mulayam Singh Yadav in Etawah. He said that Mulayam did politics by staying connected to the ground and tried to work, but later the entire system got trapped in the syndicate of nepotism and dynasty politics. He alleged that when jobs were released, the syndicate would take over. Poor and deserving youth did not get opportunities. In the name of development, only loot happened, and the state became a BIMARU state.

stories.title: UP's IPS transfer list remains pending:Decision yet to be finalised on DG of Fire Services Lucknow Police Commissioner
stories.summary: The long-awaited transfer list of IPS officers in Uttar Pradesh remains pending, with no official announcement yet. The proposed reshuffle is expected to include several senior officers holding the ranks of Director General (DG), Inspector General (IG) and Deputy Inspector General (DIG). Promotions and key postings remain on hold The delay has also affected the posting of 28 officers recently inducted into the IPS from the Provincial Police Service (PPS), all of whom are currently serving as Additional Superintendents of Police (Additional SPs). In addition, three officers promoted to the rank of Director General are awaiting fresh assignments. According to sources, the transfer list has been held up because a final decision is yet to be taken on appointments to key positions, including the Police Commissioners of the Fire Service, Lucknow and Noida. DG post vacant in Vigilance-Fire Service There are a total of 7 cadre posts of DG rank in UP. These include DGP, CID, Vigilance, UP Police Recruitment and Promotion Board, Training Directorate, Home Guard and Fire Service. At this time, the posts of DG in both Vigilance and Fire Service are vacant. DGP Rajeev Krishna has the additional charge of Vigilance. Meanwhile, the DG's chair in Fire Service has been lying vacant since 1994 batch IPS Sujit Pandey went on central deputation. 3 officers became DG, but are working at ADG posts Three officers who have recently been promoted to the rank of Director General (DG) are yet to receive postings matching their new rank and continue to serve in Additional Director General (ADG)-level positions. They include ADG, Government Railway Police (GRP), Prakash D, ADG, Gorakhpur Zone, Ashok Mutha Jain, and Lucknow Police Commissioner Amarendra Sengar. With Ashok Mutha Jain set to retire on August 31, sources said Prakash D and Amarendra Sengar are among the leading contenders for the DG, Fire Services post. CID Director General B.K. Singh is also being considered, although he currently holds multiple key responsibilities, including the CID, Cyber Crime and UP-112. 3 names in race for new Police Commissioner of Lucknow The race for the post of Lucknow Police Commissioner is also gathering pace, with several senior IPS officers under consideration. According to sources, the frontrunners include ADG, Varanasi Zone, Piyush Mordia, ADG, Lucknow Zone, Praveen Kumar, and ADG, Crime and Traffic, A. Satish Ganesh. Varanasi Police Commissioner Mohit Agarwal is also among the names being discussed for the high-profile posting. Transfer of Noida CP Laxmi Singh almost certain Gautam Buddh Nagar (Noida) is also expected to get a new Police Commissioner ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Incumbent Police Commissioner Laxmi Singh has been serving in the post since November 2022, making her one of the senior officers likely to be affected by the upcoming administrative reshuffle. Election norms make transfer almost certain According to Election Commission guidelines, District Magistrates and police chiefs who have been posted in the same district since the previous assembly elections or have completed more than three years at the same station are generally transferred before polls to ensure administrative neutrality. With Laxmi Singh set to complete the prescribed tenure, sources indicate that her transfer is being viewed as almost certain as part of the pre-election administrative exercise. 28 new IPS officers will also get new responsibilities Twenty-eight Uttar Pradesh Police Service (PPS) officers who were recently promoted to the Indian Police Service (IPS) are awaiting fresh assignments, with many expected to receive charge of a district for the first time. At present, all of them are serving as Additional Superintendents of Police (Additional SPs) across key units, including the Police Headquarters, ATS, Vigilance, CID, SSF, SDRF, Kanpur Police Commissionerate, and districts such as Barabanki, Hardoi, Etawah, Ambedkar Nagar, Azamgarh, Mathura and Gorakhpur. DG promotions and key appointments delaying reshuffle The upcoming transfer list is also expected to include postings for officers recently promoted to the rank of Director General (DG). However, the reshuffle remains pending as the government is yet to take final decisions on several high-profile appointments, including leadership positions in the Fire Services and the Police Commissionerates of Lucknow and Noida.

stories.title: Husband returns alive three days after 'his funeral':Left home after a quarrel with wife, mystery solved by anonymous call
stories.summary: In Auraiya, UP, the young man whose family and relatives had performed his last rites three days ago, suddenly returned home safe and sound. Seeing him alive in front of them, his family members were stunned. The incident is from Saidpur village in the Ajitmal Kotwali area. A year and a half ago, after a quarrel with his wife, a man left home. Despite extensive searching, no trace was found, so the family filed a missing person's report. Three days ago, the police found a decomposed body. Upon receiving information, his brother identified the body based on clothes and physique. After this, the police handed over the body to the family. The family also performed his last rites. The story took a turn when the wife called back one of the unknown numbers that had called her mobile a long time ago. The voice on the other end was that of her missing husband, Kamal. When the wife told him about the last rites, Kamal returned home at 10 PM on Saturday night. Now the police are in a dilemma. They are trying to find out who the young man was whose body was found in the ruins and cremated, and how he died. Body was found in the ruins Know the full story Sunita told the police that she was married to Kamal Singh (40) 14 years ago. Kamal supported the family by working as a labourer. They have three children. About a year and a half ago, Kamal sold his field after taking money from his nephew. A dispute arose between them over this matter. In anger, Sunita spoke ill of Kamal. His wife had scolded him, saying, "Don't show your face until you arrange 2 lakh rupees." Hurt by this, he left home. Due to financial hardship, Sunita herself took on the responsibility of the family. She started raising her three children by doing small jobs. When she got a job in a private factory in Noida, she went there on June 27. On Wednesday, July 22, Kamal's wife Sunita received a call on her mobile from her brother-in-law Dashrath from the village. Her brother-in-law informed her that Kamal's body had been found. Sunita left Noida for the village, but her family members had already performed the last rites before she arrived. Missed calls found in old mobile Sunita said that after her husband's last rites, when she checked her old mobile phone kept at home, she found many missed calls from unknown numbers. She called back those numbers. Hearing the voice of the person who received the call on a number from Etawah, she understood that it was Kamal on the other end. However, he tried to hide his identity. Sunita tearfully appealed to Kamal to return home. She told him that the family considered him dead and the police were continuously investigating his death. After hearing this, Kamal returned home on Saturday night around 10 PM. Seeing him alive, his family and villagers were astonished. Kamal said called many times, but the number was blocked Kamal said that after a dispute with his wife, he first went to Panipat, where he worked in a poultry farm for several months. Later, he became a helper with a truck driver. On June 25, after getting off the truck at Bhikhepur, he reached his in-laws' house in Baglan, but without stopping there, he went to Gwalior and started working as a plumber. Kamal said that during work, he fell from a ladder and broke his leg. During treatment, he called his wife many times, but her number was blocked. On Saturday, when his wife called, he came to know that the family had considered him dead and performed his last rites. Now, identifying the unknown body is a challenge for the police CO Ajitmal Manoj Gangwar said- Based on the identification by the family, the police had handed over the body to them. On Saturday night, information was received that Kamal is alive. Written confirmation has been taken from the family. Now an investigation is being conducted to determine whose unknown body was cremated and how he died. Further action will be taken based on the investigation.

stories.title: 6-year-old drowns in water-filled pit in Greater Noida:Authority’s alleged negligence claims boy’s life, six months after techie’s death
stories.summary: A six-year-old boy drowned in an open, water-filled pit in Greater Noida, allegedly due to negligence by the Greater Noida Development Authority. The pit, reportedly dug by the authority for boring work, was around 15 feet deep and had filled with rainwater. Despite being located inside a residential colony, it had not been barricaded, raising serious questions over safety measures. The incident comes six months after Noida techie Yuvraj Mehta was killed in a similar accident after falling into an open pit while returning home from work. The latest tragedy has once again raised questions over whether the Greater Noida Authority’s assurances on safety have remained confined to paper. According to police, the boy, Avyaan, was playing cricket in the colony on Saturday evening. While playing, he went near the pit and slipped into it because of the mud surrounding the area. The children playing with him raised an alarm, following which nearby residents rushed to the spot and pulled him out. He was taken to a hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Avyaan’s parents were devastated after seeing their son’s body. His father, Shivan Yadav, a vice-principal at a Kendriya Vidyalaya, repeatedly questioned why his family had to suffer because of someone else’s negligence. The incident occurred at Kaladham Society in the Knowledge Park-2 area of Greater Noida. FIR filed against contractor and supervisors The Greater Noida Authority has registered an FIR against contractor Manoj Jain, supervisor Johnny and technical supervisor Akash. Their services have been terminated, while the contractor has been arrested. Authorities have now barricaded the pit and installed warning signs around it. 3 pictures of the accident Boy had gone to play near park with friends Pranjal, a resident of Kaladham Society, said the Yadav family lives opposite his house. He said he was washing his car around 6:30 pm when a child ran towards him and told him that his friend had fallen into a pit while they were playing and picking up pieces of wood. Pranjal said he followed the child to the spot along with two other people. Residents used pipe to rescue the child When they reached the pit, they found the child’s shoe nearby. Pranjal said he lowered a large pipe into the pit and held it in place while two people descended into the water using the pipe. They found the child within five to 10 minutes and pulled him out. His family was informed and he was immediately taken to hospital. Doctors tried to save him but could not revive him. SDM reaches spot to assess situation Greater Noida SDM Ashutosh Gupta visited the site after receiving information about the drowning through social media. He spoke to the child’s family and residents present at the location to understand what had happened. Father: ‘My child is gone; what had he done wrong?’ Avyaan’s father, Shivan, said he had returned home in the evening and had barely sat down when residents informed him about the incident. “It is painful that despite living in a good society, we are having to suffer because of the authority’s negligence. What mistake did we make? My child is gone. What had he done to anyone?” he said. He alleged that the large pit had neither been barricaded nor marked with a warning sign. “My child drowned in that mud and water. We do not know when or how it happened. He got no chance to save himself, and nobody got a chance to save him. He was only six years old — what was his fault?” Shivan said. Authority: ‘Serious negligence found’ AK Singh, General Manager of the Noida Authority project, said serious negligence had been found in the case. “After the pit was dug, it was not barricaded. The rules clearly require any pit dug for such work to be barricaded from all sides beforehand,” he said. An FIR for culpable homicide has been registered against the contractor, supervisor and technical supervisor, Singh added.

stories.title: Building where 15 died reduced to rubble in Lucknow:No trace remains; debris clearance underway as LDA team deployed
stories.summary: The four-storey building in Lucknow’s Aliganj where 15 people were killed in a fire has been demolished 32 days after the tragedy. The structure has now been completely razed, leaving no visible trace of the building at the site. The demolition took 15 hours and 30 minutes. On Saturday at 7 am, a team of 45 officials and employees from the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) arrived at the site with three bulldozers and a hydraulic machine. The surrounding roads were closed with barricades, while more than 100 police personnel were deployed to maintain security. Demolition work then began. As darkness fell, lighting arrangements were made to continue the operation. By 10:30 pm, the building had been completely demolished. On Sunday morning, the LDA began removing the debris from the site. Its team, along with heavy machinery, remains deployed at the location. See 5 pictures Building owner says demolition will be challenged in court During the demolition operation on Saturday morning, advocate Rajendra Shukla, representing building owner Virendra Shukla, reached the spot. He alleged that the LDA had given the owner time until July 25, yet officials arrived to demolish the building on the same day. The lawyer claimed that the owner had not received a separate demolition order and that the action was being taken only on the basis of a notice. He said the demolition would be challenged in court. 15 killed in fire at animation coaching centre The building caught fire on June 22. Fifteen people died in the blaze at an animation coaching centre on the second floor. Five others managed to escape by climbing down using pipes and wires. During the fire, one young man jumped from the second floor and suffered paralysis in his leg. LDA found building was being used illegally Following the tragedy, the LDA conducted an inspection and found that the building was allegedly illegal. According to the authority, a residential building had been converted for commercial use. The LDA subsequently issued the owner a notice regarding the alleged illegal construction and sought a response within 15 days. On July 10, the authority issued a demolition order and directed the owner to demolish the building himself within 15 days. The deadline expired on Friday. After this, the LDA began the demolition itself using bulldozers.

stories.title: Sambhal violence accused joins Owaisi’s AIMIM:Leader says, ‘Will contest election if party asks; will raise Muslims’ voice as long as I live’
stories.summary: Advocate Zafar Ali, one of the main accused in the Sambhal violence case, has joined Asaduddin Owaisi’s All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM). Zafar, who is the president of Sambhal’s Shahi Jama Masjid, joined the party in Moradabad on Saturday night in the presence of AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi. After joining the party, Zafar said he would not “betray his community” and would continue to raise his voice for Muslims. “I will not betray my community. Every drop of my blood is dedicated to Islam. I will continue to raise my voice for Muslims. All the allegations against me are baseless. I have already received a stay from the High Court, and the case will soon be quashed,” Zafar said. ‘If the party asks me to contest, I will’ Zafar said he had earlier spoken about contesting an election but was not associated with any political party at the time. “I had earlier spoken about contesting an election, but at that time I did not have a party and was not a political person. Now, at the demand of the people, I have joined AIMIM. If the party asks me to contest an election, I will. I will do whatever our barrister Asaduddin sahib directs. Otherwise, I will serve AIMIM as a soldier,” he said. Owaisi praises Zafar: ‘He chose jail over compromise with the oppressor’ After handing over the party membership to Zafar, Owaisi praised him and said he had come from Sambhal. “Zafar came from Sambhal. He chose to go to jail to protect the house of Allah rather than compromise with the oppressor,” Owaisi said. A day earlier, on Friday, Zafar had shared the stage in Moradabad with AIMIM Uttar Pradesh president Shaukat Ali. AIMIM entry could split Muslim votes in Sambhal Political analysts say Samajwadi Party MLA Iqbal Mahmood’s son Suhail Iqbal has already announced his intention to contest the election. If AIMIM fields Zafar Ali from Sambhal, analysts believe the Muslim vote could be divided between the two candidates, potentially turning the contest into a triangular fight. Local residents say Zafar could receive support on both religious and local grounds if he enters the electoral fray. However, the cases against him could make the political battle more difficult. What happened during the Sambhal violence? The dispute began on November 19, 2024, when a Hindu petition was filed in the Civil Judge (Senior Division) court in Chandausi, claiming that Sambhal’s Shahi Jama Masjid was built at the site of a Shri Harihar temple. Following the court’s order, the first survey of the mosque premises was conducted the same evening. The second phase of the survey began on November 24. A large crowd gathered at the site, and tensions escalated during the survey before violence broke out. According to police, stones were pelted and shots were fired during the violence. Five people were killed, while then Superintendent of Police Krishna Kumar Bishnoi, ASP Anuj Chaudhary, a deputy collector and 29 police personnel were injured. 12 FIRs, cases against over 2,750 people A total of 12 FIRs were registered at Sambhal Kotwali and Nakhasa police stations. Several people were named in the cases, including SP MP Ziaur Rahman Barq and Suhail Iqbal, the son of SP MLA Iqbal Mahmood. Police registered cases against more than 2,750 people. However, Suhail Iqbal’s name was later removed from the chargesheet on the basis of the evidence collected during the investigation. On March 23, 2025, police sent 158 accused, including Zafar Ali, to jail. The accused included three women and three associates of absconding gangster Sharik Satha — Mulla Afroz, Waris and Ghulam. The National Security Act (NSA) was subsequently invoked against Mulla Afroz in October 2025. Similar NSA action was also taken against Waris and Ghulam. Zafar was released after 131 days in jail Zafar was released on bail from Moradabad jail on August 1, 2025, after spending 131 days behind bars. His release was marked by a grand welcome by supporters. As soon as he stepped outside the jail, supporters raised slogans in his favour, garlanded him and carried him on their shoulders to his car. Zafar then travelled in an open jeep as part of a convoy of around 10 vehicles. A 42-km-long roadshow was held from Moradabad to Sambhal. More than 3,000 people reportedly gathered in Sambhal after news of his arrival spread. As soon as he stepped out of the jeep, supporters lifted him onto their shoulders. At the time, Zafar had said, “If you want to protect something, it is very important to have power in your hands. If I had power in my hands, I would not have gone to jail.”

stories.title: Have Samajwadi Party's doors closed for Rajbhar?:49 attacks on Akhilesh in 55 days; How Jayant and Anupriya are playing it smart
stories.summary: The BJP positioned Om Prakash Rajbhar as a prominent NDA face in Uttar Pradesh in response to the Samajwadi Party’s PDA (Backward Classes, Dalits and Minorities) strategy. Behind this move, however, appears to be a carefully planned political strategy. Over the past two months, Rajbhar has repeatedly launched personal attacks on Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. At times, he even claimed that the entire SP would split. On another occasion, he questioned whether Akhilesh was genuinely a Yadav. Political circles are now discussing whether Rajbhar’s relationship with Akhilesh has weakened compared with the past. The implications are significant: if the BJP refuses to meet Rajbhar’s demands for seats ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election, he may find it difficult to leave the NDA and pursue an alternative alliance. But is the BJP’s strategy limited to Om Prakash Rajbhar? Or have other NDA allies also lost their bargaining power when it comes to seat-sharing? Let's find out in today's Sunday Big Story Regional parties judged by vote base and political options Regional parties are generally considered strong on two parameters: the strength of their electoral base and their ability to maintain political links with both ruling and opposition parties. At present, the BJP’s key allies in Uttar Pradesh include the Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP), Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD), Nishad Party and Apna Dal (Sonelal). With the 2027 Assembly election approaching, all these parties want to field candidates on their own symbols. The BJP’s core committee, meanwhile, is focusing on winning combinations and suitable candidates across all 403 Assembly constituencies. This has led to allies putting forward their respective claims for seats. Here is how their bargaining positions compare: 1. SBSP: Rajbhar has switched sides before, but this time it may be difficult Om Prakash Rajbhar contested the 2022 Assembly election in alliance with the Samajwadi Party. The SBSP fielded candidates on 16 seats and won six. After the BJP formed the government in Uttar Pradesh, Rajbhar switched sides and joined the ruling alliance. Ahead of the 2027 election, he is now projecting his party as a contender for as many as 63 seats. The BJP, however, is unlikely to agree to such a large demand. Political analyst Ratan Mani Lal says Rajbhar has a history of quickly breaking alliances. According to him, if the SP option had remained open to Rajbhar, he could have threatened to walk out of the BJP alliance during negotiations over ticket distribution. However, by encouraging Rajbhar to make personal attacks against Akhilesh, the BJP has largely closed the route for him to return to the SP. This leaves Rajbhar with little choice but to contest the election on the BJP’s terms, he argues. 2. Nishad Party: BJP has already reduced its bargaining power through bypolls Among the NDA allies in Uttar Pradesh, Sanjay Nishad’s party appears to have the least room for political bargaining. In the 2022 Assembly election, the Nishad Party received 16 seats — 10 on its own symbol and six on the BJP symbol. It won six of these seats. After Nishad Party MLAs Lalji Verma and Dr Vinod Kumar Bind became MPs, the Katehari and Majhawan Assembly seats fell vacant. In the subsequent by-elections, the BJP contested both seats with its own candidates and won them, effectively taking the constituencies away from the Nishad Party. Sanjay Nishad’s son Praveen Nishad has also lost the Sant Kabir Nagar Lok Sabha election. His current priority is reportedly to establish his sons Praveen, Sarvan and Amit in politics. His repeated anti-SP statements have also limited his options, leaving the BJP as his principal political ally. 3. RLD: Jayant Chaudhary is playing it safe and keeping his options open Among the BJP’s allies, the Rashtriya Lok Dal appears to be in the strongest bargaining position. The party has a significant hold over the Jat vote base in western Uttar Pradesh. After former Prime Minister Chaudhary Charan Singh was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2024, Jayant Chaudhary joined the NDA and subsequently became a Union minister. The RLD is seeking more than 30 seats in the 2027 Assembly election, including its nine existing seats. Sources indicate that the BJP could offer the party around 20 seats. Jayant, however, appears to be taking a long-term political view and does not want to shut the door on possible opposition alliances in the future. This is why he has largely avoided direct attacks on either Akhilesh Yadav or Mayawati. By keeping his political options open, Jayant has retained greater bargaining power within the NDA. 4. Apna Dal (Sonelal): Strong Kurmi base, avoids controversial statements Anupriya Patel’s Apna Dal (Sonelal) is considered one of the BJP’s most reliable and politically strong allies in Uttar Pradesh. Its key strength is its support among the Kurmi community. Anupriya has remained allied with the BJP continuously since 2014. The party won nine Assembly seats in 2017 and 12 in 2022. Anupriya Patel and Ashish Patel have generally avoided controversial statements against the SP, Congress or BSP. For the 2027 election, the party is preparing to seek more than 20 seats. With 13 seats currently under its control, it is reportedly hoping for another six to seven constituencies. By staying away from personal attacks and controversial remarks, the party has managed to keep its political options open. Experts: Final political equations could change everything Experts believe the BJP may have strategically cornered the SBSP and Nishad Party by encouraging aggressive political rhetoric against the opposition. However, this could only be one side of the story. Rajbhar’s political career itself suggests that equations can change at the last moment. A recurring pattern in his politics has been that leaders or parties he criticises eventually become politically important to him. The 2022 Assembly election is a clear example. Rajbhar shared the stage with Akhilesh Yadav and even made strong and sometimes objectionable remarks against BJP leaders. Yet, after the election, he successfully returned to an alliance with the BJP. Therefore, while the BJP may currently appear to have strengthened its position in negotiations with some allies, the final seat-sharing formula for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election could still be shaped by changing political equations closer to polling.

stories.title: 'Dasharath had 3 wives, why can’t we have one husband?':3 sisters marry the same friend in UP's Amroha; Is this legally valid?
stories.summary: The marriage of three sisters from Amroha to the same man has sparked widespread debate. When the video surfaced, many called it a publicity stunt. The girls responded, saying people would gradually come to believe the marriage is genuine. Hindu organisations have protested and demanded police action, to which the sisters replied: “If Lord Dasharath could have three wives, why can't we marry one man? If we're separated, we'll take our own lives.” So why did three sisters marry the same man? Is it love, or a bid to trend on social media? What does the Hindu Marriage Act say about this? Here's a full breakdown. What happened On 17 July, three sisters — Alka, Devika, and Santosh — from a village in Amroha, married a man named Vikas at a temple. Alka and Santosh are biological sisters, while Devika is their maternal aunt's daughter, who has been raised alongside them since childhood. The trio run comedy videos on social media under the name "Rajput Girls" across Instagram, Facebook, and YouTube. They have 5 lakh followers on Instagram and 91,000 on Facebook, with their videos garnering millions of views. Question 1: Why did three sisters marry the same man? Each sister offers her own reasoning. Alka says the sisters share deep love for one another and cannot bear to live apart. They wanted to be married into the same household and searched extensively for a family with three brothers, but couldn't find one. Devika explains that their father had found a groom—a government employee—for elder sister Alka. To avoid being separated, the three decided to marry the same man instead, so they could continue living together. She insists this was a well-considered decision. The youngest, Santosh, denies the marriage was for views, noting their videos already performed well before this. She says they'll continue making content, but insists the marriage isn't a joke. Alka added that whether or not Vikas loves them doesn't matter—what matters is that the three sisters remain together. She says their bond is greater than anything else in the world, and even if their husband leaves them one day, their sisterhood won't break. She credited Vikas with saving them from taking their own lives. Vikas himself says the sisters didn't want to be separated and were prepared to die rather than be apart, which is why he married them. He describes himself merely as a means for the three to stay together, adding that they don't need his love—only each other's. Question 2: Is this marriage socially and legally valid? There's often a wide gap between social custom and law. Several legally questionable practices continue in parts of India even today. For instance, the Hatti community (a Scheduled Tribe) in Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand practises polyandry, where one woman marries multiple brothers—a similar case made headlines last year. In several villages in Maharashtra's Thane district, men take two or three wives specifically so the additional wives can fetch water from miles away—a practice that has earned them the term "water wives." Turning to the legal complexities of the Amroha case: 1. A joint marriage instead of separate ones The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, mandates monogamy. Under Section 5, a second marriage is valid only if the first spouse has died or the couple has divorced. Section 11 declares any marriage conducted while a spouse is alive and undivorced as "void." Such an act is punishable under Section 82 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, carrying a sentence of 7 to 10 years. However, these provisions typically apply when second or third marriages occur on separate occasions. Here, all three sisters claim to have married in a single ceremony simultaneously—a scenario that complicates legal interpretation considerably. 2. The youngest sister's alleged minor status Based on her Class 10 mark sheet, the youngest bride Santosh's age is reported to be 15. The Child Welfare Committee (CWC) has sought a police report within three days. This would bring the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 (PCMA) into play. Under Section 9, marrying a minor girl can result in a three-month sentence. Eldest sister Alka claims Santosh is actually an adult and that a medical test will prove it. However, under Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, a Class 10 mark sheet or birth certificate is treated as the most reliable evidence of age in all POCSO and child welfare cases—taking precedence over medical tests, even if the Supreme Court (in cases like Jarnail Singh vs State of Haryana) has ruled documentary evidence should prevail when available. Notably, child marriage under the PCMA isn't automatically void. If the minor party wishes, they can have the marriage annulled through court once they turn 18—but until then, the marriage remains legally standing, even as criminal liability applies immediately. 3. Doubts over whether the marriage actually took place Questions have also been raised about the marriage's validity, since no priest appears in the wedding video. However, Section 7 of the Hindu Marriage Act clarifies that a priest's presence isn't mandatory for a valid marriage—but customary rituals must be properly performed. In 2024, the Supreme Court ruled in Dolly Rani vs Manish Kumar Chanchal that a Hindu marriage cannot be validated merely through paperwork, photos, videos, or a simple claim of marriage. Rituals such as "saptapadi" (the seven sacred steps) and "kanyadaan" must be duly performed. Without them, even a marriage certificate wouldn't render a marriage legally valid. The video does show rituals resembling saptapadi and sindoor application. Still, if investigation reveals proper customs weren't followed, the marriage could be denied legal recognition entirely—rendering any prosecution moot. 4. Where police and family stand No formal complaint has been filed so far. However, police are investigating on the CWC's directive. Hasanpur police station in-charge Rajesh Tiwari questioned all three sisters and their husband on 23 July, during which they stated the decision was entirely their own. According to media reports, the family says they don't want any legal action, and the sisters maintain their families are happy with the arrangement—though no family member has publicly come forward yet. Question 3: What happens next? With several facts still unclear—particularly the claims around the minor's age and the marriage's authenticity—multiple legal and social scenarios could unfold. Legal possibilities 1. If the minor's age is confirmed: Police could act on their own accord, treating Santosh's Class 10 mark sheet as primary evidence. This would escalate the matter into serious child marriage and POCSO charges. The CWC could take the minor into its custody immediately, regardless of her objections, since a minor's consent holds no legal weight. This is considered the most likely outcome. 2. If all three sisters are proven to be adults: This would require a lengthy legal process, with a medical test only possible on court orders. Even then, the court would decide whether to accept the report if Santosh's age comes back as 18 or older. If the court accepts the medical report establishing her adulthood, the criminal case would weaken considerably. Additionally, multiple marriage charges typically only proceed if the first wife or family files a complaint—and since the family has declined to pursue legal action and the sisters married consensually, police may find no strong legal ground to act. 3. If a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) is filed: Several Hindu organisations are questioning the marriage. Should they file a PIL—particularly around the minor's age—the Allahabad High Court, which has taken suo motu cognisance in similar cases before, could intervene. Social possibilities Family pressure: While the family currently opposes any action, community or village pressure could shift their stance, potentially leading to a formal complaint. Pressure from religious organisations: Protesting Hindu groups could pressure authorities into pursuing a formal investigation, even without a private complaint. The influencer angle: Vikas has reportedly played the role of "husband" in the sisters' video content for around six months, leading many to suspect this is a social media stunt. If proven true, the entire matter could collapse on itself.

stories.title: Owaisi says, 'We won't sit on floor mats anymore':If Akhilesh sits on chair, I'll sit opposite him with my legs crossed; govt bows to student protest
stories.summary: In Moradabad, AIMIM Chief Asaduddin Owaisi, commenting on the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, said- This is a big victory for the struggle, efforts, and sacrifice of the country's youth. The government had to bow before the students. Time will tell that we will be victorious. He said, I salute those students who, by sitting at Jantar Mantar for several weeks, chanted such a mantra that Modi had to make a video at 12 midnight. Dictatorship will not work in the country. Even power has to bow before an organized voice. It is hoped that in the future, no national or state-level competitive examination papers will be leaked. He said- Now we don't want to sit on mats on the floor. Now we want equality. If there is a chair, and Akhilesh sits, then Owaisi will sit cross-legged in front of that chair. Then he will talk about rights and justice. Owaisi said, "I have said it before and I am saying it today that Majlis does not want the BJP government to be formed again. I am ready to shake hands, I am ready to ally. Now is the time, let's talk. Don't cry after the elections are over." Owaisi made these remarks at a rally at Jama Masjid Ground at 11 pm on Saturday. The role of youth should increase in future politics Owaisi said that a large population of the country is young. The role of youth should increase in future politics. The objective of the AIMIM party is not just to give emotional speeches, but to raise the voice of the public based on issues. Owaisi said- Now when election season comes, someone will come and say that so-and-so has to be made Chief Minister, we are coming to power. Four times you made a mistake, you did not create your own leadership. How many SP workers came out on the streets for Azam? He said- I want to ask, after Azam Khan was put in jail and sentenced, how many SP people came out on the road and protested? Tell us, no one will be able to answer. Atiq was shot dead in police custody, there was no protest. How many such things can I put before you? Jauhar University demolition is part of a plan Owaisi said- Today you are seeing that there is a BJP government in Uttar Pradesh. It is trying its best to ensure that children and daughters of the Muslim minority are not educated. That is why a notice has been given to demolish Jauhar University. Akhilesh is giving false statements to gain votes Owaisi said- We saw that Samajwadi Party leader Akhilesh wrote on social media that all those buildings of Jauhar University can be regularized. He cited the law that under the Uttar Pradesh Urban Development Act of 1973, Jauhar University can be regularized. He said- Why did Akhilesh not regularize Jauhar University while he was the Chief Minister until 2017, when he had every opportunity to use the 1973 law? When they were in power, they did not save the university. Now, with elections approaching, they are giving false statements just to gain votes. BJP-RSS does not want Indian Muslims to become powerful When the lights went out, supporters lit up their mobile torches and chanted slogans The power went out for a short while during Owaisi's program. He also took a dig at the government over this. Supporters chanted slogans by lighting their mobile torches. Owaisi said - The Muslims of the state now have a big political alternative. The AIMIM party will perform better in the upcoming assembly elections. In the coming time, the voice of AIMIM will also be heard in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly. Owaisi said - I hope that 65% of our population in India is under 35 years of age. 50% of India's population is under 25 years of age. Our effort will also be that AIMIM should field young candidates in the upcoming UP assembly elections, so that they can represent fearlessly. Our effort will be that when the 2029 elections are held, no 80-year-old person will become the Prime Minister of India, but a young person of 40-45 years will become the Prime Minister of this country.

stories.title: School swept into river in UP:Rivers in spate after heavy rain; water enters medical college, alert in 25 districts
stories.summary: Heavy rainfall in the hills has caused several rivers in Uttar Pradesh to swell, with water levels in 10 rivers, including the Ganga and Yamuna, rising rapidly. Four rivers, including the Ghaghra and Sharda, have already crossed the danger mark. A government school and a house in Ballia were swept away by the Saryu River. In Gonda, more than 100 bighas of crops have been submerged by the rising Ghaghra. Residents living along the riverbanks have begun dismantling their makeshift houses and salvaging bamboo poles, wooden supports and bricks. The rising water levels of the Saryu and Ghaghra have created flood-like conditions in villages across Sitapur, Pilibhit, Lakhimpur and Bahraich. Crocodiles carried downstream by the floodwaters have also reportedly entered residential areas. Rain alert issued for 25 districts Most cities, including Lucknow, Barabanki and Agra, have had clear weather since Sunday morning, although clouds continue to pass amid sunny conditions. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for 25 districts for Sunday. Eight districts, including Varanasi and Prayagraj, are also at risk of lightning. On Saturday, 20 cities, including Varanasi, Prayagraj, Kanpur and Meerut, received rainfall. Several streets in Kanpur were waterlogged, while water entered a medical college in Meerut. Patients were seen walking through knee-deep water outside the OPD entrance. In Greater Noida, a six-year-old boy died after drowning in a water-filled pit. Rain activity to increase from July 27 Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said rainfall activity in Uttar Pradesh had temporarily weakened as winds shifted towards Rajasthan and central India. He said a low-pressure area was developing near the Bay of Bengal and Bangladesh, which would help monsoon winds return towards Uttar Pradesh. According to Singh, monsoon activity will remain subdued on Sunday, with light rain expected over limited areas. However, the spread of rainfall is likely to increase from July 27, when monsoon activity is expected to intensify across the state.

stories.title: UP sharpshooter killed in encounter over extortion:Demanded legal expenses from man whose brother he murdered
stories.summary: Meerut STF (Special Task Force) and Bagpat police shot down a criminal with a bounty of ₹50K, Vipul alias Khooni, in an encounter on Saturday. He was out on bail and was demanding extortion money. This encounter took place at 6 PM in the Singhawali Ahir area. About 12 rounds of firing occurred between the police and Vipul Khooni. During this, he was hit by four bullets and fell down. He was immediately taken to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead. According to police, there was a bounty of ₹50K on Vipul. He was an active member of the notorious Sushil Moonchh gang. A total of 36 cases were registered against him under several serious sections, including robbery, murder, and the Gangster Act. He had been absconding for a long time, and a reward of ₹50K was announced for him. Police have recovered two pistols, one motorcycle, and several empty cartridges from the encounter site. Police are conducting a thorough investigation of the entire incident and are engaged in searching for other people connected to the criminal's network. Police officials stated that the campaign against criminals in the area will continue unabated. Fired at police when he saw himself surrounded Police and STF received information that Vipul was present near the Irrigation Department bungalow in Ahir village. After this, the team cordoned off the area. According to police, seeing himself surrounded, Vipul started firing at the police team. 12 rounds of bullets were fired In retaliatory action, about 12 rounds of bullets were fired from both sides. During this, Vipul was seriously injured. Police first took him to Pilana CHC, from where he was referred to the district hospital considering his critical condition. During treatment at the district hospital, doctors declared him dead. Bagpat SP Suraj Kumar Rai informed that Vipul alias Khooni was a sharpshooter of the Sushil Moonchh gang. 36 cases of serious crimes like murder, robbery, extortion and kidnapping were registered against him in several states, including Uttar Pradesh. Shamli Police had announced a reward of ₹50K on him.

Ram Mandir donation theft:Kiran S. to lead new SIT, Ayodhya DIG, SSP included; report to be submitted in SC after 2-days
stories.summary: In the Ayodhya Ram Mandir donation theft case, the UP government has formed a new Special Investigation Team (SIT). It has three members. Its command has been given to IG Lucknow Range Kiran S. Earlier, the SIT was headed by IAS officer Vijay Vishwas Pant. Kiran S. was in his team, but Vishwas Pant was the team in-charge. The Supreme Court had ordered the formation of a new SIT headed by a senior IPS officer during the hearing of the case on July 13, 2026. This order was given during the hearing by the bench of Chief Justice Suryakant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana. The court had said that the status report would have to be presented in court on July 27. Immediately after this order, the UP government had formed the SIT. According to sources, the new SIT has also started its investigation. The court had held that the role of police officers is direct and more effective in criminal investigation and technical examination of theft cases. Therefore, by making DIG and SSP members, the scope of investigation has been directly handed over to officers of the police department. The old SIT was reporting at the state government level, whereas the new SIT will have to file status reports directly to the Supreme Court from time to time. The Supreme Court itself will monitor the investigation of the entire case. Earlier, the SIT formed on the instructions of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was headed by Lucknow Division Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant, which included the IG Lucknow Range as a member. A senior officer of the police department informed that after the new guidelines of the Supreme Court, the SIT has now been reconstituted and the IG Lucknow Range has been made its chairman, while the DIG and SSP of Ayodhya have been appointed as its members.

stories.title: NEET student gang rape accused shot by police before arrest:Cop injured; brutal assault took place on Chitrakoot hill 3-days ago
stories.summary: Police shot and captured one of the accused who had held a boyfriend hostage and gang-raped a NEET student in an encounter in Chitrakoot. During this, a constable was also shot. Both have been admitted to the Community Health Center (CHC) Shivrampur. The encounter took place on Saturday at 5 PM in the Madtha forest under Bharkoop police station. The accused has been identified as Jitendra alias Bhola. Jitendra is a resident of Kalla village in Shivrampur. On July 22, three youths had gang-raped the student at Devangana Ghat in Chitrakoot. Student had gone to Devangana Ghati with her boyfriend A 20-year-old female student from Satna, Madhya Pradesh, was sitting on a hill at Devangana Ghat with her 17-year-old boyfriend from Chitrakoot on Wednesday, July 22. Just then, 3 boys arrived there on a bike. Posing as forest workers, they threatened both of them. They beat the boyfriend with a belt and tied his hands and feet with a towel. After this, the three dragged the student into the bushes and committed a heinous act. After the incident, all three fled. The boyfriend untied his hands and feet himself and reached the student. She was in shock. The boyfriend himself called and informed the police. Devangana Ghat forest is 12 km away from the district headquarters. The student was living in Kota, Rajasthan, preparing for NEET. Her boyfriend studies in 12th grade. Based on the student's complaint, the police have registered an FIR and are trying to catch the accused. One accused, Jitendra, was injured in an encounter. Meanwhile, his 2 companions have not been traced yet. All three accused were seen going on a bike in CCTV footage. The police had also released CCTV pictures of all three. Read what the boyfriend told the police Threatened girlfriend saying they would throw her off the hill if she screamed On the day of the incident, the boyfriend told the police - I became friends with the girl on social media 2 years ago. A few days ago, the girl came home on leave. I had called her to Chitrakoot for sightseeing. On July 22 (Wednesday) afternoon, she reached Chitrakoot. At 1 pm, both of us reached Devangana Valley on a bike. We were sitting on the hill making reels. At 3 PM, 3 boys arrived on a bike. They suddenly stopped the bike and started interrogating us. They started touching my girlfriend inappropriately. When I protested, they beat me with a belt. One boy grabbed me. They tied my hands and feet with a towel. The other two started threatening my girlfriend. They said if she made noise, they would throw her down the hill. Then they forcibly took my girlfriend into the bushes and committed brutality with her. After a while, the boy who was standing near me as a hostage also went into the bushes. He also raped my girlfriend. My girlfriend kept screaming. After those boys left, I somehow freed my hands. I ran to my girlfriend. I called Dial-112 from my mobile. But the call didn't go through due to no network. After this, we climbed down the hill a bit, then the mobile got network. I called again and summoned the police. Police arrived at 4:45 PM and admitted both of us to the hospital.

stories.title: Akhilesh says, 'Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation is youth's victory':Young generation stays awake at night; that's why PM had to deliver his speech during night
stories.summary: After Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation in the NEET paper leak case, political activity in UP has intensified. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav called it a major victory for the youth. He said, ''The new generation stays awake at night; that's why the PM had to give a speech at night. Seeing the power of youth, he tilted his mobile. This decision should have been taken earlier.'' Apna Dal Kamerawadi MLA Pallavi Patel said, ''What no one could do, the country's youth have done. Those who had robbed their future were forced to resign. This is a warning for the government. If the students had waited a few more days, they would have changed both the power and the system of the country.'' Meanwhile, UP Congress President Ajay Rai said, ''Lakhs of hardworking students of the country have won. The BJP government, which tried to suppress the truth, had to bow down before the determination of the youth today. No culprit who played with the future of the youth should be spared.'' Ajay Rai said- This is the victory of lakhs of students of the country UP Congress President Ajay Rai said, ''The BJP government, which tried to suppress the truth with the force of lathis, tear gas and police repression, had to bow down before the determination of the youth today! This victory belongs to the lakhs of hardworking students of the country, who stood on the streets overnight for their future.'' Our leader Rahul Gandhi and every Congress worker stood shoulder to shoulder with the youth and will continue to do so. Now the demand is clear- there should be a thorough investigation of this entire system and no culprit who played with the future of the youth should be spared! Irfan Solanki said - Truth can be troubled, not defeated Former SP MLA Irfan Solanki said - In Delhi, for almost a month, the youth, the elderly, everyone proved that truth can be troubled but not defeated. Finally, the victory is ours, of those Indians who fought this battle for rights. Congratulations to all of you. May Allah make your future brighter, better, and glorious. Meanwhile, MLA Naseem Solanki from Sisamau said - I congratulate those children, those students, all the children of the country who have placed the agenda of education before the public, before the government today. Their demand has been fulfilled, so I congratulate them from my heart. Naseem said - I salute those parents who have such fighting spirit children... who came forward and put forth their point. And this is the future of our India. May their future be bright; I pray for this. Thank you again from the heart.

stories.title: First sends lover to jail, now wants to marry him:Drinks phenyl outside police station; keeps demanding marriage with accused
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, on Saturday, a 22-year-old girl, insisting on marrying her lover, drank phenyl in front of the Chauri Chaura police station gate. After this, a chaotic atmosphere ensued there. The girl fell unconscious right in front of the police station. The police immediately took her to Chauri Chaura CHC in the police jeep, where doctors have started her treatment. According to the police, the girl had filed an FIR at Chauri Chaura police station, accusing her lover of physical exploitation by luring her with marriage. The police arrested the accused and sent him to jail on Friday. On Saturday, the girl once again came to the police station and was insisting on marrying her lover who was in jail. She was counselled. During this, she came out of the police station and drank phenyl. Incident at 2:30 PM A young woman from the Mahuadih police station area of Deoria reached the Chauri Chaura police station around 2:30 PM. Upon entering the station, she insisted to the police personnel that they arrange her marriage with her lover. When the police personnel tried to explain, she went outside and drank phenyl. She had brought the phenyl in her bag beforehand. Hearing the commotion from nearby people, 6 to 7 female police officers present at the station rushed to her. They immediately picked up the young woman and laid her in the police jeep parked inside the station. Hurt by this, the young woman went to Chauri Chaura police station and filed a complaint against her lover, demanding strict action. Acting on this, Chauri Chaura police arrested the accused on July 24th in the afternoon, took legal action, and sent him to jail. SP North Gyanendra Kumar stated that the young woman was asking the young man to marry her. An FIR was also filed against the same young man. Based on this, action was taken, the accused was arrested, and the police sent him to jail. The young woman has been sent to the hospital. Now her condition is stable.
