stories.title: Why Governor said Additional Chief Secretary 'keeps moving files around':8 major UP projects stalled, MLAs anxious ahead of Assembly polls
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Governor Anandiben Patel has held Additional Chief Secretary (Higher Education) M.P. Agarwal responsible for the delay in providing scooters to eligible girl students. Expressing her displeasure, she remarked, ‘They keep moving this file from one office to another.’ Following the Governor's sharp criticism, Dainik Bhaskar examined the progress of several flagship projects under the Yogi Adityanath government. The investigation found that some schemes have either failed to take off or remain stuck due to bureaucratic delays, procedural bottlenecks and internal disputes. With Assembly elections approaching, MLAs are likely to face questions from voters over the lack of progress. Here are eight major projects that remain delayed. 1. Rani Lakshmi Bai Scooty Yojana One year spent framing rules, which still exclude many rural students Announcement: The BJP had promised to provide scooters to meritorious girl students in its 2022 election manifesto. The state allocated ₹400 crore for the scheme in the 2025–26 Budget. Bureaucratic hurdle: Officials took nearly a year to frame the scheme's rules. The final eligibility criteria require students to score at least 90%, a condition that has drawn criticism. Impact: Governor Anandiben Patel objected to the rule, saying it would mainly benefit girls in urban areas studying in private schools with access to tuition. She said girls from rural areas, many of whom walk 10–12 km to attend school, would largely be excluded from the scheme. 2. Bus Stand Redevelopment (PPP Mode) Tender process delayed by dispute between senior officials Project: Forty-nine bus stands across Uttar Pradesh are to be modernised under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model. Bureaucratic hurdle: Under government rules, tenders should be opened the day after submission. However, an ongoing dispute between Additional Chief Secretary Archana Agarwal and Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (UPSRTC) Managing Director P.N. Singh has stalled the process. First-phase tenders have remained pending for a month, while second-phase tenders have been delayed by 11 days. Impact: Even after intervention by Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh, the files did not move forward. With elections nearing, MLAs want construction work to begin quickly in their constituencies. Skill Development Minister Kapil Dev Agarwal has also written to the government urging action. 3. Smartphone and Tablet Distribution Scheme Target of two crore beneficiaries in five years; only 60 lakh devices distributed in four years Promise: The government planned to distribute smartphones and tablets to two crore students over five years. The 2025–26 Budget earmarked ₹2,374 crore to provide devices to 40 lakh students. Bureaucratic hurdle: Delays in framing guidelines, issuing tenders and completing procurement slowed implementation. In four years, only 60 lakh devices have been distributed. The nodal agency, UPDESCO, and the Industrial Development Department are still engaged in the tendering and price negotiation process. Impact: Ahead of the Assembly elections, MLAs want devices distributed through them to students aged over 18, hoping the programme reaches beneficiaries before polling. However, large-scale procurement and supply are expected to take more time. 4. Outsourced Services Corporation Corporation established, but no recruitment after one year Announcement: Following the 2025 Budget, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath announced that the minimum honorarium for outsourced employees would be increased to ₹16,000 per month and that an Outsourced Services Corporation would be created to manage recruitment. In September 2025, IAS officer Amrita Soni was appointed Managing Director of the corporation. Bureaucratic hurdle: Nearly a year after its formation, not a single recruitment has been initiated through the corporation. Impact: There is still no clarity on revised salaries, allowances, provident fund deductions or gratuity benefits. More than three lakh outsourced employees continue to wait for the promised increase in their honorarium. Four more major projects progressing slowly 1. UP Startup mission In July 2024, Information Technology Minister Sunil Sharma directed officials to launch the UP Startup Mission. However, the proposal remained stuck in bureaucratic processes for nearly two years before recently receiving Cabinet approval. There is still no timeline for its launch. Meanwhile, the SWAN-3 project, intended to provide high-speed digital connectivity to blocks and gram panchayats, has also seen little progress under the Higher Education Department led by ACS Alok Kumar. 2. Family ID Scheme The government had promised employment opportunities for at least one member of every family under the 'Ek parivar, Ek pehchan' initiative. However, due to administrative delays, the scheme has yet to move beyond the planning stage and remains largely on paper. 3. Labour Adda Scheme The government announced in the 2025 Budget that Labour Addas would be established for construction workers in all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh. More than a year later, the scheme has been implemented only in six major cities, including Lucknow, Noida and Ghaziabad. The remaining 69 districts are yet to see any progress. 4. Groundbreaking ceremony Following the first Ground Breaking Ceremony in February 2024, investors have been waiting for the second edition. When asked about the delay in projects handled by Invest UP and the Industrial Development Department, ACS Alok Kumar said the department was fully prepared and that the programme would be held once the Chief Minister finalised a suitable date.

stories.title: Brij Bhushan's changed tone sparks speculation:Praises Akhilesh as ‘Krishna’s descendant’, swipe at BJP fuels talks over his discontent
stories.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader and six-time former MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh has once again sparked political debate with a series of statements that appear to contradict his party's official position. His recent remarks rejecting Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's claim about Hanumangarhi and describing Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav as a "religious person" and a "descendant of Lord Krishna" have fueled speculation over whether he is signalling political dissent or preparing for a new political role. The statements come amid a pattern of public positions over the past two years in which Brij Bhushan has alternately praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi, questioned Yogi Adityanath's leadership, criticised the Ram Mandir Trust, and made comments at odds with the BJP's broader political messaging. The Hanumangarhi row On July 10, while addressing a gathering at Sohawal in Ayodhya, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath claimed: "During the Samajwadi Party government, namaz was offered on the steps of Hanumangarhi temple and Roza Iftar was organised there. If opposition parties are truly secular, can they organise a Hanuman Chalisa recital inside a Jama Masjid?" Seven days later, Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh publicly contradicted the Chief Minister. He said: "Namaz was never offered at Hanumangarhi. That claim is completely false. The Hanumangarhi temple was constructed by a Muslim, and even today a stone bearing his name is installed there." The remark immediately drew attention because it directly challenged the Chief Minister's version of events. A pattern of contradictory statements Political observers note that this is not the first time Brij Bhushan has departed from the BJP's official narrative. Over the past two years, he has: These repeated interventions have led to speculation that the veteran leader may be attempting to redefine his political position. Shared political roots with Yogi Adityanath Despite the recent differences, Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and Yogi Adityanath share a long political association. Both were disciples of Mahant Avaidyanath, the former head of the Gorakhnath Math. A frequently recalled incident from Parliament involved Yogi Adityanath becoming emotional during a speech, when Brij Bhushan, seated beside him, handed him a handkerchief. Even so, their public statements in recent years have often suggested growing political distance. Political experts see long-term strategy Senior journalist Anand Rai believes politicians frame public statements around future political objectives. According to him, Brij Bhushan has always respected Mahant Avaidyanath, and while no personal hostility between him and Yogi Adityanath has openly emerged, his recent remarks indicate political calculations that may relate to future ambitions. 'His political stature extends beyond BJP' Senior Ayodhya-based journalist Indrabhushan Pandey argues that Brij Bhushan's political identity is larger than his party affiliation. He points out that despite the BJP's stated opposition to dynastic politics, the party fielded both Brij Bhushan's wife and son in elections, reflecting his political influence. Pandey also maintains that Brij Bhushan's comments on Hanumangarhi are consistent with historical records. According to him, historical gazetteers mention that Nawab Shuja-ud-Daula played a role in the construction of Hanumangarhi, and there is no historical evidence of namaz or Roza Iftar being organised on the temple steps. He also noted that Brij Bhushan was one of the prominent leaders of the Ram Temple movement and felt slighted after not receiving an invitation to the consecration ceremony. Pandey further said that some religious scholars, including all four Shankaracharyas, consider the temple religiously incomplete because its shikhara (spire) and religious flag have not yet been installed. Openly speaking on reservation and upper-caste politics While the BJP has taken a cautious approach on issues such as caste census and reservation, Brij Bhushan has frequently voiced support for upper-caste concerns. Senior journalist Suresh Bahadur Singh says Brij Bhushan has never openly endorsed reservation in its present form and believes those who have already benefited should not repeatedly receive reservation benefits. According to Singh, Brij Bhushan has consistently cultivated upper-caste politics because of the demographic composition of his constituency. At the same time, Singh notes that the former MP also enjoys support across caste and religious groups, including among Muslims. Signals of a new political alignment? Following the controversy involving allegations by women wrestlers, Brij Bhushan's own political standing within the BJP appears to have weakened, although his political family remains influential, with one son serving as an MLA and another as an MP. Suresh Bahadur Singh believes Brij Bhushan still feels politically sidelined and has publicly expressed his desire to return to Parliament—whether on a BJP ticket or as an Independent. According to him, Brij Bhushan's recent statements may indicate efforts to rebuild his political relevance and negotiate from a stronger position. Could the Samajwadi Party become an option again? This would not be the first time Brij Bhushan has switched political camps. After being expelled from the BJP in 2008, he joined the Samajwadi Party under Mulayam Singh Yadav and won the 2009 Lok Sabha election on an SP ticket. Ironically, Mulayam Singh had earlier ordered his arrest during the Ram Temple movement. Political observers believe Brij Bhushan's recent praise of Akhilesh Yadav may be a form of "pressure politics"—signalling to the BJP leadership that he has political alternatives. Anand Rai says Brij Bhushan's earlier conflict with the SP stemmed largely from his rivalry with Gonda politician Vinod Singh alias Pandit Singh, whom Mulayam Singh reportedly favoured. Why is Brij Bhushan considered upset? Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh has been elected to the Lok Sabha six times—in 1991, 1999, 2004, 2009, 2014 and 2019—from Kaiserganj, Gonda and Balrampur. He also secured parliamentary victories for his wife in 1996 and his son in 2024. Despite his electoral influence, he has never been given a major ministerial or organisational role in either the state or central leadership, something political observers say he believes he deserved. After the wrestlers' protest, he was forced to step down from the Wrestling Federation, and the BJP denied him a ticket in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Why BJP cannot ignore him Political analysts believe Brij Bhushan continues to wield considerable influence in eastern Uttar Pradesh. He is considered influential across nearly 20 Assembly constituencies in districts such as Gonda, Basti, Bahraich and Balrampur, while his reach among Rajput voters extends to nearly 50 Assembly seats in Purvanchal. Earlier this year, he demonstrated his organisational strength through the 'Rashtrakatha' event at Nandini College in Gonda. He also remains a recognised face among Rajput communities in neighbouring Bihar, where he campaigned during Assembly elections. Potential electoral impact Analysts say Brij Bhushan may not be capable of independently delivering victories across these constituencies, but his dissatisfaction could influence Rajput voting patterns enough to hurt the BJP in closely contested seats. Political commentators draw parallels with Kalyan Singh's exit from the BJP in 2002, when he won only a handful of seats himself but was widely credited with contributing to the defeat of numerous BJP candidates. A similar impact was seen when Shivpal Yadav's rebellion affected the Samajwadi Party's prospects in the 2017 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. With his increasingly independent public stance, Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh's political moves are likely to remain under close watch as Uttar Pradesh's political landscape evolves.

Man dies after Jagannath chariot collides with high tension line:Accident amidst rain in Meerut; 11 devotees burnt, 2 thousand people were present
stories.summary: In Meerut on Friday, during the Rath Yatra of Lord Jagannath, the chariot touched an 11,000 volt high-tension line. One devotee died due to electrocution. 11 people were burnt. The accident occurred in Parikshitgarh town. This Rath Yatra was being taken out amidst rain. About 2,000 devotees were participating in it. The injured have been admitted to the hospital. According to eyewitnesses, as soon as the current struck, several people sitting on the chariot fell down. There was screaming and crying at the spot. Stampede-like conditions arose. Devotees started running here and there to save their lives. See two pictures- The Katha concluded on Thursday evening A procession and Katha program of Lord Jagannath was organized at Om Public School in Parikshitgarh town. Five days ago, a grand procession of Lord Jagannath was taken out in the city. After this, a religious discourse was being organized by Maharaj Rohit Risaliya Vrindavan. The discourse concluded on Thursday evening. On Friday afternoon, Lord Jagannath's chariot procession was taken out in the city with bands playing. This accident occurred as soon as the procession started. Chariot procession started without worship rituals Lord Jagannath was already seated on the chariot. Preparations for worship rituals were underway so that the chariot procession could begin properly. During this time, as soon as it started raining, some people began pulling the chariot rope and taking it away. Some devotees protested against this, but they didn't listen to anyone. They started taking the chariot towards the Rajwahe track. Here, the top of the chariot touched the 11000 volt high tension line passing overhead and electric current flowed down. One youth died, 11 devotees burnt In the accident, Sachin (30), a resident of Parikshitgarh, was severely burnt. He was taken to the Community Health Center, where doctors declared him dead. Meanwhile, 11 burnt devotees have been admitted to the Community Health Center and private hospitals. Sachin used to support his family by doing labor work. His father Nandkishore also does labor work. The family includes his mother, younger brother Vishal, and two sisters Prachi and Vishakha. There was chaos at home after Sachin's death. The condition of some of the injured is said to be critical. Among the burnt people are 11 including Priyanshu, Vivek, Manish residents of Aurangabad, Shivam, Yash, Pihu residents of Parikshitgarh, Nimesh resident of Ahmadpuri, Maharaj Bharatdas from Lakhimpur Kheri, Rajesh Mishra. Now what did the eyewitnesses say, let's know- Police had raised objection regarding the 14 feet height As soon as information about the accident was received, Rural SP Abhijit Kumar reached the spot. Police from several stations also reached the incident site along with him. Officials inspected the incident site and gathered information about the causes of the accident. According to police, this time the main patron of the katha was social worker Atul Sharma. This katha has been taking place in the village for the past seven years. Police are investigating how the chariot came in contact with the high-tension line and also looking into safety standards. Some villagers who reached the mortuary said that every year the organizers and venue of the katha change. This time the responsibility of organizing was with Atul Sharma. When this chariot was prepared, its height was approximately 14 feet. Police had raised objections to this, but the organizers did not listen. DM said - Will investigate and take action DM VK Singh said - About 11 people came in contact with the electric current in the accident. All the injured were immediately taken to CHC and district hospital. Most of them are in stable condition and are out of danger. One woman has been referred for better treatment. Teams from police, health department and administration are present at the spot. The entire matter is being investigated and necessary action is being taken.

stories.title: Explosion rocks firecracker factory, 2 dead, 2 missing:Body parts are thrown 100 metres away, houses walls shaken
stories.summary: A powerful explosion ripped through a firecracker factory in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur on Friday evening, killing two workers and leaving two others missing. Sutli bombs have reportedly been manufactured at the factory for the past five years. At the time of the blast, 24 workers were on duty, of whom 20 escaped safely. The explosion was so intense that the victims' bodies were torn apart. One body was recovered from beneath the factory debris, while the other was found nearly 100 metres away near a field. The body was badly mutilated, with the face beyond recognition and body parts scattered across the area. According to the village head, the blast occurred at around 5 pm. The impact was so strong that walls of houses in the village, located about 500 metres away, shook. Police, district officials and fire brigade teams are carrying out rescue operations at the site. The firecracker factory, spread across nearly 10 bighas of land, is located on the outskirts of Naya Gaon in Gangoh police station area, around 54 km from the district headquarters. Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Abhinandan confirmed the two deaths. He said part of the factory collapsed and caught fire after the explosion. Rescue teams are continuing to search the debris for those still trapped. The exact cause of the blast is yet to be determined. 2 pictures related to the incident

stories.title: Class 12 student dies by suicide:Shoots himself in head; father brings rifle home the previous night
stories.summary: An 18-year-old boy shot himself dead on Friday morning in Agra. He was an intermediate student and the only son of his parents. His father had brought a licensed rifle home on Thursday night. Around 10 AM, the student locked himself in a room and shot himself in the head, blowing off half of his face. Hearing the sound of firing, family members and people from the vicinity rushed to the spot, but by then he had already died. The family is in deep shock due to the child's suicidal act. The reason why he did it has not come to light. Police have questioned people. See 3 pictures... The father had arrived home at 2:30 AM, the son himself had opened the door. The incident is from Teachers Colony in Bah police station area. Aditya Sharma (18 years old), who lived here, was a 12th-grade student. His mother, Dolly, is a homemaker. His father, Sudeep Sharma, is a security guard in a private company in Rajasthan. He often stays out for work. According to family members, Sudeep Sharma reached home around 2:30 AM on Thursday late night. At that time, Aditya was awake. When his father arrived, he was the one who opened the door. Sudeep had placed the rifle on top of a trunk in the room and then went to sleep. He had no idea at that time that such a big accident would happen just a few hours later. Didn't go to school in the morning, locked himself in the room On Friday morning, Aditya did not go to school. He was sleeping in the room on the roof. Family members thought he might be resting due to staying up late. After some time, when his mother went to wake Aditya, he locked the door from inside. The mother came down from the roof and got busy with her work. Parents rushed upon hearing the gunshot Around 10 AM, Aditya shot himself with a rifle. The firing caused chaos in the house. His parents and neighbors rushed towards the roof. The police were informed. When the police broke down the door and entered, Aditya was found covered in blood. Half of his face was missing. Family said - he was treated for depression Father Sudeep said, Aditya was in depression two-three years ago. He used to get angry over small things. He was treated for it. Then he got better. In recent days, he was behaving normally. There was no problem. We don't understand why he did this. Police seized the rifle Police have taken possession of the rifle. The forensic team has also collected evidence from the spot. Currently, no suicide note has been recovered from the crime scene. Station in-charge Devi Prasad Tiwari said that according to the initial investigation, it is a case of suicide. However, further action will be taken only on the basis of the post-mortem report, forensic investigation, and other evidence.

stories.title: 34 questions for Shri Ram Trust CEO:Form asks candidates if they are ‘staunch Hindu’ or a believer
stories.summary: Information has been sought from applicants for the CEO post of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust on 34 questions. A three-member selection committee has provided an online Google Form to all applicants to fill out. It asks for information ranging from personal details to their administrative capabilities and crowd management. The selection committee has to prepare a list of three best applicants out of 5200 and submit it to the Trust before September 2. Personal and General Information In nine points, the applicant is asked for their personal information. This includes the applicant's full name, date of birth, age, and contact details (address, city, state, pin code, mobile number, email). Additionally, they will have to state their proficiency in Hindi and English. Options are provided for all answers. Educational and professional qualification The applicant will have to state their highest educational qualification. For instance, whether they are a graduate or hold any other qualification including a PhD. Are they currently employed somewhere or have they retired? The full details of that organisation must be provided. They will also have to state their total experience in the corporate, administrative, or managerial sector. For this, they will have to choose an option of 20 to 30 years or more. They will also have to state their field of work. Such as whether they are associated with corporate, defence, administration, bureaucracy, public sector undertakings, banking, IT, or any other sector. How many employees have they led so far? For this, they need to choose an option from 1000 to 5000 or more. How much experience in managing large events? Many large events take place throughout the year in Ayodhya. Millions of people gather for these. In such a situation, crowd management skills will be crucial. For this, the selection committee has asked applicants which large event they have previously operated or managed. Applicants will have to choose the option indicating how many people participated in those events: 5,000 to 20,000 or more. They will also have to state how many days the event lasted, whether it was 1 to 5 days or more than that. The applicant will also have to state in which year they led the said large event, the name of that event, and their own role played in it. Questions related to social, religious, and spiritual beliefs The applicant will have to state whether they have previously been associated with any social or religious organization or any monastery-temple. If yes, what was the duration of their experience? For this, an option of 1 to 10 years or more will have to be selected. What was the size of the said religious or social institution? The applicant will also have to state whether they are a staunch Hindu or a devout Hindu. Applicant must state their vision, plan, and references For Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra, the applicant will also have to state their vision, action plan, and suggestions. If the applicant has any specific or extraordinary achievement, they will have to state it. To verify their professional, social, and religious experiences, they will have to provide the names and contact details of at least 2 reputable individuals as references. Final selection will be under the supervision of the Center and RSS A senior member of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust said - The final selection of the CEO for this sensitive post will be under the direct supervision of the Central Government and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). The person who will sit on the CEO's chair will be someone on whom both the government and the Sangh agree. Not only that, in the future, the consent of the Center and the Sangh will play an important role in the selection of the CEO office staff.

stories.title: Officer slapped during inspection:Suspended clerk attacks official, says, ‘Take out the pistol, let’s kill him’
stories.summary: An executive engineer was allegedly assaulted inside the Irrigation Department's Flood Division office in Gorakhpur while carrying out an official inspection. According to the complaint, a suspended clerk, an assistant engineer, and another man entered the office, surrounded him and repeatedly slapped him. The engineer alleged that during the assault, the suspended clerk shouted, “Take out the pistol, let's kill him today. I won't spare him.” The altercation continued for around 20 minutes before officials and staff intervened and brought the situation under control. The incident took place at around 1 pm on Thursday, while a video of the assault surfaced on Friday. Engineer alleges attack linked to suspension of clerk The Executive Engineer alleged that he had suspended the clerk following a departmental inquiry and had also ordered his salary to be withheld. He claimed the assault was carried out in retaliation for those disciplinary actions. Based on his complaint, police have registered a case against two named and four unidentified accused. 'Office staff saved my life,' says Executive Engineer According to Executive Engineer Vipin Singh, he and Chief Engineer Vikas Singh were inspecting the Flood Division office in the Cantt police station area on Thursday afternoon when the incident occurred. Vipin Singh said- While I was inspecting the office, Irrigation Department clerk Deepak Pandey arrived with his associates. They pushed past the Chief Engineer to reach me and began abusing me. He added- When I objected, they started assaulting me. A man wearing a black helmet slapped me first, after which all three repeatedly hit me. The office staff somehow managed to save my life. The accused fled after threatening to kill me. I immediately went to Cantt police station and lodged a written complaint. Clerk had allegedly issued earlier threats The Executive Engineer further alleged that clerk Deepak Pandey had threatened him on previous occasions in January and April, including warning that he would have him abducted from his home through another employee. He said he had reported those threats to the Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), District Magistrate (DM) and Commissioner. Following a departmental inquiry, Deepak Pandey was suspended on 30 April, and his salary was withheld. Police begin investigation CO Cantt Abha Singh said a case has been registered based on the Executive Engineer's complaint. She said both parties will be questioned and statements will also be recorded from employees who were present in the office at the time of the incident. Further action will be taken after the investigation is completed.

stories.title: Heavy rain puts Uttar Pradesh on edge:Flood alert in 54 districts, 10 rivers overflow; crocodile enters village in Lakhimpur Kheri
stories.summary: Continuous rainfall over the past 15 days has begun to worsen flood conditions across Uttar Pradesh, with more than 10 rivers, including the Ganga and Yamuna, flowing above normal levels. The Hindon in Baghpat and Noida, the Ganga in Budaun, the Ghaghara in Ayodhya, Gonda and Ballia, and the Gandak in Kushinagar are all flowing above the danger mark. Meanwhile, authorities have issued a rain alert for 54 districts on Friday. Dam gates opened, floodwater enters villages In Sonbhadra, three gates of the Kanhar Dam were opened after the reservoir's water level rose significantly. In Sitapur, around 320,000 cusecs of water were released from the Banbasa, Girija and Ghaghara barrages, causing the Sharda and Ghaghara rivers to swell. Floodwater has entered several villages, and in one village, water is flowing over an unpaved road, forcing residents to travel by boat. Crocodile spotted on road, riverbank erosion intensifies In Lakhimpur Kheri, a crocodile was seen running along a village road after floodwaters spread into nearby areas. In Basti, severe erosion has been reported along the banks of the Saryu River, with several trees collapsing into the river. Rain in Lucknow, cloud cover across more than 30 districts Light rain was recorded in Lucknow and Gonda on Friday morning. Cloudy conditions prevailed in Barabanki, Agra, and more than 30 other districts across the state. On Thursday, an average of 2.2 mm of rainfall was recorded across 42 districts, with Sonbhadra receiving the highest rainfall at 13 mm. See 3 photos- CM Yogi orders officials to remain on the ground Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed officials to stay in the field and closely monitor the situation. He instructed them to provide all possible assistance to people affected by heavy rain, flooding and lightning. Rainfall to ease for three days before monsoon strengthens again According to Atul Kumar Singh, a meteorologist in Lucknow, rainfall activity is expected to decline over the next three days. With the monsoon trough shifting southwards and the low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal weakening, rainfall activity will temporarily reduce. Monsoon activity has currently shifted towards west-central India. Weather conditions are expected to change again after three to four days, and the monsoon is likely to become active once more from 26–27 July, bringing widespread rainfall.

On Thursday evening, the CBI team reached the Divisional Railway Manager (DRM) office and carried out searches at Nitesh Agarwal's office and residence. Family members and office staff were also questioned as part of the investigation.

stories.title: CM Yogi hears grievances of 150 people at Janta Darshan:Assures swift action on all complaints
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, who is on a three-day visit to Gorakhpur, once again interacted with members of the public during 'Janta Darshan' on Friday morning. This was the second consecutive day that he held the public grievance session. The Chief Minister met around 150 people, listened to their concerns and assured them that effective action would be taken on every complaint. He instructed officials present at the event to ensure that all grievances received during the Janta Darshan are resolved promptly. CM personally collects applications, directs officials on the spot On Friday morning, the Chief Minister personally met people seated outside the Mahant Digvijaynath Smriti Bhawan in the Gorakhnath Temple complex. He listened to each person individually, collected their written applications and issued directions to the officials standing nearby regarding the resolution of their grievances. Applications relating to various issues were forwarded to the concerned administrative and police officials, with instructions to ensure fair and time-bound action. Orders strict action on crime and land encroachment complaints Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath directed police officials to take strict action on complaints related to crime and illegal land encroachment. He also reviewed applications seeking financial assistance for medical treatment and instructed officials to expedite the preparation of hospital cost estimates. The Chief Minister assured applicants that once the estimates are received, the government will release the required financial assistance without delay. Several women attended the Janta Darshan with their children. During the interaction, the Chief Minister greeted the children warmly, blessed them and distributed chocolates. The Chief Minister assured applicants that once the estimates are received, the government will release the required financial assistance without delay. Several women attended the Janta Darshan with their children. During the interaction, the Chief Minister greeted the children warmly, blessed them and distributed chocolates. Cattle respond to CM's familiar voice at Gorakhnath Temple cowshed During his stay at Gorakhnath Temple on Friday morning, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath visited the temple's gaushala (cowshed) and spent time feeding the cattle. While walking through the cowshed, he called several cows by their names. Familiar with his voice, the animals came running towards him. The Chief Minister affectionately stroked their foreheads and fed them jaggery by hand. He also offered jaggery to other cows and Nandi housed in the temple cowshed. Before leaving, he instructed the cowshed staff to continue ensuring proper care and welfare of the cattle.

stories.title: Village chief's lawyer son shot dead at restaurant:Was having dinner with friends when the attacker quietly approached, shot in the head
stories.summary: A village pradhan's son was shot dead at point-blank range inside a restaurant in Jhansi on Thursday night, triggering panic in the busy commercial area. Sanjay Singh had arrived at The Mad Kitchen restaurant near Elite Chowraha in the Nawabad police station area around 9.30 pm with four friends for dinner. While they were eating, an armed assailant walked in, placed a pistol against Sanjay's head and fired a single shot. Gunman escapes on waiting motorcycle, victim dies in hospital After carrying out the attack, the shooter ran to the restaurant's parking area, where an accomplice was waiting on a motorcycle. The two fled the scene before police arrived. Sanjay's friends rushed him to the medical college for treatment, but he succumbed to his injuries at around 1 am. Police have launched an investigation and are examining CCTV footage from the area to identify the attackers. LLB student and court clerk was living in Jhansi Sanjay Singh aka Sanju (33), the son of village head Ramdevi, was a resident of Haiwatpura village under the Garautha police station limits in Jhansi district. According to family members, Ramdevi has three children. Her elder son Sarvesh and daughter Rachna are married, while Sanjay was unmarried. Worked with advocate while completing law degree Sanjay had been living at a relative's house near Nandanpura in Jhansi for the past six years while pursuing his LLB. Alongside his studies, he worked as a clerk for Advocate Dashrath Singh at the district court. It was there that he became friends with Shivam, who was also employed in the same office. Returned from Datia temple before fatal shooting Sanjay Singh had returned from a visit to the Pitambara Peeth temple in Datia just hours before he was shot dead, according to his friend Shivam. Shivam said, “The group left the court around 4.30 pm on Thursday. Advocate Narayan Ojha, who had come to Jhansi from Chandauli, wanted to visit the temple. Sanjay, Shivam, Narayan Ojha and Advocate Dashrath Singh travelled to Datia by car and returned after offering prayers.” Gunman opened fire as friends finished dinner On their way back, the group stopped for dinner at The Mad Kitchen restaurant near Elite Chowk. Sanjay also called his friend Dharmendra, and the five of them were dining together. Shivam said, “We had almost finished eating when a young man dressed in black walked in and suddenly opened fire.” He added, “At first, we couldn't understand what had happened. When I looked at Sanjay, he stood up briefly and then collapsed. He had been shot in the head, and blood was flowing.” Guard tried to stop gunman, attacker escaped on number plate-less bike According to Sanjay's friend Shivam, the shooter fled the restaurant while brandishing his pistol after opening fire. A security guard stationed in the parking area attempted to intercept the attacker, but he escaped on a motorcycle driven by an accomplice. The bike reportedly had no number plate. Shivam said neither he nor his friends had seen the assailant before. Panic at restaurant as diners fled after gunshot Restaurant owner Vansh said, “The gunshot triggered panic among customers, many of whom abandoned their meals and rushed out of the premises.” He added, “A crowd soon gathered outside the restaurant, and the police were alerted. Officers from Nawabad police station reached the scene and launched an investigation.” Police are now examining CCTV footage from the restaurant and nearby locations to identify the attackers and trace their escape route. Family says Sanjay had no known rivalry Sanjay Singh's family rushed to Jhansi after learning about the murder. During questioning by the police his elder brother Sarvesh said that the family had no known enmity with anyone and was unaware of any motive behind the attack. He said, “There was no ongoing dispute related to the village pradhan's post and that the family had not received any threats.” Victim had been living in Jhansi for six years According to Sarvesh, “Sanjay had been residing in Jhansi for the past six years and only visited his native village occasionally.” He added, “Besides pursuing his law studies and working at the district court, he was also involved in land-related work. We had no idea who carried out the shooting or what prompted the attack.” Three police teams deployed, CCTV footage under scrutiny Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) B.B.G.T.S. Murthy said, “Multiple police teams, including the Special Operations Group (SOG), have been assigned to investigate the murder.” He said, “Officers are analysing CCTV footage from the restaurant and nearby areas to identify the gunman and trace his movements before and after the attack.” Police claim key leads, hunt for accused continues The SSP said, “Investigators have already obtained some crucial leads and are actively pursuing them.” He added, “We are confident the case will be cracked soon.” However, despite the ongoing search operation, the accused had not been traced till now.

stories.title: 'Our husband is our God,' say reel-making sisters:Married to stay together in Amroha, turned down a government employee's proposal
stories.summary: “Vikas has saved us sisters, he is like God for us. Papa had found a boy with a government job for didi, but we want to stay with Vikas only. We married him for his love. Some people think we did this for social media content and views. Let us tell you that our videos already get a lot of views.” This is what the 3 sisters who married a cameraman in Amroha say. The sisters made and posted a video. They say, “Since the wedding, people are asking all kinds of questions. We want to tell everyone that we are happy and together. Everyone should accept this.” The three sisters made a video to respond to people Hasanpur Kotwali area residents Alka (20), Devika (19) and Santosh (18) are from Dhauriya village and are real sisters. All three married their cameraman Vikas in a temple on July 17. After the wedding video surfaced, people have been commenting and asking various questions. To answer these questions, they have created and shared a six-minute video. The three sisters were already famous on social media The reel-making sisters have an account on Instagram under the name Rajput Girl. They have posted 981 posts so far. They have 4.72 lakh followers. Until 16 July, funny videos were posted on this account, which received views in millions. Posted 12 videos after the wedding, got 40 million views In the Instagram videos, sometimes all three sisters appeared together, sometimes they posted separately. Cameraman Vikas also often appeared in their videos. Since the wedding, they have posted 12 videos so far, which have received 40 million views. The three sisters say, “We also thought a lot initially. We looked for homes where we could find 3 boys. But that didn't happen. Somewhere there were two boys, somewhere one boy was quite young. After all paths were closed, we chose this option. We married our cameraman.” They say being short doesn't make someone a minor Alka says, “Some people are saying that our youngest sister is a minor. Let us tell you that she became an adult last year itself. Some people have short height. Neha Kakkar is 4 feet tall, so will you people call her a minor too? Get our blood test done through the government. If someone's face looks childlike, then will you people keep calling them a minor for 100 years?” Groom said they don't need my love Cameraman Vikas, who married all three sisters, says, "I could have married just one of them if I wanted. But their situation was not like that. They wanted to stay together. I am just a means to keep them together. They don't need my love, there is already a lot of love among them. They said, “Our videos already have a lot of views” In response to those commenting on the marriage, the three sisters say, “When our family has accepted us, you people should also accept. We had only two options, either die or live together. Vikas saved us. He is God for us. We have gotten married and are happy. If you think we did this for content, then look at our account. Our videos were already getting a lot of views.” It should be noted that after the wedding video surfaced, Hindu organisations have objected to it. The police have also become active. On the morning of Thursday, July 23, at 10 AM, the three sisters and their husband were called to the police station. There, all four were interrogated for 3 hours. Married of our own free will, police told All three brides told the police, “We did not marry under any pressure. All three of us are adults. We will die, but will not separate. On the question of registering the marriage, they said that some marriages don't work even after registration. We are happy as we are. If anyone asks us for proof, then we will see. After questioning, the police let all four go home.”

stories.title: Why no consensus on Ram Mandir Trust general secretary:RSS-VHP back different names; announcement delayed as 3 names emerge for 2 posts
stories.summary: Differences have emerged within the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust over the appointment of its next General Secretary, with the RSS and the Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) backing different candidates for the post. Krishna Mohan, who is currently serving as the Acting General Secretary, is reportedly the RSS's preferred choice, with several office-bearers supporting his candidature. However, a section of the Trust members has proposed the name of VHP International General Secretary Bajrang Lal Bagra for the position. Decision on three vacant posts deferred until September The Trust also failed to reach a consensus on two other vacant positions, with the names of litterateur Yatindra Mohan Mishra, Ayodhya saint Raghavacharya and Mithilesh Nandini Sharan under consideration. While some members have backed Yatindra Mohan Mishra, others have expressed support for Mithilesh Nandini Sharan. With no agreement emerging, the Trust has decided to defer all three appointments to allow time for wider consultations. According to sources, efforts are underway to build a consensus, and the final decision is expected to be announced during the Trust's meeting scheduled for September 2. Trust meeting convened to fill General Secretary and member vacancies The July 22 meeting of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust was convened primarily to appoint a new General Secretary and fill vacant positions within the Trust. Acting General Secretary Krishna Mohan had issued the meeting notice to all Trust members on July 7. According to the notice, the meeting was scheduled to be held in two phases. No consensus despite discussion on five names The first session, which began at 3 pm, focused on filling the vacant posts. Trust members discussed the proposed candidates, with the understanding that appointments would be announced only if a consensus was reached. During the hour-long deliberations on Wednesday, five names were considered for the vacant positions. However, the members failed to arrive at a unanimous decision, prompting the Trust to defer the appointments until a broader consensus is achieved. RSS, VHP lobby for their candidates in closed-door discussions The RSS reportedly made behind-the-scenes efforts to build consensus over all three vacant positions in the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. According to sources, the exercise was coordinated by RSS Eastern Region Pracharak Anil Kumar, who held a confidential meeting with key Trust members to discuss a strategy for securing support for the Sangh's preferred candidates. The Trust meeting began at 3 pm at Maniram Cantonment under the chairmanship of Mahant Nritya Gopal Das. Deliberations centred on appointing a new General Secretary and filling vacant Trust member positions. VHP stakes claim to General Secretary's post During the meeting, some members proposed confirming Acting General Secretary Krishna Mohan, an Indian Forest Service (IFS) officer and former regional coordinator for Eastern Uttar Pradesh, as the permanent General Secretary. However, differences soon emerged. While one section argued that the post should now go to an RSS nominee, others maintained that the Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP), which played a key role in the Ram Temple movement, deserved to retain the position. VHP International General Secretary Bajrang Lal Bagra's name was formally proposed for the post. Bagra, who had attended the Trust's July 7 meeting, had also arrived in Ayodhya ahead of the July 22 meeting. Despite sustained efforts to secure approval for his candidature, the members failed to reach a consensus, leaving the appointment unresolved. Trust defers appointments after disagreement over two member posts The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust also failed to finalise appointments to two vacant member positions, with multiple names emerging during the discussions. One vacancy arose after Dr. Anil Mishra resigned on June 26 following the donation theft controversy, while the other was created after the death of Ayodhya's titular king, Bimalendra Mohan Pratap Mishra. Differences among the Trust members prevented a final decision on either post. Three names proposed, consensus remains elusive As both vacancies had previously been held by residents of Ayodhya, members agreed that the new appointees should also be from the temple town. Mahant Dinendra Das of the Nirmohi Akhara proposed the name of litterateur Yatindra Mohan Mishra, son of the late Bimalendra Mohan Pratap Mishra, describing him as an honest and widely respected figure with a literary background. The names of Ayodhya saints Raghavacharya and Mithilesh Nandini Sharan were also put forward. Raghavacharya serves as the President of the Ramlala Sadan Devasthan Trust and the Peethadhishwar of Shridham Math, Ramvarnashram, while Mithilesh Nandini Sharan is regarded as a respected scholar and is considered close to both the RSS and the VHP. With three candidates in contention for two positions, the Trust could not reach a consensus and decided to postpone the appointments until a broader agreement is achieved. Trust aims to finalise appointments at September 2 meeting The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust is expected to take a final decision on filling its vacant posts at the next meeting, likely to be held on September 2. Speaking to the media after the July 22 meeting, Trust Treasurer Govind Dev Giri said the appointments had been deferred and would be finalised in the next round of deliberations. By then, the Trust is also expected to shortlist three candidates for the post of its new Chief Executive Officer (CEO). Focus shifts to building consensus on remaining vacancies According to sources, there is relatively little disagreement over the candidature of Bajrang Lal Bagra for the General Secretary's post. The main challenge lies in reaching a consensus on the two vacant Trust member positions. The Trust plans to continue consultations over the next two weeks and will take a final decision only after a broad agreement is achieved. If consensus remains elusive, the appointments may be decided through a formal vote among the Trust members.

stories.title: Jantar Mantar lathi-charge lookalike found in Ghaziabad:Says he is receiving death threats; TMC MP had called him a 'hired goon'
stories.summary: A video showing a baton charge during a student protest at Jantar Mantar, Delhi, on 20 July 2026 has gone viral on social media. In the footage, a young man in plain clothes can be seen carrying what appears to be a police baton. Social media users claimed the man was Honey Dagar, a resident of Ghaziabad. They alleged that although he is not a Delhi Police officer, he was seen wielding a baton alongside police personnel during the crackdown. The claim also drew political attention, with Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Mahua Moitra questioning the identity of the man and asking whether he was a hired goon. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Honey Dagar, who categorically denied the allegation. That is not me. The person may resemble me to some extent, but it isn't me. I run a gym in Ghaziabad. Since that day, my name, address, mobile number and details of my gym have been circulated on social media. He said the fallout has been severe. My family and I began receiving death threats. Around 30 men came to my gym and threatened me. I had to shut the gym for several days. Read the full conversation- 'My business has stopped, and I'm receiving death threats' Honey Dagar said the harassment began on the morning of 21 July. When I woke up, I saw abusive messages on Instagram. People called me an agent of an organisation and threatened to kill and assault me. He said the abuse continued across multiple platforms. When I opened WhatsApp, I found I was being trolled there as well. Initially, I had no idea why people were abusing me. Later, I realised that my name and address were being shared on social media, claiming I was the person involved in the baton charge at Jantar Mantar. Honey insisted he has no connection with the Delhi Police. I have never served in the Delhi Police. No one in my family is in the Delhi Police. I have never even visited Jantar Mantar, nor have I ever had any dispute with anyone. He said social media users have been posting his personal details—including his name, address, mobile number, village and gym address, as if they belonged to the man seen in the viral video. People are abusing me because of mistaken identity. Gym shut after men arrived to threaten him Fearing for his safety, Honey said he removed the signboards from his gym. About 30 men came to my gym to threaten me. Because of the fear, I have stopped opening the gym. He added that he has deactivated his social media accounts and changed his phone number. I closed my Instagram and Facebook accounts. I also stopped using my WhatsApp number. Because of the threats, I bought a new SIM card. Police provide security to the family Honey said he is originally from Chhajjupur village in the Partapur police station area of Meerut. His father, Indrapal Singh, is a farmer. Honey completed a Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) at IMR College, Ghaziabad, before opening his own gym. His family includes his wife, Akanksha Chaudhary, and their three-year-old son. According to Honey, the abuse has extended to his family as well. Since 20 July, my family has also been receiving abusive messages. He said the police have now provided protection. Two police officers have been deployed for our security. The police have told me that if a crowd gathers at the gym or anyone comes to threaten us, I should inform them immediately so action can be taken. Honey has submitted a complaint at Nandgram police station in Ghaziabad, seeking the registration of an FIR. In the complaint, he stated that he has been receiving death threats because of mistaken identity. He also alleged that his wife and young son have received threats of murder and kidnapping. He claimed to have received more than 10,000 messages and phone calls. Neighbours say the man in the video is not Honey Dagar Dainik Bhaskar also spoke to Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) leader Sanjeev Chaudhary and several shopkeepers in Honey's neighbourhood. They said the Honey Dagar identified on social media is not the same person who appears in the viral video. According to them, Honey owns and operates a gym in the area and commutes daily from Chhajjupur village in Meerut, returning home each night. A nearby shopkeeper, speaking on condition of anonymity, said groups of young men have been repeatedly visiting the area looking for Honey. He said the gym remains closed because of fears that someone could vandalise the premises or physically attack him.

Researchers found that this trait is instinctive, evident even in their initial flower interactions. By aligning a dominant eye with a favored proboscis side, these insects streamline complex feeding tasks, showcasing a remarkable adaptation that enables problem-solving with a small brain.

stories.title: Around 1200 BCE, major Mediterranean civilisations began collapsing; scientists have now reconstructed the climate conditions surrounding the crisis

Drought acted as a threat multiplier, worsening existing societal challenges. Warfare and invasions interacted with environmental stress during this period. Understanding past climate pressures informs our view of societal vulnerability.

stories.title: 200 years after the first dinosaur, scientists use brain scans on a 100-million-year-old snake fossil from Brazil
stories.summary: Palaeontology has transformed from examining fossil fragments to digitally reconstructing ancient creatures. A new Cretaceous snake fossil from Brazil showcases this remarkable scientific advancement. High-resolution micro-CT scanning revealed the snake's brain anatomy and lifestyle. This technology allows detailed comparisons across millions of years of evolution. Modern methods are reshaping our understanding of prehistoric life's diversity.

The Great Pyramid was not built by slaves, but by paid workers who drank beer and ate meat.
stories.summary: Modern archaeology says that pyramid builders were not slaves but a respected workforce. These workers lived in a dedicated town and received good food and medical care. Their diet included meat, bread, and beer, ensuring strength for their labor. Burial in tombs near the pyramids honoured their significant contribution to ancient Egypt.

stories.title: In 1992, Hurricane Andrew may have helped giant Burmese pythons spread across Florida's Everglades, creating one of America's worst invasive species crises

'MPs sleeping, need wake-up call': Delhi transport bodies plan Parliament march on August 4 against E20 fuel
stories.summary: Delhi transport groups will march to Parliament on August 4. They demand the withdrawal of ethanol-blended petrol from the market. Concerns about vehicle problems and mileage reduction are being raised. The government defends the E20 fuel program as safe and beneficial. This protest aims to highlight issues with the mandated fuel blend.

stories.title: One of the world's largest rodents was imported for fur farming in North America; today it's devastating wetlands and riverbanks across US
stories.summary: Nutria, large rodents introduced for fur farming, now infest forty US states and Canada. These prolific breeders destroy vital wetland vegetation and agricultural crops like rice. Their burrowing weakens levees and dams, posing risks to infrastructure and public safety. Eradication efforts involve trapping, detection dogs, and bounty programs to control populations. These invasive creatures have caused millions of dollars in damage across affected regions.

stories.title: Researchers made flying harder for Alaskan Seabirds; only 67% returned, survivors bred better
stories.summary: Researchers clipped a few wing and tail feathers of wild black-legged kittiwakes in Alaska to make flying more energy-intensive and tracked them for several years. The birds struggled to raise chicks during that breeding season, and fewer survived to return the next year. However, those that did return migrated farther and were more likely to breed successfully, showing how energy spent in one season can affect the next.

stories.title: Joni Mitchell’s former Malibu home is listed for $27 million; its beachfront pool may be impossible to recreate today
stories.summary: Joni Mitchell's former Malibu Colony home is listed for twenty-seven million dollars. This oceanfront property features a rare beachfront swimming pool and spa. The residence offers five bedrooms and five bathrooms with direct beach access. Its Cape Cod-inspired architecture maximizes natural light and ocean views. The home highlights Malibu's evolving luxury housing market and coastal regulations.

stories.title: Rock shelter in Spain preserves the stories from hunting to farming around 8,000 years ago
'Govt breaching deal ... will protest again': CJP gives Centre ultimatum amid ongoing police action
Paris knife attack: Man arrested after three women stabbed near Porte de Clichy
stories.summary: A man was arrested after stabbing three women near Paris's Porte de Clichy on Monday. One victim, believed to be pregnant, is in critical condition after the attack. The 31-year-old suspect, who reportedly has mental health issues, was apprehended at the scene. Police found two knives in the possession of the arrested individual. An investigation into the incident has been officially opened by authorities.

stories.title: Why US strikes on Hormuz suddenly stopped despite Trump's bluster
Elon Musk says a future on Mars could help humanity survive pandemics, AI and global disasters
stories.summary: Elon Musk believes a Mars colony can protect humanity from global disasters. He argues the vast distance offers a crucial buffer against pandemics and cyber threats. A six-month journey to Mars acts as an automatic quarantine period for diseases. Digital attacks also face significant delays, providing time for mitigation efforts. This expansion ensures human civilization is not solely confined to one planet.

Ram Temple donation 'theft' case: SC tells SIT to submit status report within 2 weeks
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has directed the Special Investigation Team to submit a status report. This report concerns the alleged theft of offerings at the Ayodhya Ram Temple. The court issued this direction while hearing petitions seeking a court-monitored investigation. The Uttar Pradesh government will add a forensic auditor to the SIT. This SIT currently comprises three IPS officers.

stories.title: 'It does not end in darkness': Sonam Wangchuk visits Rajghat, congratulates youth on protest
This California river once carried thousands of salmon every year. A 1942 dam changed it forever, and scientists are still trying to bring them back
stories.summary: Friant Dam construction in 1942 altered the San Joaquin River, impacting salmon populations. A 2006 settlement agreement initiated restoration efforts for the river and its fish. The program aims to reestablish spring-run Chinook salmon while managing water for agriculture. Multiple agencies collaborate on scientific research and habitat improvements for the river. Monitoring tracks progress and guides adjustments for long-term ecological recovery.

stories.title: They bought this Laguna Beach home for $16 million and spent $20 million rebuilding it. It is now listed for $112 million
stories.summary: A Laguna Beach oceanfront estate is now on the market for $112 million. The owners invested $20 million to extensively renovate the property over two years. This remarkable residence spans 14,400 square feet and includes six bedrooms. The owners are selling as they have relocated and no longer need the large home. This listing aims to set a new residential sales record for Orange County.

stories.title: Syngenta will stop selling paraquat in Australia after strict new safety rules, but generic versions of the controversial herbicide will remain available
stories.summary: Syngenta is ceasing paraquat sales in Australia after new safety regulations were introduced. This decision impacts product choice and market stability for Australian farmers. Generic paraquat will remain available, but Syngenta's exit raises supply concerns. New rules aim to reduce exposure risks for workers and the environment. Growers must now adapt to stricter conditions and potential market shifts.

stories.title: Pangolin collected in 1836 sat unnoticed in a museum until its DNA revealed a new species
Govt mulls PM Surya Ghar 2.0 with battery storage, shared rooftop solar
Logan Paul releases new limited-edition PRIME bottle honoring Oliver Tree's legacy
stories.summary: Logan Paul has launched a limited-edition version of PRIME inspired by Oliver Tree, with every dollar earned going to the late musician's foundation. The initiative honors the late singer and supports grants for young artists. It also carries forward Tree's vision of helping creators bring their ideas to life through hands-on artistic projects.

stories.title: MEA summons Ukraine ambassador after attack on ship with 4 Indians on board
'No one can change his decision': Karnataka minister Yathindra says father Siddaramaiah 'firm' on skipping 2028 polls
stories.summary: Yathindra Siddaramaiah confirmed his father's decision to retire from electoral politics. He stated that once his father makes a firm decision, no one can change it. The senior leader is prioritizing his health as he approaches eighty years old. He will remain actively involved in politics and champion vulnerable sections. Siddaramaiah previously announced the 2023 elections would be his last contest.

stories.title: Meet Nehemiah Turner: The 11-year-old Florida boy who spent more than 100 hours reading to shelter animals and changed countless lives by helping anxious pets find forever homes
Kapil Sibal challenges anti-defection law: SC to examine tenth schedule merger rule
Hamptons Mansion Auction Set: Libbie Mugrabi estate faces $11m court sale; experts warn on equity hit
stories.summary: Socialite Libbie Mugrabi's luxury Bridgehampton mansion is set to be sold in a rare court-ordered public auction after repeated attempts to sell the property privately failed. The auction follows a legal dispute over an unpaid $3.5 million loan secured against the estate. The property, originally listed for $25 million and later reduced to $19 million, will open for bidding at $11 million on August 28.

stories.summary: Majuro, capital of the Republic of Marshall Islands, confronts severe threats from rising sea levels. Coastal erosion accelerates due to increased wind speeds and human interference. Adaptation measures like sea walls and land raising are being considered by policymakers. However, migration may become a last resort for the Marshallese people.

stories.title: CRPF to conduct 'professional post-event assessment' of RAF action at student protests
stories.summary: The CRPF will conduct a professional post-event assessment of RAF actions. This review follows the conclusion of student protests and dispersal of demonstrators. Opposition MPs have raised concerns over alleged police brutality against students. Reports suggest AK-47 rifles were used against protesters in Bihar. The Union Education Minister has resigned amid sustained student demonstrations.

stories.title: 'Rajghat, then back to the mountains': Sonam Wangchuk discharged from Medanta Hospital
stories.summary: Sonam Wangchuk has been discharged from Medanta Hospital after his hunger strike. He will now visit Rajghat to honour Mahatma Gandhi before returning home. Wangchuk led a 26-day hunger strike demanding the education minister's resignation. The protest concluded after successful talks between the CJP and the Centre. Dharmendra Pradhan later resigned, and Pralhad Joshi was appointed as the new minister.

stories.title: A 95-year-old CEO bought a bankrupt furniture store for $80,000 in 1975, then quietly built an $858 million business and gave millions away

stories.summary: The US government seeks land for a border wall near Mount Cristo Rey. This sacred site is a pilgrimage destination for thousands of faithful people. The Roman Catholic Diocese of Las Cruces opposes the land acquisition and wall construction. Church officials argue the wall infringes upon religious freedom and desecrates the holy place. A legal battle is underway as the government pursues eminent domain for the project.

stories.title: Baby goat falls after suddenly freezing mid-jump; an inherited muscle condition explains why
stories.summary: Fainting goats do not actually faint. Also known as myotonic goats, they have a rare inherited muscle condition called myotonia congenita that causes their muscles to become temporarily stiff when they are startled. The breed is valued for its heavy muscling, meat production, strong maternal instincts and ability to thrive on forage-based farming, making it much more than its unusual behaviour.

stories.title: First puffin chick in 30 years just emerged from England's south coast after 15 weeks of careful monitoring, giving new hope to the country's last mainland colony

Quote of the day by Dave Bautista: "I'm a poor kid from the streets. What I've been able to achieve has really just been through hard work and…" - an inspiring lesson on resilience, self-belief and turning adversity into achievement
stories.summary: Dave Bautista highlights his humble beginnings and the hard work behind his success. He stresses that personal circumstances do not dictate future achievements. Bautista faced significant rejection before finding acting roles in Hollywood. His career shift from wrestling to acting took considerable time and effort. The actor encourages pursuing dreams despite obstacles and doubts.

Gandhi questioned Prime Minister Modi's promises regarding student FIRs. He stated that pellet guns were fired at students in Delhi. The Congress leader demanded an apology and action against attackers.

stories.title: Kai Cenat announces first livestream with Tyla since she friend-zoned him on stream
stories.summary: Popular streamer Kai Cenat will livestream with South African singer Tyla again soon. This marks their first stream together since a viral 2024 moment. Tyla politely declined Kai's date request, becoming a popular internet meme. Fans anticipate their reunion, wondering if they will reference the past event. Both artists have achieved significant success in their respective careers.

stories.title: 'Former minister will be exposed': Vijay-led Tamil Nadu govt on DMK 'corruption' audit report
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu's finance minister will present an audit report on corruption during the previous DMK regime. This report will expose alleged irregularities in the collection of party funds. The minister also reiterated the government's commitment to abolishing the NEET exam. He stated that a permanent solution for the exam is being actively planned. The first budget of the new government will be presented on August 5.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Queen Elizabeth: "When life seems hard, the courageous do not lie down and accept defeat; instead, they…" - a timeless lesson on courage, perseverance and hope in difficult times
stories.summary: Queen Elizabeth II's 2008 Christmas broadcast offered wisdom on facing life's difficulties. She stated that courageous individuals struggle for a better future instead of accepting defeat. This perspective highlights that courage involves refusing to let fear or pain dictate actions. Staying determined after setbacks keeps future possibilities open, which is more important than immediate wins. Hope is an active pursuit, requiring effort to achieve improvements rather than passive wishing.

DMK demands immediate NEET ban, seeks probe into Jantar Mantar violence
stories.summary: The DMK party is demanding an immediate nationwide ban on the NEET medical entrance examination. MP TR Baalu submitted an adjournment motion notice in the Lok Sabha seeking this ban. This demand follows a NEET UG paper leak and student protests across the nation. The DMK also called for an inquiry into the alleged use of weapons against students.

stories.summary: Complaints were filed against former Bangladesh President Mohammed Shahabuddin on Sunday. These allegations concern crimes against humanity during the 2024 uprising against the government. Shahabuddin resigned from his presidential post on Friday citing health complications. The home minister stated the allegations do not warrant consideration by the tribunal. However, the law minister confirmed Shahabuddin will face a corruption probe.

stories.summary: The government allowed student protests and focused on conducting the NEET re-examination promptly. Culprits involved in paper leaks were arrested and brought before the judicial process. A timely re-examination prevented a year's academic disruption for students. Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned after the successful re-examination process. India also faces inflation risks from external and internal factors this year.

stories.title: PM Modi hails youth for taking India to arenas once beyond reach
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised young Indians for recent achievements. PV Sindhu won the Japan Open badminton title, making the nation proud. India's first privately developed orbital rocket, Vikram-1, also achieved a successful launch. Students excelled in international science Olympiads, securing numerous medals. These accomplishments demonstrate the nation's confident and capable young generation.

India saw more than 5,000 child adoptions last year, highest in a decade
stories.summary: India saw a record 5,022 children adopted between April 2025 and March 2026. Domestic adoptions accounted for 4,603 children, while inter-country adoptions numbered 419. Special needs children adoption increased by twenty-five percent, reaching 392 last year. Adoptions of girls also rose by eight percent, continuing past trends. Relative and step-parent adoptions saw a significant fifty percent increase.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Slavoj Žižek: 'The problem for us is not are our desires satisfied or not...'
stories.summary: Navigating modern life leaves many of us unclear about our true aspirations. The myriad choices presented by society can cloud our vision, making it hard to identify what we genuinely seek. Often, external factors influence our perceived goals, leading us to chase after things that don’t resonate with us. To find real fulfillment, we must delve into the origins of our desires and distinguish them from borrowed ambitions.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Thucydides: 'Self-control is the chief element in self-respect, and...'
stories.summary: Self-control is the foundation of self-respect, which ultimately nurtures genuine courage. Archidamus II of Sparta championed patience as a virtue over the urge for instant conflict. In Ancient Greece, ideas like sophrosyne highlighted the importance of achieving balance through self-mastery. In our fast-paced modern world, we often feel pressured to act impulsively. Cultivating self-discipline can enhance our decision-making capabilities across various situations.

stories.summary: Innovative Chinese scientists introduced a self-cloning hybrid rice system that ensures impressive yields while allowing farmers to reuse seeds. This groundbreaking method cuts down on the need for yearly seed purchases, significantly lowering production costs for agricultural operations worldwide. Consequently, this advancement plays a crucial role in enhancing food security on both national and global scales, promising to bolster China's agricultural strength.

stories.summary: Famous TikToker Sara Gilson died after her estranged husband allegedly killed her. Police believe Jeremiah Duffey shot Sara before taking his own life. stories.summary: In Calgary, invasive Prussian carp are infiltrating the stormwater system, creating a serious threat to local ecology. These fish breed swiftly, endangering aquatic life and city infrastructure. Simultaneously, encounters with elk in Canadian parks are becoming more perilous than those with bears due to their massive size and unpredictable behavior, prompting authorities to implement management strategies to confront both wildlife conflicts and invasive species.

His venture quickly attracted a large social media following and a multitude of clients, particularly during a tough summer job market for teens. stories.title: Opposition to take on government in Parliament over police action against protesting student
stories.summary: Opposition parties will strongly raise police action against protesting students in Parliament. Rahul Gandhi demanded accountability from Home Minister Amit Shah regarding the incident. He questioned the use of lethal force and deployment of plainclothes personnel. The INDIA bloc will finalize its strategy for parliamentary discussions on Monday. Opposition leaders are calling for a judicial commission to investigate the alleged assault.

Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu proposed banning young children from social media. The discussion highlights differing views on digital platform usage for youth.

'No responsibilities': Mohan Bhagwat on live-in relationships; says marriage 'instils dharma'
stories.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat discussed marriage as a discipline instilling dharma. He noted live-in relationships as a modern alternative with consequences. Bhagwat also welcomed modernity while calling live-in relationships a blind imitation. He stressed that LGBTQ people are part of society and should be accepted. Elders should practice mobile discipline and engage in family conversations.

stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a high-powered task force for examination reforms. This move follows recent irregularities in national entrance examinations like NEET-UG. The Congress party criticized the initiative as an attempt to repair the Prime Minister's image. The government aims to establish a foolproof examination system through this task force. Recommendations from a previous committee have yet to be fully implemented.

stories.title: From Jantar Mantar to Parliament: Govt, opposition brace for fight over NEET row, other issues
stories.summary: As the monsoon session reconvenes, tensions rise again over the NEET-UG paper leak scandal. Opposition factions are determined to maintain pressure on the administration following significant protests. Prime Minister Modi has introduced reforms for examinations and established a dedicated task force for student welfare. In response, Rahul Gandhi is targeting the government over police conduct. The government aims to introduce a bill designed to eradicate malpractice in examinations.

stories.title: CDSCO cancels 7 clinical trial ethics panels over serious violations
stories.summary: India's drug regulator cancelled seven Ethics Committee registrations nationwide. Inspections revealed serious violations of clinical trial rules and guidelines. These committees oversee participant rights and safety during medical studies. The action followed a thorough compliance assessment and review process. This move ensures better adherence to regulatory standards for drug trials.

stories.summary: High-powered task force to recommend tech-driven, leak-proof reforms for NTA and public exams.

stories.summary: Opposition parties will intensify their Parliament attack on the government. They are demanding Home Minister Amit Shah's resignation over police action. This action involved students protesting the NEET paper leak issue. The government is also set to introduce amendments to the anti-paper leak law. Questions are also being raised about a key higher education secretary appointment.

stories.title: Infosys co-founder, Aadhaar architect: Who is Nandan Nilekani, set to lead high-powered exam reforms task force
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a high-powered task force for examination reforms. Nandan Nilekani, Infosys co-founder, will lead this important government initiative. The task force includes prominent figures from ISRO and IIT Madras. This development follows recent student protests and a minister's resignation. The government aims to address broader reforms within the education sector.

stories.title: The Chinese bahaba, a critically endangered fish was missing from Hong Kong for over a decade
stories.summary: A recent study has confirmed the presence of the rare Chinese bahaba in Hong Kong's waters through genetic material extracted from seawater. Nicknamed the 'Panda of the Sea,' this critically endangered fish had evaded scientific capture for over ten years. Researchers utilized cutting-edge environmental DNA technology, revealing traces of the fish's DNA across various western bays, thereby advancing non-invasive methods for marine population monitoring and conservation.

stories.title: Ex-Isro chief, IIT director & more: Who is on Nandan Nilekani-led NTA exam reforms panel
