stories.summary: Nestled in Salmon, Idaho, a captivating pirate-themed house is on the market for $799,000, boasting a remarkable annual income of around $80,000 from its Airbnb bookings. The property stands out amidst a collection of luxurious and historic homes detailed in market reports. Economic shifts are shaping the landscape of luxury real estate, with affluent baby boomers opting for more spacious residences as they transition into retirement.

stories.title: PM Modi returns with message to students, announces Nandan Nilekani-led task force on exam reforms
Romania shoots down third suspected Russian drone in three days, summons Moscow's envoy
stories.summary: Romania shot down a drone entering its airspace over the Black Sea. This marked the third such interception in as many days. President Nicusor Dan condemned these repeated violations as intolerable and unacceptable. Romania summoned the Russian ambassador to protest these airspace breaches. Investigations are ongoing into the drone incidents and border tensions are high.

'Govt-ordered probe an eyewash': Tripura Congress MLA demands judicial inquiry into DGP Anurag Dhankar's death
stories.summary: Tripura Congress MLA Sudip Roy Barman reiterated the party's demand for a judicial probe. He cited unnatural circumstances surrounding the death of state DGP Anurag Dhankar. The MLA called the government's investigation an eyewash and alleged the DGP faced issues. He expressed disappointment over the high court's lack of suo motu action. The officer had previously investigated the Nirav Modi fraud case.

stories.title: Slash-and-burn farming was blamed for destroying rainforests, but a study something different
stories.summary: In various small communities, unwritten agreements are crucial for sustainable land management. These norms not only restrict deforestation, fostering forest regeneration, but also bolster biodiversity by allowing flora and fauna to thrive. Research highlights the effectiveness of these traditions in safeguarding forest health over time. It is essential for policymakers to support and uphold these local practices for robust environmental conservation.

stories.title: These fish are born female & later become male; fishing may be changing them at molecular level
stories.summary: A new study has found that heavy fishing may be changing pearly razorfish at the molecular level. Researchers found no major changes in the fish's DNA but discovered differences in DNA methylation, an epigenetic process that affects how genes work. The study also found that marine reserves help preserve larger, older fish and maintain higher genetic diversity.

stories.title: From Chita Andolan to Jal Satyagrahas: Why the Ken-Betwa project has upset MP tribals

stories.summary: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan expressed concern over shrinking public space for dissent in India. He noted that courts often grant relief belatedly and impose restrictive bail conditions. These conditions can discourage citizens from exercising their fundamental right to express views. Justice Bhuyan cited cases where individuals faced prolonged jail time for minor offenses. He stressed the need for critical examination of judicial decisions to improve the system.

stories.title: Beyond Tigers: The wildlife trade fuelled by pets and myths
stories.summary: Wildlife trafficking has moved from physical markets to online platforms. This shift impacts lesser-known species like shikras and slow lorises. Recent enforcement operations have recovered protected animals and birds. These seizures highlight a conservation crisis often overlooked by the public. Demand for exotic pets and traditional beliefs fuels this illegal trade.

stories.title: Five novelty chocolates recalled across Britain over undeclared milk and soya allergens
stories.summary: The UK Food Standards Agency has recalled several Bon Bons Wholesale chocolate products because they contain undeclared milk and soya. People with allergies to either ingredient are advised not to eat the chocolates and should return them to the store for a full refund. The recall covers products sold across England, Scotland and Wales.

stories.title: PM Modi pitches water conservation amid widespread monsoon deficit
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi urged water conservation efforts through the 'catch the rain' campaign. He asked citizens to take responsibility for local water bodies and save every drop. The nation faces a significant monsoon rainfall deficit, impacting water availability. However, improved rains are expected next week in northwest India and eastern regions. Despite potential improvements, July is still projected to end with a countrywide deficit.

stories.title: Baby crib sent flying, 800,000 flee: Typhoon Noul hits China; scary visuals emerge
stories.summary: Typhoon Noul made landfall in southern China's Guangdong province early Sunday. More than 800,000 people were relocated to safer areas in Guangdong. Hong Kong experienced significant transport chaos with hundreds of flights cancelled. Dramatic videos of the storm's impact quickly went viral on social media. The typhoon weakened inland but heavy rain threats continue through Tuesday.

stories.title: 'This is a new subject for me': Pralhad Joshi after taking charge as education minister

The government says the changes are intended to address administrative and legal gaps, while critics question the breadth of the proposed powers.

She suggested the Uttar Pradesh chief minister should learn from the Jantar Mantar protests. Mufti stated destroying the learning institution displays hatred and vengeance against students. Akhilesh Yadav also joined students protesting to save Jauhar University from demolition. The Samajwadi Party demanded the BJP halt the demolition, citing potential harm to students.

stories.title: 'PM Modi's apology awaited': Opposition to keep up NEET protest pressure in Parliament
stories.summary: Opposition parties will continue their Parliament pressure regarding alleged police brutality against students. Rahul Gandhi has demanded accountability from Home Minister Amit Shah for the protest actions. The INDIA bloc will finalize its strategy on the anti-paper leak bill soon. This proposed legislation aims to increase penalties for examination-related unfair means. The Congress seeks an apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the alleged atrocities.

stories.summary: Addressing reporters, Kishor said the movement had gone beyond political affiliations and demonstrated that public mobilisation could force those in power to respond."This is the beginning of accountability. Accountability is being enforced under public pressure. I always say that in this country, the opposition party can be weak. The opposition cannot be weak," he said.

stories.summary: A river restoration project in Somerset, UK, has shown major benefits within a year of completion. By reconnecting the River Aller with its floodplain, researchers found reduced flood peaks, cleaner water, higher groundwater levels and a sharp rise in wetland habitat. The restored landscape has also attracted more wildlife, including fish, birds and water voles.

stories.title: 'Don't cry later': Owaisi makes alliance offer to Akhilesh to oust BJP in UP polls
stories.summary: During a rally in Moradabad, the Hyderabad Lok Sabha MP said he was ready to "join hands" or "form alliance" with Samajwadi Party, which would be cautious with the offer as both parties reach out to same voter base in the 403-seat assembly. Brushing off the BJP's "B-team" tag, Owaisi said he doesn't want BJP to continue in power for the third straight term in the state given that Samajwadi Party ties up with AIMIM to avoid the split of votes.

stories.title: Assam floods: Death toll reaches 66; BJP launches Rs 12 crore relief drive - top developments
stories.summary: Assam's flood death toll has reached sixty-six people as the situation shows improvement. Over six lakh people remain affected across six districts, while water levels are receding. The state BJP has initiated a twelve crore rupee relief campaign for flood-hit families. This campaign aims to provide clothing to two lakh women and children. An inter-ministerial central team has arrived to assess the extensive flood damage.

He claimed these individuals were not students and may have foreign backing. The violence occurred during a protest concerning the alleged NEET question paper leak. Media personnel were reportedly targeted during the clashes with security forces. The state government invoked its anti-goonda law against those accused of orchestrating the violence.

Researchers say this shared frequency creates a clearer listening range, helping bats detect prey more effectively despite many overlapping calls from nearby colony members.

His father bravely intervened, and bystanders assisted until emergency services arrived. The incident resulted in the loss of Brodie's dominant right hand and a long recovery period. stories.summary: Monsoon illnesses often present with symptoms similar to common viral fevers. Overlapping symptoms and diagnostic infrastructure gaps delay timely detection of these diseases. Vector-borne illnesses like dengue and chikungunya surge during the rainy season. Climate change and urbanization contribute to year-round breeding habitats for disease vectors. Prompt medical care is crucial for infants and children facing increased monsoon health risks.

Quote of the day by Michael Faraday: 'There's nothing quite as frightening as someone who knows...'
stories.summary: The danger of absolute certainty lies in its ability to stifle necessary discussions and overlook crucial warning signs. Renowned scientist Michael Faraday emphasized the importance of maintaining doubt and curiosity in our thoughts. Psychological studies reveal that a limited understanding can cause individuals to mistakenly inflate their competence. In leadership, rigid mindsets can have disastrous consequences throughout history. Embracing new information and perspectives is essential for our survival.

stories.title: Amid manhunt for J&K cop’s terrorist killers, detentions spike to 3.5k
stories.summary: Detentions across Jammu and Kashmir linked to a terrorist killing have risen significantly. Police have stepped up their crackdown on suspected sympathizers of armed groups in the region. A comprehensive security review meeting focused on the current operational environment and threat perception. Home minister Amit Shah spoke with the slain head constable's son after visiting the family. Chief Minister Omar Abdullah criticized the detentions and controlled explosions targeting terrorist homes.

Amid rain & fresh landslides, Jammu-Srinagar NH closure enters Day 3
stories.summary: Torrential rains have caused fresh landslides across Jammu and Kashmir. The Jammu-Srinagar National Highway remains closed for traffic for a third day. Major pilgrimages, including Amarnath and Vaishno Devi Yatras, are suspended for the sixth consecutive day. Several vehicles are stranded as authorities advise against travel due to safety concerns. Flash floods also affected households in Udhampur district without any casualties.

stories.title: Haryana’s air pollution action plan: Centre suggests strict enforcement and accelerated implementation to curb pollution in a time-bound manner
stories.summary: The Centre reviewed Haryana's air pollution control measures and urged faster implementation. Focus is on stubble burning, industrial pollution, and road dust reduction. Efforts will accelerate EV adoption and manage legacy waste effectively. Information campaigns and farmer training will promote crop residue management. Strict enforcement and coordination are critical for cleaner air.

SK Group chairman Chey Tae-won ordered to pay ex-wife Roh Soh-yeong $644M in divorce settlement

'Thank you, friends': PM Modi hails 'love, support' of youth in new Insta video
In the 1980s, Scotland planted commercial trees across parts of a 9,000-year-old peatland
stories.summary: The ancient peatlands of Scotland are undergoing a significant restoration, which addresses the detrimental effects caused by tree planting. Conservationists are diligently working to eliminate commercial trees, aiming to enhance wildlife habitats and maintain stored carbon levels. This notable effort is primarily focused on the Flow Country, a treasure trove of wetlands recognized as a World Heritage Site for its global ecological importance.

Grain, not guns: MEA rejects Russia's claim on deadly ship attack that killed 4 Indians
stories.summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs stated the MV Golden Leo carried grain, not weapons. This contradicts Russia's assertion regarding the ship's cargo and its attack. The vessel's tragic incident resulted in the deaths of four Indian seafarers. India reiterated its concerns to Russia's foreign minister during a recent meeting. Attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers are unacceptable under any circumstances.

Three chemical parks to be set up under BHAVYA-Rasayan scheme
stories.summary: The Union Cabinet approved the BHAVYA-Rasayan scheme for three dedicated chemical parks. This initiative has a financial outlay of Rs 3,030 crore for infrastructure development. The scheme will run for five years, promoting chemical industry growth and competitiveness. It aims to create an environment-friendly ecosystem with centralized waste management facilities. This development is expected to generate employment and contribute to economic growth.

stories.title: Government pushes competition in power distribution
Scientists discover a 17-million-year-old ape fossil in Egypt that could rewrite early ape evolution
stories.summary: A new fossil ape named Masripithecus was found in northern Egypt. This discovery suggests northeastern Africa played a larger role in early ape evolution. Previously, East Africa was considered the primary region for ape diversification. The Masripithecus fossil fills a geographical and evolutionary gap in scientific understanding. This find expands the map of early hominoid origins beyond East Africa.

'Have a heart': Sonam Wangchuk's wife slams critics after he ends 26-day hunger strike
stories.summary: Gitanjali Angmo defended her husband Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike conclusion. He ended his 26-day fast after prolonged negotiations with Union ministers. Wangchuk stated the decision aimed to prevent potential violence across the nation. Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janata Party vows to continue its peaceful protests. They demand the education minister's resignation over the alleged NEET paper leak.

In 2015, trees covered just 1.9% of these Ethiopian drylands; nine years later...
stories.summary: In a span of nine years, Ethiopia's drylands have observed significant forest expansion alongside a reduction in soil erosion. The practices of assisted natural regeneration and active tree planting have been pivotal in enhancing forest density. As a result, severe topsoil loss in the mountainous terrain has meaningfully diminished. These outcomes resonate with Ethiopia's ecological objectives and green economy initiatives, underscoring practical approaches for restoring ravaged communal landscapes.

stories.title: Ravneet Singh Bittu resigns from Union Council of Ministers; President Murmu accepts resignation
stories.summary: President Droupadi Murmu accepted Ravneet Singh Bittu's resignation from the Union Council of Ministers. Bittu, a former Congress MP, joined the BJP earlier this year. He was inducted as a minister of state in June despite losing his election. Bittu is a grandson of former Punjab chief minister Beant Singh. His resignation's reason was not immediately announced by officials.

stories.title: Korean professor who got his students to write a research paper for his daughter's admission to a top dental school sent to jail for 3.6 years
RSS women's wing kicks off three-day national meet in Haryana
stories.summary: Rashtriya Sevika Samiti began its national executive meeting in Haryana with 500 representatives attending. The organization reviewed its past year's activities and service projects across the country. Volunteers organized various initiatives including training camps and social harmony interactions. Recent highlights included a route march in West Bengal and a conference in Delhi. The meeting continues until July 26, focusing on women's empowerment and nation-building efforts.

stories.title: PM Modi gains 1 million Instagram followers overnight after selfie video amid NEET protest
Trinamool Congress appoints Saugata Roy as Lok Sabha deputy leader after Satabdi Roy joins rebel camp
North Carolina to hold first Elk hunt In 2027 after rebuilding herd over 25 years
stories.summary: North Carolina will allow its first elk hunt in 2027, 25 years after reintroducing the species. Only two hunting permits will be issued through an auction and raffle, with proceeds supporting elk conservation. Wildlife officials say the population is now sustainable, while some local residents remain divided over whether hunting should begin.

stories.title: Seattle's 'Emerald City' from space: How glaciers and people shaped its landscape
stories.summary: Ancient glaciers sculpted Seattle's hills and valleys thousands of years ago. Humans later reshaped this terrain through extensive engineering projects. The city's development is closely tied to its numerous waterways and coastlines. These natural and man-made features create the distinctive "Emerald City" landscape. Nasa's image reveals this combined geological and engineering history.

stories.title: Why the world is coming to India for medical treatment — and not just because it is cheaper
stories.summary: India's medical tourism market is experiencing significant growth, projected to reach $16.2 billion by 2030. Patients are increasingly choosing India for its affordable and high-quality medical treatments. Digital advancements and government initiatives are further enhancing the medical travel ecosystem. International patients praise the convenience, speed, and professional care received in India. Continued collaboration will solidify India's position as a global medical destination.

stories.title: 1,600-year-old Roman guardian spirit found beneath ancient fort in northern England
stories.summary: At Vindolanda fort, archaeologists have made an exciting discovery: a sandstone carving of a Roman guardian spirit, estimated to be 1,600 years old. This striking relief depicts a genius, symbolising the protective spirit revered by the soldiers. Such archaeological finds deepen our understanding of the spiritual lives and beliefs of Roman forces stationed at this military stronghold, adding to the fort's historical narrative.

stories.title: Southwest flight attendant detained by ICE at work: 'Yes, came legally but why didn't he leave?'

Google co-founder Sergey Brin turned his $450 million superyacht into a floating headquarters with an entire deck dedicated to work
stories.summary: Google co-founder Sergey Brin's superyacht Dragonfly features a dedicated business deck. This vessel combines luxury with functionality, reflecting his entrepreneurial approach. The yacht includes a private office and helicopter hangar for global business management. Brin's increased involvement in AI development mirrors this work-centric design. Dragonfly reimagines the superyacht as a mobile and productive workspace.

How four Moose released in 1904 ended up reshaping Newfoundland's forests forever
stories.summary: A century after just four moose were released in Newfoundland to attract hunters, the introduced animals transformed the island's forests and wildlife management. Their population grew to nearly 200,000 before habitat damage triggered declines. A new management plan explains how science is now helping keep moose numbers in balance with forests, public safety and long-term ecosystem health.

stories.title: 'There are Chinese projects on territories in J&K that belong to India': MEA objects to illegal occupation
stories.summary: Ministry of External Affairs accused China of violating sovereignty and illegally occupying Indian territories. The government objected to Chinese projects in Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. This statement follows a meeting between Indian and Chinese foreign ministers. Chinese officials highlighted positive developments in bilateral relations and cooperation. Both nations aim to maintain peace and explore coexistence as major powers.

Instagram vs WhatsApp: How CJP protests are different and why that matters
stories.summary: Sonam Wangchuk ended his hunger strike after government assurances on paper leaks. The government promised fast-track courts and tougher punishments for offenders. New education secretaries were appointed, signaling bureaucratic shifts. The CJP protest utilized social media, challenging traditional political communication. This youth movement forced a direct intervention from Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

CJP students protest: RAF probes excessive force, pellet gun charges in July 20 crackdown
stories.summary: The Rapid Action Force is verifying its personnel's actions during recent student protests. Allegations of excessive force and pellet gun use are being examined by officials. The Central Reserve Police Force is overseeing this internal review process. Videos showing clashes and alleged attacks on personnel are under scrutiny. This verification follows student demands for the education minister's resignation.

stories.title: 'Anna part two': Congress MP accuses Wangchuk of striking a deal with govt; BJP hits back
stories.summary: Congress MP Imran Masood accused activist Sonam Wangchuk of striking a deal with the government. He compared Wangchuk to Anna Hazare, suggesting future silence from the activist. The Bharatiya Janata Party criticized Congress for stooping low and insulting the climate activist. Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike after negotiations with Union ministers. Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janata Party continues protests demanding a minister's resignation.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Oprah Winfrey: 'If you look at what you have in life, you'll always have more. If you look at what you don't have in life, you'll never have enough'
stories.summary: Oprah Winfrey emphasizes the profound impact of gratitude on our fulfillment in life. By centering our attention on what we possess, we cultivate a sense of satisfaction and contentment. In stark contrast, fixating on what's lacking breeds an endless cycle of dissatisfaction. In a world where constant comparison is prevalent, embracing our current situation while striving for future goals nurtures a healthier mindset.

stories.title: 'You do whatever you like?' Delhi HC pulls up EC for deploying school teachers for BLO duties during SIR
stories.summary: The Delhi high court questioned the Election Commission regarding teacher deployments. The court sought legal authority for compelling teachers to perform election duties. The commission cited Article 324 and the Representation of the People Act. Teachers are reportedly engaged during holidays and non-teaching hours. The court questioned the mandatory nature of these election assignments.

stories.title: Quote of the day by John Stuart Mill: 'A person may cause evil to others not only by his actions but by his inaction, and in either case he is justly accountable to them for the injury'
stories.summary: Philosopher John Stuart Mill emphasized the importance of accountability for both actions and inaction. He argued that choosing not to intervene in situations that could prevent harm carries its own set of responsibilities. This principle is particularly relevant in instances of bullying, corruption, or injustice, where those with authority must acknowledge their complicity. Mill's insightful quote challenges us to embrace moral responsibility and reflect on the repercussions of our silence.

stories.title: 1,800-year-old Roman camp linked to Marcus Aurelius found in Slovakia
stories.summary: Archaeologists have discovered an approximately 1,800-year-old Roman military camp in southwestern Slovakia that may have been used by Emperor Marcus Aurelius' army during the Marcomannic Wars. The site contains skeletons believed to be Roman soldiers buried in shallow graves, ditches and wells, along with weapons, armour, coins and military sandals. Researchers say the rare discovery could provide new insights into Roman military campaigns, although years of scientific analysis are needed to answer key questions about the soldiers' deaths and the camp's abandonment.

A volunteer shared Duke's story online, which reached a woman nine hours away. This woman instantly decided to adopt Duke, bringing him to his new home. Duke now lives a happy life with a family committed to him.

stories.title: 'Substantial risk of misuse by anti-national elements': Government directs GitHub to take down Bluetooth-based Bitchat app
stories.summary: India's cybercrime center has asked GitHub to remove the Bitchat application. This app allows anonymous, offline messaging which raises security concerns for the government. Officials believe it could be misused by terrorists and criminal groups for coordination. The notice cites potential violations of the Information Technology Act. This action follows the use of similar apps during recent Delhi protests.

Consumers and retailers have been advised not to use, sell, serve or distribute the affected product and to check thetwo affected best-before codes: 01AL2028 and 02AL2028.

Further discussions are scheduled as the NEET paper leak fallout continues.

Ireland has recovered the remains of 99 infants from the former Tuam mother and baby home; DNA analysis may help restore some of their identities
stories.summary: Ireland has recovered ninety-nine infant remains from a former mother and baby home. Forensic excavations are ongoing at the Tuam site, revealing hidden burial chambers. DNA analysis aims to identify the children and restore their identities to families. This effort acknowledges a dark chapter in the country's institutional history. The state is now confronting its past and treating the deceased with dignity.

stories.title: Rare 2,000-year-old Liubo boards found, but the game's rules remain a mystery
stories.summary: Ancient Liubo boards discovered in Han Dynasty tombs shed light on a beloved game that transcended social classes for centuries. Archaeologists have detailed the game's equipment and venues of play, yet the precise rules of Liubo continue to elude scholars, presenting an enduring enigma in the realm of archaeology. The allure of this lost gameplay continues to inspire curiosity.

stories.title: Spain invokes first wildfire emergency as fires rage across Europe; over 10,000 evacuated
stories.summary: Spain declared a national emergency due to widespread wildfires. France requested European Union assistance for a major blaze near Bordeaux. Tens of thousands were evacuated from affected tourist and residential areas. This crisis highlights the intensifying impact of climate change on southern Europe. The region is experiencing record-breaking heat and drought conditions.

The Wadsworth home, purchased in 2018, is now listed for sale. It features five bedrooms and five-and-a-half bathrooms across two acres. Garrett's departure marks a new chapter on the West Coast.

German farmer saves 'gay' sheep from slaughter and uses proceeds to help people flee homophobic persecution
stories.summary: A German farmer rescues gay sheep, which are often discarded by the agricultural industry. His Rainbow Wool project transforms these animals into symbols for animal and human rights. Profits from wool sales and collaborations support the LSVD+ foundation, aiding refugees. This initiative highlights the naturalness of homosexuality and challenges societal prejudices. The project continues its vital work, advocating for acceptance and safety globally.

stories.summary: An alleged paper leak surfaced at Veer Madho Singh Bhandari Uttarakhand Technical University (UTU) on Thursday, prompting the university administration to cancel two B. Tech semester examinations.

stories.title: NYC Upper West Side stabbing: Zohran Mamdani reveals disturbing details of 'hateful' attack
stories.summary: New York City police are investigating two recent stabbings on Manhattan's Upper West Side. Witnesses reported the suspect shouted "Allahu Akbar" during both assaults on victims. Authorities have arrested 51-year-old Raul Morales in connection with these separate incidents. Investigators are examining mental health factors and whether these attacks qualify as hate crimes.

stories.title: Scientists left 'Moon cement' outside the ISS for six months; it came back up to 35% stronger
stories.summary: A pioneering development in space materials, the recently created 'Moon cement' derived from lunar and Martian simulants has shown exceptional durability, surviving for half a year outside the International Space Station unscathed. Remarkably, one formulation achieved a 35% boost in compressive strength over Earth-based counterparts, illuminating promising avenues for constructing habitats on the Moon utilizing local soil resources.

NATO tests giant grass to restore Ukraine's war-damaged soil; may break down explosive residue
stories.summary: Scientists in the Czech Republic are testing giant Miscanthus, a fast-growing perennial grass, to see if it can help restore Ukraine's war-damaged farmland. Backed by a NATO project, the research aims to remove pollutants from contaminated soil, improve soil health and eventually make the land suitable for farming again while producing biomass for renewable energy.

stories.title: 'Reckless': CJI Surya Kant rejects reports of refusing hearing on police action against students
stories.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant denied reports of refusing a petition. He clarified that no formal petition challenging police action was filed. A lawyer had mentioned a letter representation before the court. The clarification came two days after a lawyer mentioned the issue before a bench headed by the CJI and sought an urgent hearing over the alleged use of force against students during the July 20 protest.

'Will monitor throughout the year': SC assures 'institutionalisation' of NEET reforms
stories.summary: ​​A bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe said the affidavit must explain the steps taken to institutionalise the reforms instead of relying on ad hoc measures. Justice Narasimha noted that the deployment of the Indian Air Force (for safe transportation of questions) after the paper leak was only an ad hoc measure and could not be a permanent solution.

stories.title: The Manhattan Project town of Los Alamos now has America's highest share of doctorate holders. Nearly 1 in 5 adults has a PhD and almost 70% hold a bachelor's degree
Jonesboro Spider-Man helps man in wheelchair
stories.summary: A man dressed as Spider-Man assisted a person in a wheelchair crossing a busy road. Christopher Hellenthal, returning from an event, saw the struggle and acted quickly. Traffic cameras captured the swift rescue which unfolded in mere seconds. The video of this real-life heroism quickly went viral online. His spontaneous act of kindness reminded everyone about timely assistance.

stories.title: 2,700-year-old sword found standing upright in a Polish forest may reveal a forgotten Bronze Age ritual
stories.summary: A 2,700-year-old bronze sword was discovered standing upright in a Polish forest. This unusual position suggests deliberate placement, possibly as a ritual offering. The well-preserved blade offers insights into Bronze Age craftsmanship and wealth. Similar discoveries have been made in the Gdańsk forest area before. This find adds significant detail to the region's ancient archaeological record.

stories.title: How Solar Impulse 2 became the first aircraft to complete a 40,000 km fuel-free journey around the world
stories.summary: Solar Impulse 2 completed the first fuel-free flight around the world. The aircraft traveled approximately 40,000 kilometers using only solar energy. It relied on solar cells and onboard batteries to power electric motors. This mission demonstrated advanced engineering and renewable energy capabilities in aviation. The project inspired future developments in electric aircraft technology.

stories.title: Scientists discover a surprising 'brain' hidden inside the heart
stories.summary: A surprising new scientific study has revealed that the heart has a small network of neurons capable of controlling essential bodily functions. The research conducted at Yale University in US, was published in July 2026 in the scientific journal Cell. It revealed that this nervous system participates in regulating heartbeats and also protects the organ during physical or physiological stress situations.

In accordance with the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India’s directions on public demonstrations, you are requested to refrain from participating in or visiting gatherings at or around Jantar Mantar, New Delhi," the University posted on X. ​Earlier, the University of Delhi (DU) has issued an official "safety advisory".

stories.title: 'How dare you threaten students': Rahul Gandhi slams Delhi University over Jantar Mantar advisory
Crackdown on paper leak: Govt planning to tweak anti-cheating law by increasing jail term
stories.summary: In the expected amendment, the government is likely to increase the jail for the offenders from the current 10-year ceiling in the proposed Bill, which the Cabinet will take up this afternoon, sources told TOI. The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 was enacted to curb paper leaks, cheating, and organised malpractices in public examinations like UPSC, SSC, and NTA tests provides for penalties, including up to 10 years in prison and a Rs 1 crore fine.

stories.title: Florida's first underwater habitat in 40 years will soon host scientists
stories.summary: A new underwater habitat has been installed off the Florida Keys coast. This habitat will allow scientists to live and work beneath the ocean for extended periods. It offers a unique opportunity to study human health responses to extreme environments. Research will also focus on coral reef restoration and climate impact assessments. This marks a significant advancement for marine science and human physiology research.

stories.title: In 1938, one radio broadcast made Americans think the world was ending: The incredible true story behind the 'War of the Worlds' panic
stories.summary: A 1938 radio drama adaptation of The War of the Worlds caused confusion among listeners. Many Americans believed they were hearing real news of a Martian invasion. This broadcast highlighted the public's trust in radio as an authoritative information source. Historians question the extent of the widespread panic initially reported. The event remains a significant lesson in media's power to influence public perception.

stories.title: After growing plants in space for years, NASA research could help astronauts grow medicines on demand, starting with tobacco and a harmless virus
Spain total solar eclipse 12 August 2026: Why thousands of eclipse chasers could miss the total solar eclipse
stories.summary: Spain anticipates thousands for a significant 2026 solar eclipse event. The eclipse's late timing near sunset presents unique viewing challenges. Obstacles like trees and hills could block the low-hanging Sun. Careful site selection and elevation are crucial for clear views. This event begins a rare three-year series of eclipses in Spain.

'Trademark arrogance': Sonia Gandhi says Modi govt treated NEET protesters as 'enemies of nation'

"Their demands have been straightforward and to the point: accountability from the Government of India and education reform. The Narendra Modi government has responded to their courage with cowardice and wanton cruelty, treating them not as inheritors of the future but as enemies of the nation," she said.

stories.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi criticised Prime Minister Modi's video message regarding the NEET-UG paper leak. stories.summary: A 2023 photo of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and Sonam Wangchuk resurfaced recently. Wangchuk is now on an indefinite hunger strike seeking accountability for examination irregularities. He previously praised Pradhan's openness to innovative educational ideas. The current protest seeks Pradhan's exit and accountability for the NEET-UG paper leak. This situation presents a sharp contrast to their earlier positive interaction.

stories.title: 'Truck carrying Abhijeet Dipke, Gitanjali, Shabana Azmi, Prakash Raj brutally attacked': CJP accuses Delhi Police of violence
stories.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party alleges police brutality during a recent Parliament march. Protesters claim public figures were assaulted and dragged from a truck. One activist's wife reportedly had her hair pulled during the police action. The group states their volunteer suffered shattered ribs and other injuries. They demand the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan and government dialogue.

stories.title: Kerala merchant navy man dies in Russian strike off Ukraine ahead of wedding
stories.summary: A 26-year-old merchant navy officer from Kerala died after his ship was hit. The cargo vessel was reportedly struck by Russian forces near Odesa. Akhil Joyan was due to marry in two months and was the sole provider. His family is seeking assistance to bring his body home. India condemned the attack on commercial shipping and civilian lives.

stories.title: 'Bound by shared democratic values': PM Modi congratulates Andy Burnham on becoming UK Prime Minister
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated Andy Burnham on his new role. He expressed confidence that India-UK ties will deepen across key sectors. The two nations share democratic values and cooperate widely in many areas. With CETA entering into force, the partnership is poised for growth. Modi looks forward to working closely to strengthen the comprehensive strategic partnership.

stories.title: Sikkim tunnel landslide: Nine dead, several feared trapped as rescue operation continues
stories.summary: At least seven workers have died in a Sikkim tunnel landslide incident. Several other workers are feared trapped inside the under-construction tunnel. Rescue operations are underway by multiple agencies to evacuate those still inside. Authorities suspect around twenty-seven workers were inside when the landslide occurred. The exact cause of the accident is still under investigation by officials.

stories.title: No let-up even after strict punishment for rape: Supreme Court
stories.summary: Awards 20-year jail term to rickshaw puller in 2016 case

stories.title: Quote of the day by Lamine Yamal: "My mother had me at 16, and my father searched for ways to bring food home. That's real pressure. All I have to do is…" - a powerful lesson on perspective, family sacrifice and why football is not the hardest battle his family has faced
stories.summary: Teenage footballer Lamine Yamal shared his perspective on pressure during the World Cup build-up. He contrasted his career with his mother's early parenthood and father's past hardships. Yamal views his demanding football career as a privilege compared to their struggles. This humility places his own challenges within a broader family context. His words offer a powerful reflection on gratitude and perspective beyond the sport.

stories.title: Supreme Court orders new SIT into Ram temple donation theft, will monitor probe
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has taken over the Ayodhya Ram Mandir fund embezzlement investigation. Local police have been removed from the probe, which will now be led by a senior IPS officer. The Shri Ram Teerth Kshetra Trust must preserve all donation receipts and accounts for scrutiny. The court cautioned against politicizing the ongoing investigation into alleged fund pilferage. Eight individuals have already been arrested as the probe progresses impartially.

stories.title: A six-year-old entered an iron lung after polio. More than 70 years later, he had become the world’s longest-known survivor
70 detained, 118 cops and 60 marchers injured: Police block protesters' march to Parliament; JP Nadda meets CJP representatives
stories.summary: A protest by the Cockroach Janta Party demanding a minister's resignation turned chaotic. Protesters clashed with police, resulting in numerous injuries on both sides. Police reported detentions and filed charges related to rioting and assault on public servants. The BJP blamed Left-affiliated student groups for instigating the organized violence. Investigations are underway to establish criminal responsibility for the disturbances.

stories.title: Who is Jelicia Westhoff? Maduka Okoye’s baby mama accuses Nigerian goalkeeper of cheating and abuse amid Cardi B rumours
stories.summary: Jelicia Westhoff has found herself in the spotlight after making a series of serious claims against Maduka Okoye. Her posts appeared shortly after the Nigerian goalkeeper was linked to Cardi B following public sightings in Italy. Here's a closer look at who Westhoff is, her relationship with Okoye, and what led to the latest controversy.

stories.title: Meet Sarah Kendzior: The bestselling author who traded her writing desk for a $17-an-hour garden centre job and found unexpected joy
Mediators propose 10-day truce to revive interim deal: Iran official
stories.summary: Iran received a 10-day ceasefire proposal from mediators to end the ongoing conflict. US strikes on Iranian cities continued for a ninth consecutive night. Iran's Revolutionary Guards attacked US military assets across the region. Two oil tankers exploded after attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz. A vessel was struck by an unknown projectile off Oman's coast.

stories.title: Have demanded extradition of Hasina aide from India: Bangladesh minister
stories.summary: Bangladesh has requested India to extradite former minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal. He fled the country amid the "2024 uprising" against the government. Kamal was sentenced to death for crimes against humanity by a tribunal. Dhaka also expects India to respond to extradition requests for other fugitives. The government stated that Hasina would face legal consequences if she surrenders.

stories.title: J&K floods: Lal Chowk flooded, Amarnath yatra stays suspended
stories.summary: Heavy rainfall inundated Srinagar's Lal Chowk and other city areas on Monday morning. Netizens criticized the government over the drainage system's alleged failure. Officials cited overwhelming rainfall, while critics questioned the Smart City infrastructure project. The Omar Abdullah cabinet previously raised concerns and ordered an external audit. Widespread rain continues across Kashmir, with risks of landslides and flash floods.

stories.title: NC’s Delhi protest draws oppn flak; BJP slams Omar for ignoring floods, PDP asks him to emulate Wangchuk
stories.summary: National Conference held a protest in Delhi seeking statehood restoration. Other parties criticized the party president and chief minister for their absence. BJP stated the government should have been present to manage flood relief efforts. PDP suggested learning from activist Sonam Wangchuk's mobilization efforts. CPM legislator Tarigami expressed full support for the protest's objective.

stories.title: Supreme Court takes exception to meagre compensation for ex-HC judges
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has taken exception to low compensation for retired High Court judges. It asked the Union government to form a committee for uniform guidelines. This committee will consider basic minimum security and services for retired judges. The panel will study issues faced by retired judges and submit recommendations. The goal is to ensure retired judges lead a dignified post-retirement life.

stories.title: No decision on ethanol blending beyond 20%: Govt
stories.summary: The government has stated no decision exists to raise ethanol blending beyond twenty percent. Lower-blended fuel or pure petrol will not be available at select outlets. Any future diesel blending will depend on evaluations and stakeholder consultations. The transition to E20 has been phased and evidence-based, with gradual increases. Claims of vehicle damage from E20 are largely misleading or unsupported by technical evidence.

stories.title: NTA rebuts claims of 5, says NEET-UG OMR sheets forged
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has refuted claims of OMR answer sheet discrepancies from five NEET-UG candidates. Images circulated by these candidates were reportedly digitally altered or regenerated using artificial intelligence. The agency verified the original OMR sheets and scores for all five students involved. These actions follow allegations of swapped OMR sheets and fewer attempted answers than recorded. Candidates submitting fabricated records may face severe penalties under relevant acts.

stories.title: Youth full of aspirations, want country to move forward: PM Modi
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi urged opposition parties to use logic and facts in Parliament. He highlighted India's youth aspirations and recent national achievements. The successful launch of a private space rocket showcased young Indian capabilities. Recent inaugurations and a hydrogen train launch also marked progress. India maintained growth despite global energy supply disruptions.

stories.title: Global urea prices ease after May spike, fall 40% in June
stories.summary: Urea prices fell significantly in June, offering government relief after earlier increases. International urea prices were $572 per tonne, down from May's figures. Other fertilizer prices like diammonium phosphate and potash remained higher than last year. Sulphur prices saw the largest increase, rising 265 percent year-on-year. Domestic urea production exceeded targets, providing comfort for the current season.

stories.title: 1st dengue vaccine gets DCGI nod, set to hit market next year
Who is TheMightyBA? Ludwig remains hopeful despite Streamer University 2026 controversy
stories.summary: TheMightyBA came under fire after his interaction with MeesterKeem at Streamer University 2026. Despite the backlash, Ludwig said he does not believe the 19-year-old creator’s career is over. He said people can change over time and used IShowSpeed as an example of someone who successfully rebuilt his public image through growth and consistency.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi claims PM Modi ‘most anti-youth PM India has seen’
stories.summary: Opposition leaders criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his government's actions. They condemned the crackdown on young protesters marching towards Parliament. Rahul Gandhi called Modi the most anti-youth Prime Minister India has seen. Leaders stated that students are not criminals and their demands are legitimate. The protests highlight widespread discontent regarding examination irregularities and education system issues.

stories.title: Delhi violence not spontaneous, says BJP, blames Left
stories.summary: The BJP has blamed Left-affiliated student groups for protests and violence. Organised groups were also accused of instigating and mobilising crowds. Similar allegations were made regarding the Delhi riots and ongoing legal proceedings. The party stated that the violence did not appear spontaneous and was orchestrated. Investigations will establish criminal responsibility for the real conspirators.

stories.title: Day 1 of Parliament’s monsoon session washed out amid NEET, donation chori protests
stories.summary: The first day of Parliament's monsoon session was disrupted by opposition protests. Opposition parties raised concerns over various issues, including temple donations and exam leaks. Frequent adjournments led to the cancellation of proceedings in both houses. A bill to increase the number of Supreme Court judges was introduced in Lok Sabha. The changed seating arrangement for rebel TMC MPs also drew attention.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Aeschylus: 'When one is wise, it's wisest to seem foolish' and a lesson on strategic survival
Can't force parents to create Apaar IDs for students: Supreme Court
stories.summary: 'Will pass an order to include an 'opt out' option in consent forms'

stories.title: Quote of the Day by Seneca: 'We suffer more often in imagination than in reality'
stories.summary: Seneca, the ancient Stoic philosopher, observed that our imagination often causes us more suffering than actual events. His timeless insight resonates with issues of anxiety faced today. Contemporary research shows our brain struggles to differentiate between real threats and imagined ones. Cognitive Behavioral Therapy leverages this understanding to help individuals challenge distorted thoughts, enabling them to tackle fears more effectively and manage anxiety around potential issues.

stories.title: Supreme Court seeks more exclusive UAPA, NDPS courts to speed up trials
Looksmaxxing creator Hullo reportedly returns to TikTok after 15 CSAM charges
stories.summary: Mason Hull, known online as Hullo, has reportedly resumed posting on TikTok. This comeback follows his recent charges for child sexual abuse material possession. Many social media users are discussing his return and platform policies. His legal case remains ongoing, with no verdict reached yet. The creator's online presence continues to spark debate among the public.

stories.title: J&K flood toll climbs to 28 as fresh deaths hit Poonch, Doda; rescuers dig through debris as rain threat persists
stories.summary: Torrential rain caused flash floods and landslides, killing twenty-eight people across Jammu division. Poonch reported twenty-three deaths, including several children, after a house collapse. Rescuers dug four bodies from rubble left by raging streams and collapsing hillsides. Amarnath Yatra and pilgrimages to Vaishno Devi shrine remained suspended for a second day. The India Meteorological Department issued a red alert warning of extremely heavy rain.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Epicurus: 'Death does not concern us, because as long as we exist...'
stories.summary: Epicurus, the ancient Greek philosopher, offered a compelling perspective on the fear of death, asserting that it should not concern us since our existence ceases when death arrives. This notion, termed the symmetry argument, challenges the fears associated with dying. Residing in a community known as The Garden, Epicurus sought to promote tranquility through his teachings, which continue to resonate today amidst contemporary worries about life and health.

stories.title: AIIMS RDA seeks President’s intervention over Jantar Mantar crackdown, Wangchuk hospitalisation
Quote of the day by Usha Vance: 'There's nothing more exciting than getting to see the world through the eye of kids as they're growing up' and the joys of motherhood
Scientists tracked endangered Australian cockatoos for three breeding seasons and found...
stories.summary: The peril faced by Carnaby's black cockatoos is escalating, as pesticide contamination in their food reaches alarming rates. Testing of seed samples revealed that toxic chemicals present are hundreds of times higher than what is legally permissible. This exposure might shed light on the troubling paralysis syndrome afflicting these endangered birds. Furthermore, researchers identified neurotoxic substances banned in various regions of Europe.

stories.title: Asmongold’s girlfriend Kaise finds cockroach head in streamer’s fridge during live stream
stories.summary: Popular streamer Asmongold's girlfriend Kaise discovered a cockroach head in his refrigerator. The unexpected find occurred during a recent livestream while preparing food together. Asmongold casually explained the possible accidental presence of the insect part. This incident added to ongoing discussions about the streamer's home condition. Kaise's visit continues to provide memorable moments for viewers.

stories.title: Tina Sodhi paid $2,000 for wellness treatment in Florida, she never made it home; doctor charged with manslaughter a year later
Canadian wildfire smoke linked to fewer sightings of 40 bird species in New York
stories.summary: A new University at Buffalo study has found that smoke from Canadian wildfires may have made many bird species harder to spot in New York State during the 2021–2023 breeding seasons. Researchers linked higher levels of wildfire-related PM2.5 air pollution with fewer sightings of 40 bird species. They say the birds may have changed their behaviour rather than disappeared, highlighting the need to consider air quality when monitoring wildlife.

stories.title: Indus Water Treaty in present form no longer exists, Pak aiding terrorism: India
Unlicensed doctor arrested in New York after woman dies from anti-ageing injection
'Will not be arrested in US': Trump responds to Mamdani's Netanyahu remarks
stories.summary: Donald Trump stated Benjamin Netanyahu will not face arrest in the United States. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani considered legal actions against the Israeli leader. Netanyahu faces an International Criminal Court arrest warrant for alleged crimes. Mamdani believes the Prime Minister belongs in The Hague for his actions. Trump defended Netanyahu's fight against Iran and criticized its leadership.

stories.title: Scientists found an anemone that can distinguish helpful bacteria from harmful bacteria without...
stories.summary: Sea anemones distinguish helpful bacteria from harmful invaders without antibodies. Specialized cell structures engulf and destroy foreign bacteria while preserving beneficial microbes. Gene editing revealed a key gene regulating this selective bacterial identification process. This discovery challenges long-held assumptions about early animal immune system evolution. These primitive pathways offer insights into ancient immune memory and maternal transfer.

stories.title: "Modi Govt has become extremely arrogant": Arvind Kejriwal on Lathi-Charge against protesters
stories.summary: AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal on Monday launched a scathing attack on the Centre over the police action against students, calling the Modi government "extremely arrogant" for using force against peaceful protesters.

stories.title: 16 days after Nolan Wells' death, no one knows what exactly happened to the Mississippi footballer who went to Horn Island with friends
'Cherry-picking numbers': Trump admin slams report claiming Pentagon withheld data on troop injuries in Iran war
Father saved for years so that I could study in America but...: Woman's 'American Dream' turns into 'Make in India'
'Power does not last forever': Rahul Gandhi's warning to police after tear gas, lathicharge on student protesters
A human-bred aquarium fish prized for its bright colour has escaped into a Philippines crater lake
stories.summary: Flowerhorn cichlids, bred by humans, have found their way into Lake Sampaloc, a crater lake in the Philippines. Their presence poses a significant threat to the local ecosystem, competing aggressively with native ayungin fish and disrupting aquaculture. Experts raise alarms about the potential for disease transmission and the rapid expansion of this invasive species, underscoring a pressing global issue of domesticated animals affecting natural habitats.

stories.title: CJP march: Police say detained protesters 'not students'; more arrests likely
4 Indians killed, 1 critically injured after cargo ship attacked off Ukraine's Odesa coast
In 1918, an empire collapsed and a 137-carat diamond vanished. More than a century later, its whereabouts may finally be known
Trump scores own-goal as World Cup overflows with politics
How wild snapdragons tune colors for bees
stories.summary: Wild snapdragons showcase an impressive ability to adjust their petal colors with the help of seven genes, aimed at attracting bees. These vibrant flowers utilize this precise color calibration as visual cues for their pollinators. Researchers discovered that these genetic variations create subtle yet significant differences, which are critical for survival in narrow hybrid zones where less effective colors are less likely to thrive.

stories.title: Xi's US trip appears on track even as Trump's election interference claims inject fresh strain
A floating 'igloo' research station has left France for Arctic, where it will drift with polar ice
stories.summary: A floating research station shaped like a giant aluminium igloo has left France on a two-year Arctic mission to study biodiversity and the effects of climate change. The station will drift with sea ice while an international team of scientists collects more than 10,000 samples despite extreme cold, months of darkness and the risk of polar bear encounters.

stories.title: After years of living in a trailer, a couple self-built their 3,600-square-foot home for $410K
stories.summary: Allison Brown and her husband spent six years living in a 1,500-square-foot trailer in South Dakota to keep their housing costs low and save money. Those savings later helped them build their own 3,600-square-foot home for about $410,000 by managing the project themselves. They also turned their old trailer into an Airbnb, creating an additoinal source of income.

stories.title: Archaeologists uncover 7,000-year-old fish traps that rewrite the story of life before farming in Scandinavia
Nepal's Re 1 coin gets a makeover: Controversial Kalapani-Lipulekh-Limpiyadhura map removed
California city manager arrested over alleged yacht burglary weeks after taking office
'No prima facie case': HC rejects plea of Mamata Banerjee faction to operate TMC accounts worth Rs 440 crore
stories.summary: The Calcutta high court denied interim relief to the Trinamool Congress faction. Three party bank accounts frozen by the Enforcement Directorate will remain inaccessible. The court found no prima facie case for the petitioners' request. The Enforcement Directorate is investigating alleged money laundering and dishonest financial transactions. The matter will be heard again on August 26.

stories.title: Scientists marked this coral reef as dead in the 1960s; underwater drones found it alive...
stories.summary: After being presumed extinct for sixty years, a remarkable coral reef off West Africa has been rediscovered, thriving with an array of fish and coral species. This vibrant mesophotic coral ecosystem thrives in low-light environments beneath the ocean's surface. Researchers speculate that similar hidden reefs could exist along the West African coastline, providing valuable insights into the evolutionary history of the region's marine life and past environmental changes.

stories.title: Who will ask if you’re home? The economy growing around urban loneliness
stories.summary: India faces a growing loneliness crisis as its population ages rapidly. Urbanization and changing social structures contribute to this increasing isolation. Young migrants and older adults alike experience profound feelings of not belonging. The emerging "silver economy" offers market-based solutions for connection and care. This situation highlights the need to address loneliness as a fundamental human requirement.

stories.title: FedEx CEO Raj Subramaniam grabbed the opportunity that his roommate rejected: He can't come but can I send my resume?
Kolkata Chai announces tie-up with Bungalow Hospitality Investments
Illinois farmers are making up to $200,000 a year without growing more crops as solar companies offer long-term leases worth up to $2,000 per acre
'Hopefully govt will fix accountability': Sonam Wangchuk to continue his hunger strike
stories.summary: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk continues his hunger strike after witnessing police actions against protestors. He demands that youth leaders meet parliamentarians or he be allowed to meet them. Wangchuk appeals to the government and police to let students present their grievances. Thousands marched to Parliament demanding the Education Minister's resignation over examination irregularities. Police used tear gas and force, detaining several protestors during the march.

stories.title: DS Group launches Pallu Protection PPE to shield women farmers from pesticide exposure
Some species of mosquitoes in the UK spread avian malaria
stories.summary: In a landmark study, researchers have pinpointed certain mosquito species that spread avian malaria in the UK. Among twelve species analyzed, nine were found to harbor traces of this bird disease. Notably, the Ochlerotatus detritus mosquito is suspected to transmit Plasmodium vaughani to blackbirds, with additional species identified as potential carriers for parasites that threaten various native birds.

stories.title: Trainee IPS officer, accused of sexual harassment by colleague, hospitalised after suspected suicide attempt
stories.summary: A trainee IPS officer was hospitalized after a suspected suicide attempt following serious allegations. He faces charges of stalking and sexually harassing a fellow trainee at the police academy. The woman trainee accused him of sending abusive messages and physical assault. The officer denied the allegations on social media, calling them baseless. Investigators will issue a notice for him to appear in connection with the case.

stories.title: 'Disgusting what government is doing': Rahul Gandhi slams police action against protesters; shares video
A 26-year-old quit corporate job in Chicago to be a seamstress for $19.25 an hour
stories.summary: Zoe De La Paz, 26, left her corporate engineering job in Chicago to work as a seamstress at Yellowstone National Park, turning a high-school hobby into a full-time career. After gaining experience through backstage jobs at music venues, she now repairs uniforms at Yellowstone while working towards her long-term goal of joining Broadway and film costume departments in New York City.
