Saudi Arabia launches new one-year, multiple-entry Umrah visa with 90-day stay
Hunters carried trout past waterfalls into fishless Norwegian mountain lakes 7,000 years ago
stories.summary: In a remarkable feat 7,000 years ago, ancient hunter-gatherers transformed Norwegian mountain lakes by introducing brown trout. Archaeologists discovered remnants of intricate fish traps from 5000 BC, highlighting how these early communities intentionally manipulated their ecosystems for sustainable food resources. They even transported live fish through rugged landscapes, paving the way for the fisheries we know today, where anglers still catch their ancient descendants.

stories.title: 'It destroys academic freedom': TMC on VBSA bill as JPC defers report
A couple bought their dream home and got the keys, only to discover the property was a snake habitat after moving in
stories.summary: Tyler and Lauren Bouldin bought an abandoned historic Pennsylvania home in 2020. They discovered the neglected grounds had become a thriving habitat for various snakes. The couple learned to manage the wildlife by making the property less attractive to them. They safely captured and relocated snakes encountered near their home. Five years later, the property is transformed into their dream family home.

stories.title: Fresh landslide kills seven in rain-ravaged Poonch, J&K toll rises to 17
Indian techie in Ohio dies from 'rare, life-threatening condition'; felt severe pain in left leg after dinner
Florida turns restaurant waste into reefs; fish and dolphins rebound
stories.summary: Florida restored parts of the Gulf of Mexico by returning more than 500,000 tonnes of recycled oyster and clam shells to the sea between 2007 and 2024. The shells helped rebuild oyster reefs, improve water quality and support the return of fish, turtles and dolphins to levels not seen in over 25 years.

stories.title: 'Weaponisation of water': Pakistan seeks Canada's help to revive Indus Waters Treaty with India
stories.summary: Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar requested Canadian support for the Indus Waters Treaty. He stated India suspended the agreement, adding a new dynamic to security. Dar urged India to end water weaponization and uphold international law. India maintains its position remains in abeyance due to terrorism. Pakistan views the Indus as a lifeline and will defend its sovereignty.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: CJP delegation meets JP Nadda as protest intensifies, Andy Burnham becomes UK's new PM & more
'Waiting for their arrival': Iran dares US ground invasion on Kharg Island
Nasa explores human hibernation for Mars, but major challenges remain
Ram Temple donation row: Trust deploys new cash-counting team, introduces two-shift system under SBI supervision
stories.summary: The Ram Temple trust has implemented a new cash counting system with two shifts. This new process is now under the supervision of the State Bank of India. A new in-charge has been appointed after the previous one was jailed. This follows an investigation into alleged theft of donation money. Authorities arrested eight individuals and recovered significant cash and valuables.

stories.title: Delhi HC seeks comprehensive medical record on Sonam Wangchuk's condition
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court requested comprehensive medical records for Sonam Wangchuk. Authorities must submit all health documents and reports from various hospitals. Doctors treating Wangchuk were directed to appear before the court. This action follows an appeal against a single judge's decision on his hospital transfer. The court is reviewing the government's decision regarding his deteriorating health condition.

stories.title: Trump says Qatari-gifted Boeing 747-8 will be taken out of service to be 'maxed out'
'A new path for Britain': Andy Burnham becomes 7th UK PM in 10 years, promises stability after Starmer exit
Who is Khalil al-Hayya, the Hamas leader named as group's new chief
Meet Brunello Cucinelli: The billionaire building a Universal Library in Italy for the next 1,000 years with free access to humanity's greatest books, inspired by the ancient Library of Alexandria
Why did Clavicular break up with Lily Snyder? Streamer's shocking split leaves viewers stunned
stories.summary: Streamer Clavicular confirmed his breakup with Lily Snyder during a live broadcast. He cited manipulative and volatile behavior as reasons for the split. An incident involving his ear surgery recovery also contributed to the decision. The streamer mentioned ongoing conflicts with his content creation style. Their relationship had previously faced numerous difficulties and near-breakups.

stories.title: Australia's Finke River called the oldest river on Earth, but it's more complicated
Govt, opposition face off on Day 1 of Monsoon Session: Key takeaways
'My work is done': Keir Starmer bows out as PM, says UK 'stronger & fairer'
stories.summary: Keir Starmer has resigned as the United Kingdom's prime minister after two years in office. Andy Burnham will now formally become Britain's prime minister following Starmer's departure. Burnham takes office after replacing Starmer as Labour leader on Friday. The parliamentary system allows for such leadership changes without a general election. Burnham pledged to restore political stability and make politics less toxic.

stories.title: PayBae and Lacy controversy explained after questionable Streamer University 2026 interaction
stories.summary: Streamer University 2026 saw controversy involving Twitch streamer PayBae and Nick Lacy. A video showed PayBae pulling Lacy's injured leg, causing him pain. Lacy questioned why his injury was not respected during the incident. PayBae apologized but felt the situation was being amplified by Lacy's audience. She also claimed a prior "fake beef" influenced her reaction.

stories.title: 'Where did your 56-inch chest go?' Kharge hits back at PM Modi's '56-year-old youth' jab
Tear gas fired, protesters lathicharged: Videos capture chaotic scenes from CJP's 'sansad chalo' march
Biohacker Bryan Johnson claims ice packs boost male fertility: Does science agree?
stories.summary: Bryan Johnson, a longevity influencer, claims that icing his testicles greatly increases his sperm count. His unique approach has inspired several Redditors to experiment with this method for improving fertility. Although some research hints at the benefits of mild scrotal cooling for male fertility, experts caution that there is insufficient evidence to suggest significant improvements in testosterone or overall sperm production.

stories.title: Scientists find toxins from Florida's toxic algae blooms travel through air, raise risk of ALS
stories.summary: Recent research reveals the presence of cyanobacterial toxins in the air of Southwest Florida, matching those found in dolphins displaying Alzheimer's characteristics. This airborne contamination indicates that inhabitants may be exposed to lower concentrations of these toxins, which are believed to heighten the chances of ALS and various ailments. Unlike food-related toxins, mitigating exposure through breath poses a significant and complex challenge.

stories.title: Ram temple donation 'theft' row: Simple case of crime, don't politicise it, says SC
HasanAbi says he may file a restraining order against Destiny after latest livestream comments
stories.summary: In a troubling turn of events, HasanAbi is weighing the option of filing a restraining order against fellow creator Destiny due to what he describes as continuous harassment stemming from Destiny's supporters. He has accused this community of orchestrated harassment and doxxing attempts. HasanAbi insists that this issue is not just about him but is essential for the protection of others.

stories.title: Indian-origin scientist Satchin Panda resigns from California's Salk institute amid sexual misconduct probe
'These are our children': Priyanka Gandhi slams Centre over police action at CJP protest
Frankford Avenue Bridge: The oldest bridge in the US still carrying traffic was built in 1697 and has survived more than 320 years of history
stories.summary: Philadelphia's Frankford Avenue Bridge, built in 1697, remains in continuous use. This stone arch structure is the oldest surviving roadway bridge still carrying vehicles. It served as a vital link for colonial travel and witnessed revolutionary events. The bridge has been widened and modified over centuries to accommodate modern transport. Designated a National Historic Civil Engineering Landmark, it preserves a connection to America's colonial past.

stories.title: A Quebecer noticed a strange circular pit on Google Maps; scientists confirm it's a crater
stories.summary: An amateur astronomer found a circular depression on a map. Scientists investigated and confirmed it as a meteorite impact crater. This ancient crater is approximately 390 million years old. The discovery adds Uhackatik to Canada's list of impact structures. Modern tools enable everyday people to contribute to scientific understanding.

stories.title: 'Got no commitments': CJP leaders handover 3 demands to JP Nadda; minister says end 'sit-in'
stories.summary: Cockroach Janata Party leaders met Union minister JP Nadda regarding the NEET-UG paper leak case. Protesters marched towards Parliament demanding accountability and specific government actions. The Union minister sought time to consult leadership on the party's demands. Meanwhile, Union Home Minister Amit Shah met the Education Minister at Parliament. Police used mild force and tear gas as demonstrators attempted to breach barricades.

stories.title: Scientists find sudden ‘switch-off’ in Sun’s cycle
stories.summary: Scientists have developed a new method to predict solar cycle strength. This approach identifies a precise point where extreme space weather abruptly ceases. Researchers can now forecast the next solar cycle's activity up to seven years in advance. Early predictions suggest Solar Cycle 26 may be moderate in strength. Further refinement of these forecasts will occur in approximately two years.

stories.title: 50 cops hurt, stones pelted, Wangchuk's wife 'assaulted': Protest turns ugly as Delhi Police, CJP make conflicting claims
'Lacklustre, deliberately understated event': PDP takes swipe at NC's Delhi protest for J&K statehood
stories.summary: Peoples Democratic Party leader Iltija Mufti criticized the National Conference protest for statehood restoration. She deemed the demonstration lacklustre and deliberately understated, lacking a call for Article 370. Mufti argued a Jantar Mantar protest would have demanded special status reinstatement. The PDP stayed away, insisting on Article 370 restoration and prisoner release. This follows the 2019 revocation of Article 370 and state bifurcation.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Nico Williams: "I run very fast, but I can't run as fast as my mother. Because she once escaped death and…" - an emotional tribute to his mother, the extraordinary journey behind his success and the sacrifices that shaped a football star
stories.summary: Spanish footballer Nico Williams honored his mother after Euro 2024 victory. He gave his medal to her, recognizing her difficult journey. His mother escaped death and crossed the Sahara Desert from Ghana to Spain. This arduous migration paved the way for his and his brother's careers. Williams highlighted his mother's sacrifice as more deserving than his own athletic achievement.

stories.title: In 1928, a German architect planned to block the Strait of Gibraltar, drain the Mediterranean and create a new continent called Atlantropa
Spain and Portugal have been hiding a second rabbit species for nearly 2 million years
FIFA World Cup 2026 Final: IShowSpeed hypes BTS halftime show; backstage photo lights up X
stories.summary: Popular streamer IShowSpeed enjoyed one of the biggest moments of the FIFA World Cup final after watching BTS perform during the halftime show. The viral streamer later met the K-pop group backstage. The internet personality became a trending topic as videos of his hilarious reaction spread across social media during the championship match between Spain and Argentina.

stories.title: TheMightyBA's Streamer University 2026 controversy explained as Ludwig speaks about his future
stories.summary: The controversy at Streamer University 2026 surrounding TheMightyBA intensified when footage surfaced of him patting MeesterKeem's head, triggering a storm of criticism. Ludwig stood by TheMightyBA, suggesting that redemption is possible, drawing parallels to IShowSpeed’s remarkable evolution. With persistent effort and time, creators can address their past errors and forge a path to redemption.

stories.title: In 2020, a couple bought an abandoned 1830s house at auction and found a snake-filled property; 5 years later, they revealed how they turned it into a family home
Why activists threw balloons full of acidic mixture on Microsoft's upcoming data centre in Amsterdam
stories.summary: AI data center construction is igniting a storm of environmental and social dilemmas. Community activists are protesting against these facilities, highlighting their substantial energy and water usage. Tensions have risen in Amsterdam, with protests turning into acts of vandalism. Residents living nearby complain of noise issues and land seizures. Tech firms find themselves facing mounting backlash from activists and impacted local property owners.

stories.title: More than 2,200 years ago, an ancient Greek scholar calculated the Earth's circumference with a stick and the Sun
Tripura DGP Anurag Dhankar found dead at Agartala police headquarters
Japan's forest bathing idea in 1982: 40 years of research found a more complicated picture
Two North Dakota men discover they were switched at birth, raised by each other's families for nearly four decades before a Christmas gift changed everything

Quote of the day by Dwayne Johnson: "The men I idolized built their bodies and became somebody, like Sylvester Stallone and Arnold Schwarzenegger, and I thought…" - a powerful lesson on ambition, role models and how small decisions can shape an entire life
stories.summary: Dwayne Johnson highlights how significant life changes often begin subtly. He started working out after admiring Sylvester Stallone and Arnold Schwarzenegger. This initial step felt ordinary then but proved defining later. Many important decisions lack immediate clarity and reveal their impact over time. Recognizing these turning points usually happens in hindsight after life unfolds.

stories.title: Debris of asteroid shattered 800 million yrs ago may have bombarded Earth for 150 million yrs
stories.summary: A new study suggests that a giant asteroid breakup in the main asteroid belt about 800 million years ago may have triggered a long period of impacts across Earth, the Moon and Mars. Researchers linked the event to the Eulalia asteroid family and say it could explain ancient lunar craters. While the impacts coincided with major climate and biological changes on Earth, the study does not prove they caused them.

stories.title: Six tiny fossil jaws found in Australia have pushed the origin of its carnivorous marsupials back by 5 million years
stories.summary: A significant fossil discovery in Queensland has revealed Australia's oldest carnivorous marsupial. These ancient predators, dating back twenty-three million years, inhabited lush rainforests. The tiny fossil jaws belong to a newly identified species named Miyumba chrisdickmani. This finding fills a major gap in the continent's evolutionary history. It suggests dasyurids originated in wet habitats before adapting to drier landscapes.

stories.title: Big Bear Eagles need $10 million to protect their habitat before July 31
stories.summary: Thousands of people around the world are watching bald eagles Jackie and Shadow raise their two eaglets through a live nest camera in California's Big Bear Valley. As the chicks continue to grow, conservationists are also racing to raise $10 million to protect the surrounding habitat from development, highlighting the importance of preserving the forests and open spaces the eagles need to survive.

stories.title: How Amazon soy pact collapse could affect Brazil
stories.summary: A voluntary soy deforestation pact has collapsed after nearly two decades of success. This collapse is predicted to cause significant future deforestation in the Amazon rainforest. Researchers estimate over one million hectares of forest loss by 2036. This deforestation will release substantial carbon emissions equivalent to Canada's annual output. Aggressive enforcement and stronger import demands are now recommended to protect the Amazon.

stories.title: NTA names 5 NEET candidates, says OMR claims built on digital forgeries
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has dismissed allegations regarding discrepancies in OMR sheets presented by five NEET-UG candidates. They emphasized that the images circulating are likely digitally altered, enhanced with AI, or otherwise modified. The agency affirmed the authenticity of the OMR sheets and the accuracy of the candidates' scores. Severe penalties may be imposed for submitting fraudulent records under new regulations.

stories.title: India approves its first dengue vaccine QDENGA after DCGI clearance
stories.summary: Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral disease reported in more than 125 countries. According to the company, India accounts for nearly one-third of the global dengue burden, with rapid urbanisation, climate change and widespread mosquito breeding continuing to increase the risk of infection across the country. Vaccine QDENGA is given as two injections of 0.5 ml, administered under the skin three months apart.

stories.title: Meet Wally Funk: She passed NASA's astronaut tests but waited 60 years to reach space
Chinese woman declared dead and nearly cremated in 1995 was saved by a funeral home worker's last-second discovery; today, she is an award-winning artist
'Neet hai ya cheat hai?' Dimple Yadav joins CJP's 'Sansad Chalo' protest at Jantar Mantar
stories.summary: Carrying the 'NEET hai, ki Cheat hai' placard, Dimple Yadav said "we stand with the students", adding that the "entire process is corrupt, and it is the country's youth and students who are bearing the brunt of it and suffering immense mental stress".​​ Akhilesh Yadav also accused the BJP-led government of ignoring students' concerns and alleged that repeated paper leaks had taken place in Uttar Pradesh.

stories.title: An exoplanet found 48 light-years away has given scientists hope for life, here's why
Humanoid robot 'Sally' to teach AI to 11th and 12th grade students in New York school in a first-ever experiment in US
stories.summary: Sally, a humanoid robot teacher, is set to debut at a New York high school, providing personalized educational experiences in specialized classes. Designed to be relatable with her realistic appearance and western New York accent, Sally will support both students and teachers with curriculum-aligned learning and translations. Additionally, the school has taken steps to reassure parents and the local community about the integration of artificial intelligence in the classroom.

stories.title: Scientists reveal whether 400,000-year-old rock fragments be the oldest known evidence of human fire-making
A dog ate marijuana on Scotland's highest mountain, got too high to stand and had to be carried down by mountain rescuers
Kerala court sentences 61-year-old to death in Nenmara double murder case
stories.summary: The quantum of punishment was decided after the sentencing hearing concluded last Tuesday before Judge Kenneth George, who heard detailed submissions from both the prosecution and the defence before reserving the verdict. The prosecution urged the court to impose the death penalty, arguing that the crime fell within the "rarest of rare" category. It told the court that Chenthamara posed a continuing threat to society and cited his remarks after conviction to argue that he had shown no remorse.

stories.title: 'Not talking about some 56-year-old youth': PM Modi takes apparent swipe at Rahul Gandhi
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi lauded India's young space innovators while addressing Parliament. He highlighted Skyroot Aerospace's average team age of twenty-eight years. This achievement marks a significant milestone for India's private space sector. The Prime Minister also discussed India's economic resilience amidst global challenges. He appealed for productive discussions during the Monsoon Session of Parliament.

stories.title: 'Hope for productive monsoon session': PM Modi highlights India's gains ahead of Parliament proceedings
stories.summary: Taunting Rahul Gandhi in a veiled attack, PM Modi praised the succcessful mission of Vikram-1 orbital launch vehicle highlighting how the average age of the young Skyroot team is merely 28 years, unlike a "56-year-old youth."​​ "India's youth have embarked on a new journey into space. I was told that the average age of the entire team working at the 'Skyroot' startup is merely 28 years. Young people like these have accomplished this feat. I am not speaking of a 56-year-old youth," PM Modi said.

stories.title: 'They should pay us': Trump threatens Canada PM with tariffs over 'poisoned air' affecting US cities
Sonam Wangchuk's wife challenges Delhi HC order, says it 'illegally confines' him to Safdarjung hospital
'They came very late': CJP claims govt reached out, but 'no clarity' on talks
stories.summary: Supporters gathered at Jantar Mantar ahead of the proposed 'Chalo Sansad' march to Parliament on Monday. Addressing the gathering, CJP president Abhijeet Dipke said the march would go ahead despite restrictions. "The biggest march in India's history is about to take place. For the past 10-12 years, attempts have been made to destroy democracy in this country. By sitting at Jantar Mantar for a month, you have revived democracy," Abhijeet Dipke said.

stories.title: First Cholesterol-Lowering Pill to Replace PCSK9 Injections Gets US Nod
stories.summary: The US FDA has given the green light to the world's first oral PCSK9 inhibitor, a groundbreaking medication that promises a convenient once-daily tablet alternative to injections for managing high cholesterol in adults, particularly those with genetic variations. When combined with other treatments, this innovative drug has shown a significant reduction in bad cholesterol levels. Unfortunately, it may not be available in India right away.

stories.title: Wangchuk's wife moves Delhi HC again over plea to shift him to private hospital
stories.summary: ​In the appeal, Angmo has contended that the Single Judge’s order effectively deprives Wangchuk and his family of the right to decide his medical treatment and place of treatment. The appeal also argues that the order overlooks the principles of informed consent, bodily autonomy under Article 21, and unlawfully confines Wangchuk to the government hospital despite there being no order of arrest or detention against him, reported news agency ANI.

stories.title: 'Misleading the families?' AI-171 victims' kin seek black box data, memorial after AAIB affidavit
stories.summary: Families question withholding of cockpit recordings, seek greater transparency as AAIB says final probe report is expected in October. They question the investigation bureau's decision to withhold black box information. The flight crashed on June 12, 2025, killing hundreds of people. Families seek transparency and direct access to the raw black box data. They also renewed calls for a permanent memorial at the crash site.

stories.title: Arizona mass shooting: 10 injured after gunman opens fire in Tucson
stories.summary: A mass shooting in crowded downtown Tucson wounded at least ten people early Sunday. Police officers on patrol heard gunfire and responded to the crowded entertainment district. They encountered and shot the suspected gunman, who sustained life-threatening injuries. Nine other adults were shot and taken to hospitals in critical condition.

stories.title: Heavy security at Jantar Mantar as CJP gears up for Parliament march: Top developments
CJP’s 'Sansad Chalo' march: Thousands gather at Jantar Mantar amid tight security — top developments
Abhijeet Dipke detained by Delhi Police, says CJP; Amit Shah meets Dharmendra Pradhan
14 killed, many missing as flash floods, landslides ravage J&K’s Poonch, Rajouri
stories.summary: Torrential rain caused flash floods and landslides in Poonch and Rajouri districts. At least fourteen people died, and several others remain missing after homes were buried. Rescue operations are underway for those trapped beneath debris and mud. Traffic on the Jammu-Srinagar NH-44 was disrupted, and the Amarnath Yatra was suspended. Authorities issued a flood alert across Jammu division as river water levels surged.

stories.title: Net services remain suspended in J&K’s Doda 3 days after man’s death in police firing
Farooq Abdullah meets Wangchuk’s wife, wishes him good health
Bill seeks 3-year jail for disturbing rendition of ‘Vande Mataram’
stories.summary: A new bill plans to jail individuals disrupting Vande Mataram singing. This proposed legislation aims to amend existing laws regarding national honor. Disrupting the national song could lead to three years imprisonment. The government cites historical significance for this proposed amendment. This bill will be introduced during the upcoming Parliament session.

stories.title: 'Fabrications aimed at making bad performance': NTA warns of criminal action on AI, fake OMRs
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has warned of strict action against fake OMR sheets. Several OMR sheets submitted for NEET-UG result grievances were found to be fake or AI-generated. Candidates submitting digitally altered documents face cancellation of results and debarment. The agency is scrutinizing all complaints and will take corrective measures if discrepancies are found. Fabricated documents are being used to challenge results after the recent retest.

stories.title: Congress demands independent probe into donation chori
stories.summary: Opposition leaders have demanded an independent probe into Ram temple donations. They also warned the government's credibility depends on swift action regarding this issue. Activists and a political party plan a march to Parliament over paper leaks. Many opposition parties support this protest and may join the Parliament gherao. These twin issues are likely to dominate the upcoming monsoon session's first week.

stories.title: Monsoon session begins today as oppn gears up to corner Centre over temple row, NEET, E20
stories.summary: Cong can raise demand, can't force govt: Rijiju

stories.title: DMK confirms TOI report it’s open to rethink on delimit bill
stories.summary: The DMK party will state its position on the Lok Sabha strength bill later. This regional party holds a significant bloc of 22 Members of Parliament. They are open to revisiting their delimitation stance if southern states are not harmed. DMK previously protested a similar bill, which was defeated by the opposition. The party awaits the government's proposed legislation to clarify its future actions.

stories.title: Minister Manohar Lal dismantles Central Public Works Department’s ‘Delhi Club’
Opposition protests invite to TMC rebels to all-party meeting
stories.summary: Opposition parties staged a walkout from an all-party meeting on Sunday. They protested the government's decision to invite a breakaway faction of the Trinamool Congress. The government defended its invitation, stating it must include all groups. Both warring factions of the Trinamool Congress exchanged sharp remarks during the meeting. This event foreshadows a potentially contentious parliamentary session beginning Monday.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Democritus: 'If your desires are not great, a little will seem much to you'
Well-oiled labour supply chain facilitating illegal infiltration of Bangladeshis
stories.summary: Illegal immigrants from Bangladesh enter India through a planned labor supply chain. Touts facilitate their infiltration and transport to various job sites across India. Indian employers utilize these networks for cheap, unskilled labor in sectors like textiles and construction. Forged documents are arranged, enabling immigrants to work and even register as voters. Assam seeks legal accountability for Indian employers involved in this exploitation.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Confucius: 'If I am walking with two other men, each of them will serve...'
Government may seek Parliamentary nod for additional spending
stories.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman may seek parliamentary approval for additional spending. Increased expenditure on fertiliser subsidies and electronics manufacturing initiatives is driving this need. GST and direct tax revenues remain on track, and DIPAM is pushing for additional realisations. The IDBI Bank transaction's finalisation could provide significant financial comfort. Sitharaman aims to maintain the government's fiscal deficit target of 4.3% of GDP.

stories.title: Larry Ellison once struggled to pay his electricity bills. Now, he has written a $300 million cheque to...
stories.summary: Once grappling with utility bills for his workshop, tech magnate Larry Ellison transformed his fortunes by acquiring 98 percent of a Hawaiian island for a staggering $300 million. Now residing full-time on Lanai, he envisions a luxury destination coupled with a sustainable community. Despite fluctuations in his wealth driven by market trends, Oracle's cloud operations showcase remarkable strength amid ongoing challenges.

stories.title: IShowSpeed performs 'Champions' at FIFA World Cup 2026 final closing ceremony
stories.summary: IShowSpeed performed his song "Champions" at the FIFA World Cup 2026 final closing ceremony. He became the first content creator to perform live at this major global sporting event. His viral World Cup anthem gained significant popularity among football fans worldwide. FIFA secured rights to his song, which became a recognized tournament track. This performance highlighted the growing influence of online creators on international stages.

stories.title: MacKenzie Scott once fixed a broken tooth with glue. Now she's giving $20 million to struggling teenagers
stories.summary: Philanthropist MacKenzie Scott gave a record $20 million to Active Minds. This donation addresses the critical youth mental health crisis in America. Scott's past financial struggles influenced her generous giving approach. The funding will expand mental health programs across schools and universities. Active Minds aims to reduce stigma and improve support accessibility for young people.

stories.title: Even as fertility rates drop, young still aspire to partnership, parenthood, shows UN report
stories.summary: Young adults worldwide and in India still desire marriage and family life. Financial security and stable employment are crucial for partnership decisions. Many young people aspire to partnership and parenthood despite demographic shifts. India's youth express optimism about the future while worrying about economic insecurity. Ideal family sizes are reported, with older respondents having fewer children.

stories.title: Less than half of 483 Lok Sabha MPs attended 90-100% of sittings in Parliament’s budget session, shows analysis
stories.summary: Smaller parties demonstrated the highest average Member of Parliament attendance during the recent budget session. RLP and RLD achieved one hundred percent attendance for all thirty-one sittings. BJP and Congress, the largest parties, recorded lower average attendance figures. In Rajya Sabha, regional parties also led in parliamentary attendance percentages. This analysis highlights attendance trends among various political parties in both Houses.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Aristotle: "The ideal man bears the accidents of life with dignity and…" - a powerful lesson on resilience, character and how people respond when life does not go according to plan
stories.summary: Life's unpredictable events require a dignified and graceful response from individuals. Aristotle's philosophy emphasizes maintaining composure during both good and bad fortune. Dignity involves retaining self-worth while experiencing emotions like grief or fear. Grace means responding firmly to injustice without succumbing to anger. This approach focuses on how one handles setbacks, not on avoiding them.

stories.title: Thrown into battle in two weeks': Russia plans 500,000-strong mobilisation, Ukraine claims
'Rise in instability in Iran': Indian embassy sounds alarm; urges people to leave, postpone travel
Iran's unseen Supreme Leader may turn to Putin as first foreign contact amid war
Scientists used children’s ‘silly sprinklers’ to solve Feynman's physics problem
stories.summary: Mathematicians have solved a physics puzzle using backyard sprinklers. Experiments with silly sprinklers clarified how reverse sprinklers rotate. The key lies in how water momentum collides inside the central chamber. This principle applies across various sprinkler arm shapes and designs. The findings offer insights for fluid dynamics in engineering applications.

stories.title: Pay quarterly, not yearly: Saudi Arabia introduces 3-month residency permit renewal option for domestic workers
Scientists studied found flies rebuild their biological clock into a separate seasonal mode
stories.summary: In a fascinating discovery, scientists have found that fruit flies adapt their internal biological clocks to survive winter by employing a genetic mechanism known as the winter lock. This adaptation allows them to remain inactive until warmer weather arrives, showcasing a seasonal shift in their molecular structure. These insights not only open avenues for innovative pest control strategies but also enhance our understanding of seasonal variations in human health issues.

stories.title: ‘People’s safety our highest priority’: Assam govt requests Army, Air Force to remain on standby for flood evacuations
'Stay here for the night': CJP's Abhijeet Dipke calls for night-long vigil ahead of 'Chalo Sansad' march
Mediterranean seagrass survives in dim seabed light by expanding its photosynthetic antenna
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered how the Mediterranean seagrass Posidonia oceanicahas adapted its photosynthetic system to survive in the dim, blue-green light of the seabed. The plant captures more light while moving energy more efficiently by altering its photosynthetic machinery. Researchers say the findings could help develop crop plants that make better use of limited sunlight under dense canopies.

stories.title: 'We intend to work with PM Modi': Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar announces entry into NDA with 20 Mamata rebels
stories.summary: Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar announced her group's move to join the ruling NDA in Parliament. Twenty former TMC MPs are now aligning with the NCPI parliamentary group. This group intends to work with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Amit Shah. They will support the government's initiatives and focus on constructive debate. The rebels' realignment follows the TMC's recent election defeat in West Bengal.

stories.title: Residents kept reporting Dolphins. Underwater microphones revealed their visits
stories.summary: Scientists from Kyoto University used underwater microphones to monitor dolphins in two bays along Japan's Sea of Japan coast. They found dolphin sounds only about once every 10 days, suggesting the animals visit these waters occasionally. The study also shows that long-term underwater listening can help scientists better understand and conserve marine life.

stories.title: Warming seas are bringing octopus, red mullet and bream into UK waters
stories.summary: As the seas warm, British waters are now seeing an influx of Mediterranean species. This environmental transformation is compelling local fishers to modify their traditional techniques. Notably, octopus populations are surging, impacting native shellfish and depleting other seafood supplies. In response, chefs are creatively revamping menus to highlight these new arrivals like octopus and bream, balancing the challenges with exciting culinary possibilities.

stories.title: Florida is planting 15,000 milkweeds along highways to help monarch butterflies
stories.summary: Scientists and transport officials in Florida have planted 15,000 milkweed plants along roadsides to help monarch butterflies survive and reproduce. Milkweed is the only plant on which monarchs lay their eggs, making it essential for their life cycle. The project also supports bees and other pollinators while testing whether roadside habitats can become long-term wildlife corridors across the state.

stories.title: Elisha Cuthbert has sold her longtime LA home for $1.93 million after cutting the asking price
stories.summary: Hollywood actress Elisha Cuthbert has sold her Los Angeles home for $1.93 million after several unsuccessful attempts to find a buyer. The property was sold shortly after a final price cut. The sale comes as Cuthbert returns to acting following a four-year break, during which she focused on raising her two children with husband Dion Phaneuf.

stories.title: 'No permission sought or granted': Delhi Police on CJP's Parliament march
stories.summary: Delhi Police has denied permission for a proposed march to Parliament on July 20. Prohibitory orders are in effect across the New Delhi district, banning assemblies. Unauthorized gatherings will face legal action under new Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita provisions. The Delhi High Court previously upheld the Centre's intervention in Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike. Authorities urge public cooperation to ensure security during the upcoming Parliament session.

stories.title: Scientists discover a ‘third cell’ that helps regrow hair
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking development, Japanese researchers have unveiled a pivotal third cell integral to the regeneration of hair follicles. This finding holds the potential to reverse conditions like baldness and thinning hair by collaborating with two established cell types. Successful experiments conducted on mice demonstrated the complete cycle of hair growth, paving the way for pioneering regenerative treatments aimed at combating hair loss.

stories.title: The real-life Gilmore Girls house from the pilot episode is for sale for $2.7 million in Ontario, where Unionville first stood in for Stars Hollow
stories.summary: A historic Unionville home, which served as Lorelai and Rory Gilmore’s house in the pilot episode, is now for sale. This property, listed at $3.88 million CAD, offers a tangible connection to the beloved show. The surrounding neighborhood also featured as key Stars Hollow locations, enhancing its appeal. The house, built around 1875, blends Victorian charm with modern amenities for comfortable living.

stories.title: Archaeologists unearthed a rare 2,600-year-old Assyrian stele, a decade after ISIS damaged the city
stories.summary: A stunning 2,600-year-old Assyrian monument has surfaced in Nineveh, Iraq, celebrating the architectural feats of King Ashurbanipal. Unearthed amidst restoration efforts at the Shamash Gate, this stone artifact reveals essential details about Assyrian urban development. This significant find stands as a testament to the resilience of cultural identities, aiding in reconciling historical disruptions and preservation.

stories.title: Scientists identify rare meteorite behind dinosaur extinction
stories.summary: Scientists have identified a rare CO chondrite meteorite as the impactor that caused dinosaur extinction. This space rock, which struck Earth 66 million years ago, wiped out most life. Advanced nickel isotope analysis traced the meteorite's chemical signature to the deadly impact event. The rare nature of this projectile highlights the dinosaurs' extreme misfortune. This impact created the Chicxulub crater and led to a mass extinction.

stories.title: Tiny plastics in drinking water may help harmful bacteria resist disinfectants
stories.summary: New research reveals nanoplastics can strengthen harmful bacterial biofilms in water systems. These tiny plastic particles help microbes survive disinfection treatments more effectively. This makes maintaining clean drinking water infrastructure significantly more challenging. The presence of nanoplastics may contribute to the rise of antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Understanding these interactions is crucial for public health and water management efforts.

stories.title: Astronomers just spotted erythrulose, the tastiest sugar found in some berries here on Earth, and why this discovery could change how we search for life in space
Earth has regulated its climate for 60 million years through a hidden ocean feedback
stories.summary: A new study has identified a natural process that may have helped keep Earth's climate stable for the past 60 million years. Researchers found that changes in sea level controlled the amount of phosphate reaching the oceans, affecting marine life, carbon burial beneath the seafloor and the level of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere. The findings offer a new explanation for how Earth naturally regulated long-term warming and cooling.

stories.title: Mount Olympus, the mythological home of Zeus and the ancient Greek gods, is being considered for UNESCO World Heritage status as Greece seeks protection for its tallest mountain
stories.summary: Mount Olympus, a site of myth and nature, seeks UNESCO World Heritage recognition. This ancient Greek mountain is home to gods and diverse ecosystems. Locals hope for global acknowledgment to ensure its continued protection. The nomination process involves careful review and potential further requirements. Recognition would bring responsibilities for preserving its unique cultural and natural values.

stories.title: Scientists played human voices near Alaska salmon streams and found that bears and eagles fled
stories.summary: New findings from Canadian researchers reveal that human sounds near Alaska's salmon streams significantly disturb wildlife, leading to grizzly bears avoiding feeding areas. This interference disrupts the natural nutrient transfer to surrounding forests, emphasizing the detrimental effects of human activity on essential ecosystem dynamics. Scientists propose enhanced land management practices to safeguard these critical ecological processes.

stories.title: In 1948, Idaho dropped 76 beavers by parachute into remote wilderness, and they soon began building dams
How 58 beavers revived a valley buried by Mount St. Helens eruption
stories.summary: More than 40 years after the Mount St. Helens eruption buried a Washington river valley under volcanic sediment, 58 relocated beavers have helped restore the damaged landscape. Their dams and wetlands brought back native plants, fish and wildlife. However, conservationists fear a planned government project to raise a sediment retention structure could undo years of natural restoration.

stories.title: Bumblebees survive pesticide exposure, but reproductive genes begin changing
